author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: 510(k) Submission K162447 - ApexHip Total Hip System
gist: Formal cover letter submitting the 510(k) for ApexHip, identifying ClassicHip as predicate device, summarizing substantial equivalence based on materials (Co/Cr femoral head/stem, Co/Cr acetabular cup with KinetiCoat porous titanium coating) and intended use for active adults 45-65. References wear testing per ISO 14242 protocol approved at DR-3. Requests expedited review given prior clearance history with predicate devices.

author: Dr. P. Anand
subject: RE: 510(k) Submission K162447 - Additional Information Request
gist: FDA Additional Information request letter asking Veridian to clarify wear testing methodology, specifically whether cup inclination angles beyond the standard 45 degree protocol were evaluated, and to provide further biocompatibility data on the KinetiCoat coating layer. Cites 21 CFR 807.87 requirements. Sets 180-day response clock.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA AI request on K162447 - need wear test response
gist: Dana forwards the FDA AI letter to Tom and Priya, top message asks Tom to confirm the DR-3 wear-test protocol used only standard 45-degree inclination testing per ISO 14242 and to draft language explaining why that scope was deemed adequate for the design inputs approved in 2015. Notes the 180-day clock and asks for a draft response within three weeks.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: RE: FDA AI request on K162447 - need wear test response
gist: tom replies confirming the protocol was 45 degrees only per DR-3 committee decision in nov 2016, says testing at higher inclination angles was discussed but not pursued because standard predicate comparisons didn't require it. mentions he can pull the meridian labs test report numbers for the response draft. tone is matter-of-fact but slightly defensive about scope.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Response to Additional Information Request - K162447
gist: Formal response letter to FDA's AI request, explaining that ApexHip wear testing followed ISO 14242 at the standard 45 degree cup inclination angle consistent with the ClassicHip predicate comparison, citing Meridian Testing Labs report numbers and stating this scope is adequate to demonstrate substantial equivalence. Includes summary wear-rate data tables comparing ApexHip to predicate.

author: Dr. P. Anand
subject: 510(k) Clearance Letter - K162447 ApexHip Total Hip System
gist: FDA clearance letter granting 510(k) clearance for ApexHip under K162447, confirming substantial equivalence to ClassicHip predicate, listing cleared indications for total hip replacement in active adults. Standard boilerplate about general controls and post-market obligations including MDR reporting requirements under 21 CFR 803.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: ApexHip cleared - K162447
gist: Dana announces FDA clearance of ApexHip via K162447, notes clearance came through without further delay after the AI response, and reminds the team of ongoing MDR reporting obligations now that the device is cleared for commercial launch. Short, celebratory but formal tone.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: ApexHip Launch Readiness - Regulatory Sign-off
gist: Calendar invite for a launch readiness meeting to confirm regulatory documentation and complaint-handling procedures are in place ahead of US commercial launch on April 17, 2017. No substantive content, purely scheduling.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Atlanta cluster - MDR reportability question
gist: Priya raises the first cluster of metal-ion complaints from Dr. Feld's Atlanta practice, three patients logged in TrackWise, asking Dana whether these meet MDR reportability thresholds under 21 CFR 803.50 given they appear to be early-stage elevated cobalt levels rather than confirmed device malfunction. Notes TrackWise entries but doesn't cite specific TW numbers yet.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Atlanta cluster - MDR reportability question
gist: Dana responds citing 21 CFR 803.50(a) criteria, asks Devon to run the reportability analysis and prepare draft MDR filings if warranted, states preliminary view that elevated ion levels alone without confirmed malfunction or serious injury may not trigger mandatory reporting but wants documentation of the analysis for the file. Numbered list of next steps.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Atlanta cluster - MDR reportability question
gist: Devon reports back that after reviewing the three Atlanta cases he recommends filing MDRs for two of the three patients given documented elevated Co/Cr ion levels and physician-noted tissue reaction, drafts are attached for review, third case deferred pending more clinical data. Includes filing deadline calculations.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR Filing - TrackWise TW-2018-0231 Atlanta Patient A
gist: Completed MDR intake form documenting a patient complaint from Dr. Feld's Atlanta practice: elevated cobalt/chromium serum levels detected post-ApexHip implantation, symptoms consistent with early ARMD per treating physician notes. Includes device lot numbers, implant date, complaint narrative, and event code classification for FDA submission.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR Filing - TrackWise TW-2018-0232 Atlanta Patient B
gist: Second MDR intake form for the Atlanta cluster, similar structure documenting elevated metal ion levels and physician suspicion of adverse reaction to metal debris in a second patient implanted with ApexHip, notes revision surgery being considered. Lot numbers and implant dates included consistent with the cluster.

author: Dr. P. Anand
subject: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis
gist: FDA sends an Additional Information request asking Veridian to provide a trending analysis of MDR filings related to ApexHip over the prior 18 months, specifically inquiring whether the volume and nature of metal-ion related complaints suggest a broader post-market surveillance issue requiring further evaluation. References the Atlanta cluster reports filed in 2018.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FW: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis
gist: Dana forwards the FDA request, top message directs Priya to compile complaint trending data from TrackWise for the past 18 months across all ApexHip complaint categories, not just the Atlanta cluster, and asks Devon to draft the narrative response emphasizing the company's ongoing post-market surveillance program.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: FW: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis
gist: priya sends trending numbers - 14 metal-ion related complaints logged in TrackWise since launch, concentrated in Atlanta and Nashville, complaint rate still below the threshold that would normally trigger a formal CAPA per her read of the SOP, but she flags that the rate has been increasing quarter over quarter. attaches spreadsheet Apex_complaint_trend_2019.xlsx. tone is careful, almost defensive about the numbers.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis
gist: Devon's formal response letter to FDA summarizing the complaint trending analysis, stating 14 metal-ion related complaints have been logged since launch, that the company's PMS program continues to monitor the trend, and that no design change has been deemed necessary at this time based on available clinical data. Signed by Dana Okonkwo as VP Regulatory Affairs.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA response sent
gist: brief teams chat between dana and priya confirming the MDR trending response letter was sent to fda on june 3rd, priya asks if she should update the internal tracker, dana says yes and to loop in devon. no new substantive facts beyond confirming the filing.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: wear test re-run results - concerning
gist: tom emails priya and carlos about his re-run of wear testing at higher cup inclination angles (55 degrees), finding 4-6x wear rates compared to standard 45 degree testing, attaches Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx. says this could explain some of the atlanta and nashville complaints since edge loading at high inclination would elevate metal ion release. asks whether this should go to regulatory given the ongoing FDA trending inquiry.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: wear test re-run results - concerning
gist: Priya loops in Dana on Tom's wear test findings, notes this data wasn't part of the original design verification and asks whether it needs to be reported to FDA given the recently closed AI request on trending, or whether it's more of a design engineering matter to track internally first. Cautious, procedural tone.
gray_rationale: This references design/wear-test data (RFP 2) and touches on whether FDA disclosure is needed (RFP 4), but does not mention the coating/manufacturing recall issue, so a reviewer might exclude it from RFP 1 despite the word 'wear'.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: wear test re-run results - concerning
gist: Dana responds that the 55-degree wear data alone likely does not trigger an immediate MDR filing obligation since no specific adverse event is directly tied to the finding yet, but instructs Tom to formalize the analysis as a memo for the design history file and instructs Priya to continue monitoring complaint trends closely for any correlation to inclination angle at implant.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: ApexHip Wear Test Re-Analysis Memo - Design History File
gist: Formal memo documenting the February 2019 wear-test re-run at 55 degree cup inclination, presenting the 4-6x wear rate increase versus standard 45 degree testing, discussing edge-loading mechanics as the likely cause, and proposing an evaluation of design change ECO-2019-118 to modify cup geometry or head diameter recommendations to reduce edge-loading risk at high inclination angles. Concludes that further clinical correlation study is warranted before committing to a design change; addressed to Priya Raman and Carlos Mendes for the DHF.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: ApexHip Wear Test Re-Analysis Memo - Design History File
gist: Carlos acknowledges receiving Tom's wear test memo, raises concerns about how a design change proposal (ECO-2019-118) would be messaged to the sales force and KOLs if surgeons ask about it, but does not object to the technical findings. Asks whether marketing materials need review in parallel.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: KneeFlex launch - regulatory checklist final
gist: Devon confirms the regulatory checklist for the KneeFlex launch is complete, all FDA clearance documentation filed and ready for the October launch, no mention of ApexHip anywhere in the email. Routine administrative confirmation.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Q4 complaint trend update - ApexHip metal ion category
gist: Priya provides a quarterly update noting the metal-ion complaint category for ApexHip has grown to 22 total complaints since launch, mentions the ECO-2019-118 design change discussion from September has stalled without a decision, and asks whether regulatory wants to revisit reportability given the growing count. Ends by noting next FDA touchpoint isn't until the 2021 inspection cycle unless something changes.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Q4 complaint trend
gist: quick chat exchange, dana tells priya she'll review the trend memo next week and to keep the tracker current, no substantive decision made yet, mostly scheduling a follow-up call for later in november.
gray_rationale: References the complaint trend memo in passing without adding new substantive complaint information, so a reviewer could argue it merely schedules a follow-up rather than being responsive itself.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Annual Report Supplement - K162447 ApexHip
gist: Routine annual regulatory status letter to FDA noting no design changes have been implemented since clearance, referencing that a design change evaluation (ECO-2019-118) was considered internally in 2019 but not adopted, and confirming ongoing post-market complaint monitoring continues per procedure. Brief, administrative in tone.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Q1 sales kickoff - Dallas venue confirmed
gist: Marcus confirms venue and catering for the Q1 ApexHip sales kickoff event in Dallas, no discussion of complaints, wear data, or FDA correspondence, purely logistics for the sales event.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Reminder - 2019 MDR trending response still active with FDA
gist: Devon reminds Dana and Priya that FDA's file on the 2019 trending AI response remains open and that if the metal-ion complaint count crosses 25 total, per his internal tracking they should proactively consider a supplemental filing rather than wait for FDA to ask again. Notes current count sits at 24 as of March per the latest TrackWise export.

author: FDA CDRH / ODE, Office of Compliance
subject: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis for ApexHip System K162447
gist: Formal FDA Additional Information request letter signed by Lead Reviewer Dr. P. Anand asking Veridian to explain an apparent upward trend in metal-ion related MDRs for ApexHip filed since Q3 2018, requesting a root-cause narrative, complaint rate calculations by lot, and a corrective action timeline within 30 days. References specific MDR numbers and cites 21 CFR 803. This is the top-level content of the letter, straightforward FDA correspondence.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FW: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis for ApexHip System K162447
gist: Dana forwards the FDA AI request to Devon and Priya, numbering the required response elements per 21 CFR 803 and asking Priya to pull complaint trend data by TrackWise ID and Devon to draft the narrative. Notes the 30-day clock started May 8. Tone is precise and formal, top message is the substantive assignment.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis for ApexHip System K162447
gist: Priya replies with a summary of the complaint trend data: 41 metal-ion-related complaints logged since Aug 2018 across TrackWise IDs starting TW-2019-0410 through TW-2019-0451, concentrated among Dr. Feld's Atlanta patients and several Nashville cases tied to Dr. Rao. She flags that complaint rate per 1,000 implants is trending upward quarter over quarter and that Halvorsen's 2019-02 wear-test re-analysis at 55 degrees inclination may be relevant context for the root cause narrative. This is the key data underlying the FDA response.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Additional Information Request - MDR Trending Analysis for ApexHip System K162447
gist: Devon sends Dana a draft narrative for the FDA response, attaching ApexHip_AI_Response_Draft_v2.docx, explaining the complaint trend as consistent with expected variability at higher implant volumes and proposing enhanced surgeon education on cup positioning rather than a design change, while noting Halvorsen's wear data is being evaluated separately by engineering. Asks Dana to review tone before it goes to legal.

author: Dana Okonkwo
recipients: FDA CDRH / ODE, Office of Compliance
subject: Response to Additional Information Request - ApexHip K162447 MDR Trending
gist: Formal outgoing letter to FDA (attn Dr. P. Anand) responding to the May 8 AI request. States that the complaint rate increase reflects growing implant volume rather than a device defect, references complaint rate of 0.29% versus prior year 0.24%, describes ongoing engineering evaluation of wear characteristics, and commits to a follow-up report in Q4 2019 if trends continue. Signed by Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Q4 2019 follow-up report to FDA due in 3 weeks
gist: Devon reminds the team of the committed Q4 2019 follow-up report to FDA on MDR trending, asks Priya for updated complaint counts through October and Dana whether Halvorsen's wear-test findings should be summarized in the report. Notes the complaint count has risen to 58 metal-ion related TrackWise entries since the original filing.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Q4 2019 follow-up report to FDA due in 3 weeks
gist: Priya provides updated numbers per procedure: complaint rate now 0.34%, still within the pre-established alert threshold of 0.5% per her complaint handling procedure, so no CAPA has been formally opened. She adds that engineering (Halvorsen) has proposed a design change (later designated ECO-2019-118) but it has not been approved, and suggests the follow-up report describe it as 'under evaluation' rather than committed. This framing decision sits at the end of her message.

author: Dana Okonkwo
recipients: FDA CDRH / ODE, Office of Compliance
subject: Q4 2019 Follow-Up Report - ApexHip MDR Trending per 2019-05-08 Correspondence
gist: Formal follow-up letter to FDA per the committed timeline, reporting complaint rate now at 0.34%, describing an ongoing engineering evaluation of wear characteristics at higher cup inclination angles without naming a specific corrective action, and stating the company will continue to monitor and report significant changes. No mention of specific test results or the magnitude of wear increase found internally.
gray_rationale: The letter references an engineering wear evaluation tied to the original 45-degree-only test protocol design decision, which a reviewer might connect to design history rather than treating purely as FDA correspondence.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Teams: FDA follow-up filed
gist: Short Teams exchange confirming the Q4 2019 follow-up letter was filed and acknowledged by FDA with no further immediate action requested, Dana notes they should keep tracking complaint trend quarterly, Devon agrees to set a calendar reminder.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: FDA Warsaw Facility Inspection - Prep Meeting
gist: Calendar invite for a prep meeting ahead of an announced FDA inspection of the Warsaw facility scheduled for mid-June, agenda line mentions reviewing complaint handling procedures and design history file organization. No substantive findings discussed, purely scheduling.
gray_rationale: Mentions complaint handling and DHF review topics in the agenda line but contains no substantive content, so a strict reviewer would treat it as non-responsive scheduling.

author: FDA CDRH / ODE, Office of Compliance
subject: FDA Form 483 - Inspectional Observations, Warsaw Facility
gist: Form 483 issued by Investigator R. Delgado following the June 2021 inspection, listing three observations: (1) complaint investigations for metal-ion related events were not completed within the timeframe specified in the firm's own procedure, citing specific TrackWise IDs including TW-2019-0417 and several 2020 entries with investigation delays of 60-90 days; (2) minor labeling documentation gap; (3) training record deficiency for two complaint handling staff. Observation 1 is the substantive finding, presented plainly at the top of the form.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Form 483 - need response plan within 15 business days
gist: Dana circulates the Form 483 and asks Priya to draft corrective actions for the complaint-trending timeliness observation, cc's Rachel Steinberg for visibility given anticipated sensitivity, and sets an internal deadline of July 9 for a full draft. States FDA expects a written response within 15 business days of issuance.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Form 483 - need response plan within 15 business days
gist: Priya responds with a proposed corrective action: reassigning two complaint handlers, adding a weekly aging report reviewed by her directly, and revising the SOP timeliness target from 30 to 21 days for initial triage. She acknowledges some of the delayed investigations, including TW-2019-0417, involved cases later tied to the metal-ion cluster and says those files are being re-reviewed for completeness.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Form 483 - need response plan within 15 business days
gist: Devon compiles the draft 483 response letter combining Priya's corrective actions and Dana's regulatory framing, attaching Apex_483_Response_Draft.docx, and flags that observation 2 (labeling) and observation 3 (training records) need input from Lisa Tran in HR for training documentation.

author: Dana Okonkwo
recipients: FDA CDRH / ODE, Office of Compliance
subject: Response to Form 483 Observations - Warsaw Facility Inspection dated 2021-06-25
gist: Formal Form 483 response letter to FDA, addressing all three observations with corrective action commitments: revised complaint SOP with 21-day triage target, additional staffing, weekly aging reports reviewed by Priya Raman, updated labeling documentation procedures, and refreshed training records for the two identified staff. Notes completion target of September 30, 2021 for all corrective actions.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Teams: 483 response filed
gist: Brief Teams message confirming the Form 483 response was sent and Priya has scheduled the weekly aging report reviews to start Monday. Dana thanks her and asks to be looped in if any complaint investigation exceeds 21 days going forward.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Weekly aging report - week of 8/16
gist: Routine weekly complaint aging report email, table listing open TrackWise investigations and days outstanding, all currently within the new 21-day target, no metal-ion cases flagged this week. Mostly administrative status update, a hard negative in tone though it touches complaint handling in a purely procedural, non-substantive way this particular week.
gray_rationale: It is a routine complaint aging status report with no cases of substance flagged, so while it touches complaint handling process it lacks investigative content a reviewer would consider responsive.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Dear Doctor letter - need FDA notification confirmation
gist: Dana asks Devon to confirm whether the surgeon 'Dear Doctor' letter being drafted following the Registry Signal Review meeting needs to be filed with or copied to FDA, noting the labeling update accompanying it may trigger a special 510(k) or at minimum a courtesy notification. References the September 14 Registry Signal Review decision to continue selling with a label update.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Dear Doctor letter - need FDA notification confirmation
gist: Devon researches and responds that the labeling update (adding language on cup inclination sensitivity and recommended surgical technique) likely does not require a new 510(k) since it does not change intended use, but recommends a courtesy notification letter to the reviewing branch describing the update and referencing the NJR data that prompted it, to preempt questions during any future inspection.

author: Dana Okonkwo
recipients: FDA CDRH / ODE, Office of Compliance
subject: Courtesy Notification - ApexHip Labeling Update Regarding Surgical Technique and Cup Positioning
gist: Courtesy letter to FDA notifying them of a voluntary labeling update to the ApexHip Instructions for Use, adding guidance on cup inclination angle and surgical technique, referencing the March 2021 NJR annual report finding a 7.1% five-year revision rate versus 3.2% class average as the basis for the update, and stating the company does not believe the change requires a new 510(k) submission. Also references the accompanying Dear Doctor letter being sent to surgeons in October 2021.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA courtesy letter sent - archive copy
gist: Short email confirming the courtesy notification letter was sent to FDA and asking Devon to archive a copy alongside the Dear Doctor letter and Registry Signal Review minutes for the regulatory file. No new substantive content beyond the filing confirmation.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Ethics hotline report - possible overlap with FDA correspondence file
gist: Devon flags to Dana that an anonymous ethics hotline report alleging complaint trend suppression in Quality has come in, and asks whether any of the prior FDA correspondence (the 2019 AI response, the Q4 2019 follow-up, or the Form 483 response) needs to be reviewed again in light of the allegation, out of caution. Dana's reply is not included in this message; this is Devon raising the issue.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Ethics hotline report - possible overlap with FDA correspondence file
gist: Dana responds cautiously, cc'ing Rachel Steinberg, saying the prior FDA filings were accurate as of the dates submitted based on the data available at the time, but agrees a review of complaint trending documentation referenced in those filings would be prudent, and asks Devon to compile the file for legal's review. This message sits at the bottom of a growing thread and contains the key substantive admission about reviewing past filings.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Teams: complaint file compilation for legal
gist: Priya confirms she has compiled the complaint trending files referenced in the 2019 and 2021 FDA correspondence for Rachel Steinberg's review, listing TrackWise ID ranges TW-2019-0410 through TW-2021-0512, and mentions it took most of the week to assemble given the volume.

author: Elena Ruiz
subject: Litigation hold scope - FDA correspondence file
gist: Outside counsel Elena Ruiz at Whitfield & Barr writes confirming the scope of the anticipated litigation hold effective February 1, 2022, and specifically lists the 2019 AI request and response, the Q4 2019 follow-up letter, the June 2021 Form 483 and response, and the October 2021 courtesy notification letter as documents that must be preserved and are likely relevant to anticipated claims.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Reserve conference room - Q1 regulatory file review
gist: Simple calendar invite reserving a conference room for a quarterly regulatory file review meeting, no agenda details included, purely logistical with no substantive content about any FDA matter.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Regulatory file review notes - FDA correspondence chronology
gist: Dana asks Devon to prepare a clean chronology memo of all ApexHip FDA correspondence from the 2017 510(k) clearance through the October 2021 courtesy notification, for internal reference ahead of anticipated litigation, noting it should include dates, letter types, and a one-line summary of each filing's substance.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: ApexHip FDA Correspondence Chronology, 2017-2021
gist: Internal chronology memo listing every FDA interaction on ApexHip: the March 2017 510(k) clearance K162447, the May 2019 AI request and June 2019 response on MDR trending, the December 2019 Q4 follow-up report, the June 2021 Form 483 with three observations and July 2021 response, and the October 2021 courtesy notification tied to the labeling update. Each entry includes a one-line substance summary; the memo notes complaint rates cited grew from 0.24% to 0.34% over the period covered by the correspondence.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: RE: ApexHip FDA Correspondence Chronology, 2017-2021 - please do not forward
gist: Rachel Steinberg thanks Devon for the chronology memo, adds a privileged and confidential banner, and asks that no further copies be distributed outside the litigation working group, but does not dispute the accuracy of any dates or figures in the memo. Contains no new substantive facts beyond acknowledging receipt.
gray_rationale: The message is largely a privilege/distribution instruction rather than substantive FDA correspondence content, though it directly discusses and forwards the correspondence chronology memo.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Teams: KneeFlex AI request - unrelated to Apex
gist: Devon mentions a new, unrelated FDA Additional Information request that came in regarding a KneeFlex 510(k) supplement, asking Dana if she wants to be looped in even though it is a different product line. Dana says no need, that's a knee-team matter, keep it separate from the Apex file.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Preparation for FDA inspection at Warsaw - complaint files
gist: Raman circulates a memo listing the complaint files and TrackWise records to have ready for the upcoming FDA inspection of the Warsaw facility, including ApexHip TW-2018-0301 through TW-2019-0417 series and MDR tracking logs. Notes that complaint trending timeliness has been a soft spot internally and asks Mitchell to reconcile the 30-day MDR clock on three late-filed reports. Mentions investigator will likely be R. Delgado based on prior visits. Tone is careful, procedure-oriented, some anxiety about scrutiny.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Preparation for FDA inspection at Warsaw - complaint files
gist: Mitchell replies confirming he pulled the late MDR files and found the delays traced to a data-entry backlog in Quality, not a substantive underreporting issue. Lists three complaint IDs with actual filing dates versus due dates. Says he will bring binder copies to the inspection room Monday.

author: R. Delgado
subject: Form 483 - Inspectional Observations, Veridian Orthopedics Warsaw Facility
gist: FDA Form 483 letter listing three inspectional observations from the June 2021 inspection: (1) complaint investigation records did not consistently document timeliness against the 30-day MDR reporting requirement under 21 CFR 803, (2) CAPA effectiveness checks for a 2019 coating issue lacked follow-up data, (3) minor labeling document control gap. Formal, numbered, government letter tone. This is the core FDA correspondence document establishing the inspection findings.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FW: Form 483 - Inspectional Observations
gist: Okonkwo forwards the Form 483 internally, flagging the 30-day deadline to respond and asking Raman to draft the complaint-trending corrective action section while Mitchell handles labeling controls. Notes Steinberg should review before submission. Top message is short and directive; the full 483 text is quoted below.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: FW: Form 483 - Inspectional Observations
gist: Raman responds with a draft outline of corrective actions for observation 1 (complaint trending timeliness): retraining complaint intake staff, adding a TrackWise automated aging alert at 20 days, and a quarterly audit of MDR decision trees. She notes the underlying volume of ApexHip metal-ion complaints from 2018-2019 contributed to the backlog reviewers cited.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Response to Form 483 Observations dated June 25, 2021
gist: Formal FDA response letter addressing each of the three 483 observations with committed corrective actions and target completion dates: retraining by August 2021, TrackWise aging alert live by September 2021, and a retrospective audit of 2018-2020 ApexHip complaint files for MDR reportability. States corrective actions do not indicate a product defect, only administrative timeliness gaps. Signed by Okonkwo citing 21 CFR 820 and 803 references.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Retrospective audit results - ApexHip complaint files 2018-2020
gist: Mitchell reports results of the retrospective audit committed in the 483 response, identifying two additional ApexHip complaints (Atlanta cluster, Dr. Feld's practice) that arguably should have been filed as MDRs sooner but were ultimately not required to be reportable under the decision tree criteria. Recommends documenting the rationale clearly in TrackWise to close the loop with FDA.
gray_rationale: The complaints are discussed mainly in the context of MDR reportability process rather than substantively describing the complaint facts themselves, so a reviewer might code it primarily to FDA correspondence rather than the complaint-handling RFP.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Internal review - 483 response closure documentation
gist: Simple calendar invite scheduling a 30-minute meeting to finalize the closure package sent to FDA. No substantive content beyond time, location (Hub conference room Reserve B), and attendee list.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: MDR filing - Atlanta explant, patient AJ-4471
gist: Okonkwo directs Mitchell to prepare and file an MDR for a recent ApexHip revision surgery in Atlanta involving elevated cobalt levels and tissue necrosis, citing the 30-day clock starting from the date Quality became aware. References the ongoing registry signal discussion as context for heightened attention to timely filing. States this MDR should reference lot H-3092 head and S-7145 stem.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR Report Form - Patient AJ-4471, ApexHip revision
gist: Completed MDR form documenting the adverse event: patient underwent revision surgery for ARMD with elevated serum cobalt/chromium, explanted ApexHip components lot H-3092/S-7145, event date, device history, and event description referencing metal debris and tissue necrosis findings. Standard FDA MDR form fields filled in with clinical narrative section describing pseudotumor finding.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Dear Doctor letter - regulatory review before mailing
gist: Okonkwo asks Mitchell and Raman to review the draft Dear Doctor letter (following the Registry Signal Review decision) for regulatory accuracy before it is mailed to surgeons, specifically checking that the revision-rate language matches the NJR data and does not overstate or understate risk. Notes FDA does not require pre-clearance of the letter but wants internal sign-off documented.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Dear Doctor letter - regulatory review before mailing
gist: Raman confirms the 7.1% versus 3.2% revision-rate figures are correctly sourced from the March 2021 NJR report and suggests softening the phrase 'no design defect identified' to 'no design defect has been confirmed' for accuracy. Approves for mailing pending that edit.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Important Product Information - ApexHip Total Hip System
gist: The finalized Dear Doctor letter sent to surgeons, describing updated labeling information regarding revision rates observed in registry data, recommending enhanced patient monitoring for elevated metal ion levels, and noting the product remains on the market with an updated instructions-for-use. References the March 2021 NJR figures. This letter is central FDA-adjacent regulatory correspondence tied to labeling.

author: Anita Rao
subject: Question re: Dear Doctor letter monitoring recommendation
gist: Dr. Rao writes asking for clarification on what serum metal ion testing interval Veridian recommends post-letter, noting some of her patients are asking. She references having seen two of her own early revision cases recently. Okonkwo's short reply (quoted below in a later thread) is not included here; this stands alone as incoming correspondence.
gray_rationale: Rao mentions revision cases in passing while primarily asking a labeling/monitoring question, so it sits at the boundary between FDA labeling correspondence and complaint signal content.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR quarterly summary - Q3 2021 ApexHip filings
gist: Mitchell sends a summary of Q3 2021 MDR filings for ApexHip: 6 filed, all related to revision surgeries citing elevated metal ion levels or ARMD, none late per the new TrackWise aging alert implemented after the 483 response. Notes the count is up from 2 in Q3 2020, consistent with the registry signal trend Novak has been tracking.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: Anonymous ethics hotline report - complaint trending
gist: Tran forwards notice of an anonymous ethics hotline report alleging that complaint trending data for ApexHip was suppressed or delayed to avoid regulatory attention, and asks Raman and Okonkwo to preserve relevant records pending an HR/Quality investigation. States outside counsel may need to be looped in given potential regulatory implications.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Anonymous ethics hotline report - complaint trending
gist: Okonkwo responds that Regulatory will independently review the MDR trending logs referenced in the hotline complaint to confirm filing timeliness matches the 483 response commitments, and offers to share the Q3 2021 summary already sent to FDA as a baseline. Tone is measured, slightly defensive.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR clock question
gist: Short Teams chat where Mitchell asks Raman whether a new complaint from Denver (Dr. Whitaker's patient, suspected pseudotumor) starts the MDR clock from the complaint intake date or the date imaging confirmed the finding. Raman answers per procedure it's the date Veridian becomes aware of information reasonably suggesting reportability, so intake date, and to file by mid-December.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR Report Form - Patient JW-1102, ApexHip revision (Denver)
gist: Completed MDR form for Dr. Whitaker's Denver patient JW-1102, describing revision surgery finding of pseudotumor and elevated cobalt levels, explanted components lot H-3105/V-2087 (cup lot outside the later recall range), device history, and narrative referencing metal-on-metal wear as suspected cause.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Litigation hold considerations tied to MDR trending records
gist: Okonkwo emails counsel noting that with claims anticipated, the MDR filing history and 483 correspondence records for ApexHip should be part of the litigation hold scope, and asks whether Whitfield & Barr wants copies of the 2021 483 response and Dear Doctor letter for reference. Steinberg's short reply below confirms and says a hold notice is being drafted separately.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Draft response to FDA information request on MDR backlog closure
gist: Mitchell circulates a draft cover letter to FDA closing out the loop on the 2021 483 corrective actions, summarizing that the TrackWise aging alert has been operational for four months with zero late MDR filings since implementation, and that the retrospective audit found no unreported reportable events requiring late filing. Asks Okonkwo to review tone before sending.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Closure of Form 483 corrective actions - Warsaw facility
gist: Formal closure letter to FDA confirming completion of all three corrective actions from the June 2021 Form 483: retraining completed, TrackWise aging alert live since September 2021 with documented performance, and CAPA effectiveness check process updated for coating-related issues. States Veridian considers all observations closed and welcomes further FDA review.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: KneeFlex labeling question for upcoming submission
gist: Mendes asks Okonkwo a routine question about whether a minor KneeFlex labeling change requires a new 510(k) submission or can go through the letter-to-file process, referencing KneeFlex-specific design history only. No mention of ApexHip.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA follow-up call recap - ApexHip MDR trend inquiry
gist: Okonkwo recaps a phone call with the FDA reviewer (referencing the 483 closure) who asked informally whether the MDR trend for ApexHip metal-ion related revisions had continued to rise into Q4 2021 and Q1 2022, given the closure letter. Okonkwo notes she gave a general answer that trending continues to be monitored and offered to provide updated data if formally requested, and flags internally that a formal information request may follow.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Prep call - possible FDA formal information request
gist: Calendar invite for a prep call ahead of a possible formal FDA information request, no agenda details beyond the title and a note 'bring Q4 2021/Q1 2022 MDR numbers.' Mostly scheduling but the single line referencing the MDR numbers ties it to the ongoing regulatory matter.
gray_rationale: The invite is largely scheduling logistics with only a brief substantive reference to gathering MDR data for the anticipated FDA request, so reviewers could differ on whether it counts as FDA correspondence.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: FDA formal request received - ApexHip MDR trending update
gist: Mitchell forwards a formal FDA additional information request asking Veridian to provide updated MDR trending data for ApexHip covering 2019 through Q1 2022 and to explain any correlation with the registry signal findings referenced publicly. This is the top-level substantive content establishing a new formal FDA correspondence obligation.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: FDA formal request received - ApexHip MDR trending update
gist: Okonkwo asks Novak to pull the underlying registry data referenced by FDA and asks Raman to compile the full MDR trend table since 2019 for the response, setting a target response deadline consistent with the regulatory clock. Notes response will need Steinberg's review given litigation sensitivity.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA Warsaw Inspection - Prep Agenda
gist: Agenda for internal prep ahead of an announced FDA general GMP inspection at the Warsaw facility beginning June 14, 2021. Lists topics: complaint file review readiness, CAPA log status, design history file access for ApexHip, and document room logistics. Mentions inspector will likely review MDR trending given prior 2019 AI request. No findings yet, purely preparatory.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: FDA Warsaw Inspection - Prep Agenda - Notes from Prep Meeting
gist: Minutes of the prep meeting confirming roles: Okonkwo as front room lead, Raman handling complaint file questions, Mitchell as scribe. Notes that the complaint trending SOP was last revised in 2020 and that the team should be ready to explain the 2019 gap in MDR timeliness identified in the earlier FDA AI request response. Assigns Kowalski to have Cork batch records available electronically.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Response to Form FDA 483, Warsaw, Indiana Facility
gist: Formal letter responding to a Form 483 issued after the June 2021 inspection, addressing three observations. Observation 2 concerns timeliness of complaint trending analysis for ApexHip; Veridian commits to revising SOP-QA-114 to require monthly (not quarterly) trend review and to retraining complaint handling staff by September 2021. References specific TrackWise complaint counts reviewed during inspection. Signed by Dana, cites 21 CFR 820.198 and 820.100.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: 483 Response - CAPA Assignment
gist: Raman confirms she will open a CAPA (CAPA-2021-047) to track the SOP-QA-114 revision commitment made in the 483 response letter. She notes the retraining will cover all complaint intake staff and asks Mitchell to log the CAPA due date of September 30, 2021 in the tracker. Brief, procedural, top of thread is the substantive commitment.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR Filing - TW-2021-0655 (Denver, Dr. Whitaker patient)
gist: Mitchell drafts an MDR submission summary for a complaint from Dr. Whitaker's Denver patient reporting elevated cobalt levels and early revision surgery at 3.5 years post-implant. States the MDR will be filed within the 30-day requirement and references similar prior complaints trending upward per the Q2 2021 report. Asks Okonkwo to review before submission to FDA's MedWatch/eMDR system.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: MDR Filing - TW-2021-0655 (Denver, Dr. Whitaker patient)
gist: Okonkwo approves the MDR language with minor edits, instructing Mitchell to soften causation language to 'reported elevated ion levels' rather than 'confirmed metal toxicity' pending explant analysis. Confirms filing deadline and asks for confirmation number once submitted.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: MDR Filing - TW-2021-0655 (Denver, Dr. Whitaker patient) - Filed
gist: Mitchell confirms MDR was electronically submitted to FDA with confirmation number eMDR-2021-88213, within the 30-day window. Notes this is the fourth ApexHip MDR filed in 2021 related to metal ion/revision complaints, consistent with the trend discussed at the Registry Signal Review meeting in September.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Notification of Labeling Update - ApexHip Total Hip System
gist: Letter to FDA notifying of a voluntary labeling update for ApexHip adding language on monitoring recommendations for patients with high cup inclination angles, following the September 2021 Registry Signal Review decision. States the change does not require a new 510(k) as it is a labeling clarification, not a design change. References the March 2021 NJR data (7.1% five-year revision rate) as the basis for the update.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Notification of Labeling Update - ApexHip Total Hip System
gist: Mitchell forwards the surgeon 'Dear Doctor' letter for final regulatory review before mailing, noting FDA has not objected to the labeling notification filed October 5. Mendes is copied to coordinate distribution timing with the sales team. No new substantive facts beyond the labeling notification already filed.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Notification to FDA - Draft for Review
gist: Okonkwo circulates the draft recall notification letter to FDA for cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, citing the KinetiCoat adhesion failures discovered at Northgate Health System and a Denver hospital. States 1,140 units distributed, 412 implanted, root cause traced to plasma-spray parameter drift after a chamber maintenance event at Cork. Asks Kowalski to confirm final unit counts before filing tomorrow.
gray_rationale: This document is primarily about recall filing mechanics but the underlying event is the coating recall itself, so some reviewers might also code it to the recall-execution topic rather than purely FDA correspondence.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Voluntary Recall Notification - ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200 to V-2299
gist: Final letter formally notifying FDA of the voluntary Class II recall, assigned recall number Z-1418-2022. Details the affected lot range, manufacturing dates (Nov 2021-Feb 2022, Cork), root cause (plasma-spray parameter drift), and corrective actions including chamber requalification. States customer notification letters are being sent concurrently.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Recall Notification to FDA - Draft for Review - FDA Ack Received
gist: Mitchell confirms FDA acknowledged receipt of the recall notification and assigned recall number Z-1418-2022, matching the letter. Notes FDA requested a copy of the effectiveness check plan within 30 days, which Raman's team is preparing separately.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Draft MDR Trend Summary for FDA Follow-Up
gist: Raman shares a draft complaint trend summary requested informally by FDA following the recall, covering both the coating adhesion complaints (recall-related) and the separate, ongoing metal-ion/revision complaint trend for ApexHip. She flags that combining the two trend lines in one chart could be confusing to a reviewer and asks whether they should be presented separately.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Draft MDR Trend Summary for FDA Follow-Up
gist: Okonkwo agrees the two trend categories (coating adhesion vs. metal-ion/ARMD) should be presented as separate charts to avoid conflating the recall issue with the unrelated wear/ion issue, since they have different root causes. Instructs Raman to finalize by end of week for submission to FDA.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR Filing - TW-2022-0891 (Feld patient, revision at 4 yrs)
gist: Mitchell reports a new MDR being prepared for a complaint from Dr. Feld's practice involving a patient revised at 4 years with elevated serum cobalt (32 mcg/L) and evidence of ARMD on explant pathology. Notes this is one of several similar complaints accumulating from Feld's cluster and that the explant will be sent to Meridian Testing Labs for wear analysis.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: MDR Filing - TW-2022-0891 (Feld patient, revision at 4 yrs) - Filed and Cross-Referenced
gist: Okonkwo confirms the MDR was filed on time and instructs Mitchell to cross-reference it internally with three other Feld-cluster complaints in TrackWise for the quarterly trend report, given the pattern of elevated cobalt readings.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: FDA Effectiveness Check Status Call
gist: Calendar invite for a routine internal status call to review effectiveness check completion rates for the June 2022 recall, ahead of the mandated 30/60/90-day reports to FDA. No substantive content in the invite itself beyond meeting logistics and attendee list.
gray_rationale: Pure scheduling for a topic that is itself responsive, but the invite carries no substantive content, so a strict reviewer would exclude it.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: FDA Effectiveness Check Status Call - 90-Day Report Draft
gist: Raman circulates the draft 90-day effectiveness check report for FDA showing 96% of the 412 implanted-lot patients' surgeons had been notified, with follow-up ongoing for the remainder. Asks Okonkwo to review before the December 15 FDA submission deadline.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA Informal Inquiry - MDL Awareness
gist: Okonkwo relays that an FDA compliance officer informally asked whether Veridian was aware of the newly filed state-court suits referencing ApexHip metal-ion complaints, and whether that changes MDR reporting practices. Okonkwo instructs Mitchell to prepare a brief written response confirming ongoing MDR compliance and no change in reporting threshold, coordinating with Rachel Steinberg given the litigation context.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: FDA Informal Inquiry - MDL Awareness - Draft Response
gist: Mitchell shares the draft response letter to FDA confirming Veridian's continued MDR compliance program and complaint trending practices, noting the letter avoids characterizing pending litigation. Steinberg is asked to review for legal tone before it goes out under Okonkwo's signature.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Notification of Voluntary Market Withdrawal - ApexHip Total Hip System
gist: Formal letter notifying FDA that Veridian intends to voluntarily withdraw the ApexHip system from the US market effective February 2, 2024, citing the totality of registry data (NJR 7.1% five-year revision rate, AJRR trends) and the MDL formed in December 2023. Distinguishes this withdrawal from the 2022 coating recall, clarifying it addresses the separate metal-ion/wear performance profile. States existing patients should continue routine follow-up per surgeon judgment.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Notification of Voluntary Market Withdrawal - Internal Distribution
gist: Okonkwo circulates the filed withdrawal letter internally, asking Novak to prepare an updated registry data summary and Raman to ensure complaint trending reports for Q4 2023 are finalized in case FDA follows up with questions during the withdrawal review period.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: FDA Request for Additional Information - Withdrawal Notification
gist: Mitchell forwards an FDA request for additional information regarding the market withdrawal, asking Veridian to provide the full complaint trending dataset from 2018-2023 and the September 2021 Registry Signal Review meeting materials. Mitchell notes the deadline for response is 30 days and asks whether Steinberg should be looped in given the document requests overlap with MDL discovery.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: FDA Request for Additional Information - Withdrawal Notification - Data Compilation
gist: Okonkwo assigns Novak to compile the 2018-2023 registry and complaint trend dataset, and Raman to gather the underlying TrackWise trend reports referenced in the September 2021 Registry Signal Review. Notes the response letter itself will be drafted by Mitchell once data is compiled, targeting submission by February 14, 2024.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: FDA Request for Additional Information - Withdrawal Notification - Response Submission
gist: Formal response letter to FDA providing the compiled complaint trending data, registry analyses, and a summary of the September 2021 Registry Signal Review decision-making process, submitted one day ahead of the February 14 deadline. States Veridian believes the voluntary withdrawal, announced February 2, 2024, appropriately addresses the identified performance signal.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Post-Withdrawal MDR Filing - Continuing Complaints
gist: Mitchell notes that despite the market withdrawal, complaints continue to arrive for previously implanted ApexHip units and confirms the MDR filing obligation continues for these units under 21 CFR 803. Reports two new MDRs filed in February 2024 for revision surgeries with elevated cobalt findings, both cross-referenced to the ongoing trend report.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Post-Withdrawal MDR Filing - Continuing Complaints - SOP Confirmation
gist: Okonkwo confirms the complaint handling and MDR filing SOPs remain in effect post-withdrawal and instructs the team to maintain the same trending cadence established after the 2021 483 response, since implanted units will continue to generate complaints for years.

author: Paula Nguyen
subject: IT Ticket - Regulatory SharePoint Access Restored
gist: IT service desk boilerplate confirming Okonkwo's access to the Regulatory Affairs SharePoint site has been restored after a password reset, unrelated to any substantive regulatory content. Purely an IT ticket closure notice.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA Closeout - Withdrawal Docket Reference
gist: Okonkwo informs the group that FDA has closed its review of the withdrawal notification without further comment, referencing the docket number for internal recordkeeping. Notes the recall docket (Z-1418-2022) remains separately open pending final effectiveness check confirmation, distinguishing the two matters clearly for the file.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: ApexHip concept design kickoff notes
gist: Halvorsen circulates initial concept design notes for the ApexHip system, describing the Co/Cr femoral head and stem paired with a new titanium porous coating from the recently evaluated KBT technology. Lists target design inputs: head diameters 36-50mm, cup sizes 44-62mm, target wear rate below existing ClassicHip benchmark, and a target inclination range for cup placement. Notes that design inputs are expected to be finalized and approved by September 2015. Mentions the team is still deciding on wear-test protocol standards and references ISO 14242 as the likely baseline. Tone is technical and forward-looking, entirely about early design planning.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: ApexHip concept design kickoff notes
gist: Raman confirms design inputs were approved in a design review, listing the finalized specs (head sizes, cup sizes, target wear performance) and asks Halvorsen to begin drafting the FMEA for the acetabular cup coating interface. She notes complaint-handling procedures will need updating once the product nears launch but that's a later-stage task. The email quotes Halvorsen's original kickoff notes below.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: KBT acquisition closes - KinetiCoat now ours
gist: Mendes announces the closing of the $41M acquisition of Kinetic Bearing Technologies, giving Veridian rights to the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating technology. He notes the due diligence report flagged limited long-term adhesion data for the coating and asks Halvorsen to factor that into the ApexHip cup coating validation plan. Ends with marketing excitement about positioning KinetiCoat as a differentiator for bone ingrowth.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: RE: KBT acquisition closes - KinetiCoat now ours
gist: halvorsen replies tersely that he's already flagged the adhesion data gap to the design team and wants a dedicated coating adhesion test added to the DHF verification plan before DR-3. says he'll bring it up formally at the design review. quoted history below shows Mendes's original announcement.

author: Priya Raman
subject: DR-3 Design Review - ApexHip Wear Test Protocol
gist: Calendar invite for the DR-3 design review meeting to be held at the Hub, agenda item being finalization of the wear-test protocol per ISO 14242. No substantive content beyond meeting logistics, room (Reserve conference room B), and attendee list.
gray_rationale: A reviewer might consider a design review calendar invite responsive as part of the design history, but with no substantive content it is more appropriately excluded as pure scheduling.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: DR-3 Design Review Minutes - Wear Test Protocol Approval
gist: Minutes of the DR-3 design review documenting the decision to adopt ISO 14242 wear testing at the standard 45-degree inclination angle only, rejecting a proposal from Halvorsen to also test at higher inclination angles (55 degrees) as out of scope and cost-prohibitive given timeline pressure for the 510(k) submission. Attendees: Halvorsen, Raman, Mendes, Okonkwo. Action items include finalizing the verification test plan and sending samples to Meridian Testing Labs. Notes the coating adhesion test proposed by Halvorsen was added to the plan per his earlier email.

author: Meridian Testing Labs
subject: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report - ApexHip Prototype Lot P-001
gist: Formal wear test report from Meridian Testing Labs summarizing results of ISO 14242 wear simulation testing on ApexHip prototype units at the standard 45-degree cup inclination angle. Reports wear rate of 2.1 mm3 per million cycles, well within acceptable range compared to predicate ClassicHip. Notes testing was conducted only at 45 degrees per the approved protocol; no off-angle or edge-loading testing was performed. Concludes the design meets wear performance targets under the tested conditions.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: RE: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report - ApexHip Prototype Lot P-001
gist: Halvorsen forwards the Meridian wear test report to Raman and Okonkwo, noting the results look good for the 510(k) submission but privately flags in the last paragraph that he still thinks edge-loading behavior at higher inclination angles is untested and could be relevant given anatomical variation in cup placement across surgeons. Suggests it as a future R&D item post-launch rather than a submission blocker.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: DHF index for ApexHip - please review sections
gist: Okonkwo circulates the design history file index for ApexHip ahead of 510(k) submission, listing required sections: design inputs, design outputs, verification (wear test, coating adhesion), validation, risk analysis (FMEA), and design review records including DR-3 minutes. Asks each recipient to confirm their sections are complete and cross-referenced correctly per 21 CFR 820.30. Entirely administrative/organizational about the DHF compilation.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: DHF index for ApexHip - please review sections
gist: Raman confirms the FMEA section is complete, listing the top risk items identified: coating delamination (mitigated by process controls per KBT integration), stem fracture (mitigated by material spec), and wear debris generation (mitigated by surface finish spec, tested per the approved 45-degree protocol). Notes higher-inclination wear was discussed but deemed out of scope for this design cycle per DR-3 decision.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: submission timeline
gist: Short Teams chat where Halvorsen asks Mendes about the target 510(k) submission date and Mendes confirms early March, tied to the sales kickoff planning in Dallas for April. No substantive design content, purely scheduling and business planning chatter.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: 510(k) Submission Checklist - ApexHip K162447
gist: Internal regulatory checklist form tracking completeness of the 510(k) submission package for ApexHip, referencing predicate device ClassicHip. Line items include substantial equivalence comparison, biocompatibility data, sterilization validation, and the ISO 14242 wear test summary (45-degree protocol) as an attachment reference. All items checked complete as of the form date. Signed by Okonkwo and Mitchell.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: ApexHip cleared - 510(k) K162447
gist: Okonkwo announces FDA has granted 510(k) clearance for ApexHip under K162447 with ClassicHip as predicate, effective March 9 2017. She thanks the design and regulatory teams and notes the clearance letter references the wear testing and coating adhesion data submitted. Castellano replies briefly congratulating the team, no substantive content in his reply.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: launch prep
gist: Casual Teams chat about launch event catering and booth setup for the April 17 Dallas sales kickoff. Mendes asks Halvorsen if he can attend to answer engineering questions from reps; Halvorsen agrees. No design or wear-test substance discussed.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Post-launch design monitoring plan for ApexHip
gist: Halvorsen drafts a memo proposing a post-market design monitoring plan, recommending the team periodically re-evaluate wear performance data as real-world usage data (registry and complaint data) accumulates, specifically flagging that cup inclination angles in actual surgical practice may exceed the 45-degree condition tested in the original verification protocol. Suggests revisiting higher-angle wear testing within 18-24 months of launch. This recommendation sits in the middle of the memo among other routine monitoring items like coating lot traceability and complaint volume thresholds.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Design change control process reminder
gist: Routine reminder email from Mendes about the ECO (engineering change order) process for any post-launch design modifications to ApexHip, referencing the standard change control SOP. No specific change discussed yet, purely procedural reminder ahead of anticipated future updates.
gray_rationale: A generic process reminder with no specific design content is arguably outside design-history scope, but it directly concerns the design change control mechanism that governs the ApexHip design history file.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Early complaint trend - coating and revision surgeries
gist: Raman reports a small early uptick in complaints logged in TrackWise related to ApexHip revisions, noting two cases mention surgeon-reported difficulty with cup seating and one note referencing higher observed wear on retrieval. She asks Halvorsen whether this could relate to the inclination angle limitation discussed at DR-3, tying the emerging complaint signal back to the original design decision to test only at 45 degrees.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: RE: Early complaint trend - coating and revision surgeries
gist: Halvorsen responds that it's too early to draw conclusions from two cases but agrees the inclination angle question from DR-3 is worth keeping on the radar. Says he'll start compiling retrieval analysis data informally to see if a pattern emerges before recommending any formal re-test. Quoted history includes Raman's original message.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: ApexHip retrieval analysis tracker - informal
gist: Spreadsheet summary Halvorsen maintains informally tracking retrieved ApexHip components sent back for analysis after revision surgeries. Columns include lot number (cup lots V-2xxx, head lots H-3xxx), surgeon, implant duration, and observed wear pattern notes. Six entries logged so far, three noting wear patterns consistent with edge-loading at estimated high inclination angles. Table sits mid-document after an intro paragraph explaining the tracker's informal purpose pending a possible formal re-test.

author: Priya Raman
subject: coating lot question
gist: Quick chat where Raman asks Halvorsen to confirm which KinetiCoat batch spec version was used for early production lots for a customer inquiry. Halvorsen confirms the version number. Purely a lot-traceability administrative question, not about design history substance or wear performance.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: KneeFlex design review scheduling
gist: Mendes schedules an upcoming KneeFlex design review meeting, listing agenda items about the knee implant's own FMEA and wear testing timeline. Mentions in passing that KneeFlex's design control process will mirror what was used for ApexHip, but the substance is entirely about the KneeFlex product, a different device.
gray_rationale: The email references the ApexHip design control process only by analogy for a different product, which a strict reviewer would treat as non-responsive since no ApexHip substance is discussed.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Proposal to re-run ApexHip wear testing at higher inclination angles
gist: Formal memo from Halvorsen proposing a new round of wear testing at 55-degree cup inclination, citing the accumulating retrieval data from his informal tracker showing edge-loading wear patterns and the 2018 Atlanta complaint cluster as motivating factors. References the original DR-3 decision to limit testing to 45 degrees and argues real-world surgical variation in cup placement justifies revisiting that assumption now, roughly two years post-launch as he'd recommended in his 2017 monitoring memo. Requests budget and lab time with Meridian Testing Labs.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Proposal to re-run ApexHip wear testing at higher inclination angles
gist: Raman supports Halvorsen's proposal to re-test at 55 degrees, noting the complaint trend data from Quality corroborates his retrieval findings, and asks Okonkwo to weigh in on regulatory implications of new test data given the existing 510(k) clearance. Quoted history includes Halvorsen's memo summary.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: budget question
gist: Mendes asks Halvorsen how much the proposed re-testing would cost and how long it would delay any other planned engineering work; Halvorsen gives a rough estimate of cost and a 6-8 week lab turnaround with Meridian. Brief, logistical, but directly tied to the re-testing proposal already circulating.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: 55-degree wear retest results - concerning
gist: Halvorsen reports that re-running ISO 14242 wear testing at 55 degree inclination (versus the original 45 degree protocol from DR-3) shows 4-6x higher wear rates at the cup rim, consistent with edge-loading. He attaches Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx and says this could explain the Atlanta metal-ion cluster logged in TrackWise. He proposes convening a design review to discuss a possible cup geometry change and flags this as urgent, not routine. Tone is worried, blunt engineer language.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: 55-degree wear retest results - concerning
gist: Raman responds cautiously, noting the original wear-test protocol approved at DR-3 only specified 45 degrees per then-current practice and asking whether the 55-degree condition reflects realistic surgical positioning or a worst-case outlier. She asks Halvorsen to loop in Meridian Testing Labs for an independent read before escalating further, worried about overreacting. She references TW-2019-0417 as the complaint record possibly linked.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: 55-degree wear retest results - concerning
gist: Mendes weighs in from a product management view, saying a geometry change now would disrupt the sales narrative around 'designed to last' and asks if there's a way to address this through updated surgical technique guidance (targeting lower cup inclination angles at implantation) instead of a hardware redesign. He suggests raising it at the next design review but wants messaging kept internal for now.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Design Review - Apex Wear Data Follow-up
gist: Meeting invite for a design review to discuss the 55-degree wear retest findings and consider ECO options. Location Warsaw Hub conference room, agenda attached separately. Purely scheduling with a one-line description referencing the wear data as the topic.
gray_rationale: The invite itself is scheduling logistics but names the wear-data topic directly, so a reviewer would likely still code it responsive though a stricter reviewer might treat it as pure scheduling.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Design Review Minutes - Apex Wear Data Follow-up
gist: Minutes record attendees Halvorsen, Raman, Mendes, Okonkwo. Summary: 55-degree wear retest data reviewed; team acknowledges edge-loading wear risk at high inclination but decides not to change the wear-test protocol used for regulatory submissions (remains 45 degrees per K162447 predicate comparison). A design change proposal for cup rim geometry is opened as ECO-2019-118 but deferred pending further clinical correlation data and cost-benefit analysis. Action item: Halvorsen to draft design change rationale memo; Raman to monitor complaint trend; Okonkwo to assess regulatory reporting implications separately.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Design Change Rationale - ECO-2019-118 (Cup Rim Geometry)
gist: Formal memo documenting the technical rationale for proposed ECO-2019-118, a cup rim geometry modification intended to reduce edge-loading wear at higher inclination angles. Describes the 2019 wear retest methodology, the 4-6x wear multiplier found at 55 degrees versus baseline 45-degree testing, and references the original 2016 DR-3 protocol decision to test only at 45 degrees per then-industry-standard practice. Recommends either a redesign or supplemental surgical technique guidance; notes cost estimate of $2.1M for tooling changes and 9-month timeline if pursued. Concludes with an explicit statement that the change has been deferred by management pending additional clinical correlation data.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Regulatory implications of deferred ECO-2019-118
gist: Okonkwo, precise and citing 21 CFR 820.30 design control requirements, writes that deferring ECO-2019-118 must be documented in the DHF with clear rationale to withstand audit scrutiny, and separately flags that if complaint trending (TW records) shows a statistically meaningful increase tied to the wear issue, an MDR reportability assessment may be triggered independent of the design decision. She asks Raman to run updated trend numbers for the next 90 days.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Apex wear test data summary - 45 vs 55 degree comparison
gist: Spreadsheet summary described in text with a small table comparing wear rates: at 45 degrees inclination, average wear rate 2.1 mm3/million cycles; at 55 degrees, 9.8-12.6 mm3/million cycles (4.7-6x increase). Table lists test conditions, head sizes (36-50mm), cup lot samples used (from early V-2xxx production runs), and Meridian Testing Labs report reference numbers. Bottom note states this data supports the ECO-2019-118 rationale memo and should be retained in the DHF folder for wear testing.

author: Priya Raman
subject: 90-day complaint trend update - Apex metal ion
gist: Raman provides the requested 90-day trend: 11 new TrackWise complaints involving elevated cobalt/chromium or revision surgery, up from 6 in the prior period, concentrated among Dr. Feld's Atlanta patients and a smaller Nashville cluster. She notes the increase correlates temporally with the wear-mechanism concerns Halvorsen raised but says a formal statistical significance test hasn't been run yet. She recommends continued monitoring rather than immediate MDR escalation, pending Okonkwo's regulatory read.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: eco status
gist: Short Teams chat where Halvorsen asks Raman for a status check on ECO-2019-118 since management hasn't formally closed or approved it, and mentions he's still uneasy leaving the cup geometry unchanged given the wear data. Raman replies it's still parked pending the cost-benefit review and Okonkwo's regulatory memo, and that no timeline has been set. Casual, lowercase, a few typos.

author: Meridian Testing Labs
subject: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report - ApexHip Supplemental Inclination Study

Report is addressed to Halvorsen for internal distribution to the design team.

He asks whether this changes anyone's view on urgency.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: FW: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report - ApexHip Supplemental Inclination Study

author: Tom Halvorsen

author: Priya Raman

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: RE: Complaint trend continuing to climb - request to revisit ECO-2019-118

author: Tom Halvorsen

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Re-test results at 55 degree inclination - concerning wear rates

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Re-test results at 55 degree inclination - concerning wear rates

author: Tom Halvorsen

author: Tom Halvorsen

Concludes with a statement that this evaluation will be revisited annually or upon new signal.

subject: ECO-2019-118 formal closure memo
gist: Formal memo closing ECO-2019-118 for the DHF. Recounts full history: design inputs approved 2015-09, DR-3 in Nov 2016 approved the ISO 14242 wear-test protocol at standard 45-degree inclination only, K162447 clearance March 2017, launch April 2017. States that in Feb 2019 Halvorsen re-ran wear testing at 55-degree inclination and found 4-6x wear versus standard testing, prompting the ECO proposal for a design change to the cup/liner geometry. Documents that the change was deferred in mid-2019 due to projected $2-3M requalification cost and an 18-month timeline that leadership determined was not warranted given market performance data available at the time. Formally closes the ECO as

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Coating flaking on incoming inspection - two hospital reports
gist: Kowalski reports that incoming inspection at Northgate Health System and a Denver hospital found KinetiCoat flaking on unwrapped acetabular cups from lots V-2214 and V-2231. He notes both lots were made at the Cork plant between Dec 2021 and Jan 2022, right after a chamber maintenance event in November. He asks Raman to open TrackWise complaints and wants to know if other lots in that range should be pulled for review. Tone is worried, operational, references batch records.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Coating flaking on incoming inspection - two hospital reports
gist: Raman confirms she has opened TrackWise complaints TW-2022-0311 and TW-2022-0312 for the Northgate and Denver reports, and loops in Okonkwo given the pattern suggests a possible reportable trend. She asks Kowalski for the full list of cup lots produced in the affected window so they can assess scope, and flags this could implicate more than two lots.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Coating flaking on incoming inspection - two hospital reports
gist: Okonkwo directs that a formal lot trace begin immediately per 21 CFR 820.100 and asks Kowalski to pull the plasma-spray process parameters (chamber temperature, spray rate, standoff distance) for all lots produced Nov 2021 through Feb 2022. She wants a root-cause hypothesis within a week and says she will assess MDR reportability once more data is in hand.

author: Priya Raman
subject: TrackWise Complaint Intake TW-2022-0311
gist: Complaint intake form for a cup from lot V-2214 received at Northgate Health System; purchasing contact Deb Marsh reported coating flaking off in visible flakes upon opening the sterile package, unit not implanted. Fields include product code, lot number, date received, device disposition (quarantined, returned to Warsaw for analysis), and initial risk assessment marked 'potential trend - notify RA'. Investigation status is open, assigned to Priya Raman.

author: Priya Raman
subject: TrackWise Complaint Intake TW-2022-0312
gist: Second complaint intake form, this one from a Denver hospital (unnamed purchasing contact), for a cup from lot V-2231 with the same coating flaking issue observed during incoming inspection, unit not implanted. Notes the similarity to TW-2022-0311 filed the day before and recommends escalation to a coordinated investigation rather than handling as isolated events.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Cork chamber maintenance
gist: Halvorsen asks Kowalski in a Teams chat what exactly changed during the November chamber maintenance event, since he's heard plasma-spray parameters may have drifted afterward. Kowalski replies that a heating element was replaced and recalibration records show the spray rate setpoint was off by a small margin for a few weeks before someone caught it. Short, informal, technical back and forth.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Preliminary Root Cause Assessment - KinetiCoat Adhesion Failures
gist: Formal memo from Kowalski summarizing the Cork plant investigation: plasma-spray chamber maintenance on 2021-11-18 led to an undetected drift in spray parameters (chamber temperature and standoff distance) that persisted through early February 2022, affecting cup lots in the V-2200 through V-2299 range. Bond strength testing on retained samples from these lots shows adhesion values below the specification of 20 MPa, some as low as 12 MPa, versus lots outside the range which test at 24-28 MPa. Recommends quarantining all remaining inventory in the affected lot range and considering field action. Includes a small table of tested lots and bond strength values.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: MDR reportability assessment - coating adhesion
gist: Okonkwo circulates her assessment that the coating adhesion issue meets 21 CFR 803.50 MDR reportability criteria since it could cause serious injury if implanted, and states she intends to file MDRs for the two known complaints within the 30-day window. She also raises the question of whether a field action (recall) is warranted given the scope of affected lots identified in Kowalski's root cause memo, and asks Steinberg to weigh in on process for outside counsel notification.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Draft lot trace results - V-2200 series
gist: Raman sends the completed lot trace showing 1,140 units in the V-2200-V-2299 range were distributed, with 412 confirmed implanted based on hospital tracking records; remaining units are believed to be in hospital inventory or Veridian's own warehouse. She notes distribution went to approximately 60 hospital accounts across the US and a smaller number in the EU, and flags that identifying exact implant dates for the 412 units will take additional time working with hospital risk management contacts.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Apex Coating Issue - Field Action Decision Meeting
gist: Calendar invite for a meeting to decide whether to initiate a voluntary recall of the affected cup lots; agenda line references root cause memo and lot trace results as pre-reads. No substantive discussion in the invite itself beyond meeting logistics and attached documents list.
gray_rationale: A scheduling invite with only a topic reference and pre-read list could be seen as non-substantive, but naming the specific decision (recall of affected lots) makes it reasonably responsive.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Minutes - Apex Coating Issue Field Action Decision Meeting
gist: Meeting minutes documenting the decision to proceed with a voluntary Class II recall of cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 due to KinetiCoat adhesion failures, distinct from any metal-ion concerns which were explicitly noted as out of scope for this action. Attendees discussed the 1,140 units distributed and 412 implanted figures, agreed on a target recall initiation date of mid-June 2022, assigned Okonkwo to draft the FDA notification and Raman to prepare hospital notification letters, and asked Park to begin financial reserve modeling. Action items and owners listed at the end.

author: Owen Park
subject: RE: Minutes - Apex Coating Issue Field Action Decision Meeting
gist: Park acknowledges the meeting outcome and asks for the estimated per-unit replacement/return cost and any anticipated litigation exposure so he can begin scoping a reserve, noting he wants to loop in Hannah Berg for the modeling work. Mostly financial/process, but explicitly references the planned recall of the coating lots decided in the prior meeting.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Draft hospital notification letter for review
