gist: Raman sends Mendes a draft of the hospital notification letter for the upcoming recall, asking him to review the language for tone before it goes to Legal. The draft references lot numbers V-2200-V-2299, describes the coating adhesion issue found during incoming inspection, and instructs hospitals to quarantine unused units and await further instructions. She emphasizes the letter must not reference the metal-ion registry data since this is a manufacturing issue only.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Notification letter tone
gist: Mendes gives quick feedback in Teams that the draft letter reads a bit alarming and suggests softening 'immediately quarantine' to 'promptly quarantine' and adding a line thanking hospitals for their partnership. Raman pushes back slightly, saying Legal wants the urgency preserved given the adhesion failure risk. Short exchange, references the same lot range.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: MDR filings for TW-2022-0311 and TW-2022-0312
gist: Okonkwo directs Mitchell to prepare and file two MDRs with FDA for the Northgate and Denver coating complaints, citing the 30-calendar-day requirement from date of awareness (April 4-5, 2022). She provides draft narrative language describing the flaking observed on lots V-2214 and V-2231 and instructs him to reference the ongoing root cause investigation but not to speculate on scope until the field action is finalized.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Medical Device Report - ApexHip Acetabular Cup Coating Adhesion Failure
gist: Formal MDR narrative letter submitted to FDA describing two complaint events (lots V-2214 and V-2231) where KinetiCoat coating was found flaking off acetabular cups during hospital incoming inspection prior to implantation, no patient injury occurred, and Veridian's internal investigation into root cause is ongoing. States Veridian will supplement the report with root cause findings and any field action determination. References TrackWise complaint numbers.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Updated lot list - additional flaking samples found in retained inventory testing
gist: Kowalski reports that destructive bond-strength testing on retained samples from three additional lots (V-2247, V-2255, V-2268) found adhesion below spec, expanding the confirmed problem set within the V-2200-V-2299 range. He recommends the recall scope remain the full 100-lot range rather than narrowing it, since retained sample testing suggests the drift was continuous through the affected period rather than sporadic.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Updated lot list - additional flaking samples found in retained inventory testing
gist: Okonkwo agrees to keep the full V-2200-V-2299 lot range in scope for the recall based on Kowalski's expanded testing findings, and says she will update the draft FDA recall notification accordingly before the planned filing. She asks Steinberg to confirm the recall classification recommendation (Class II) is still appropriate given the expanded but still coating-only scope.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Cork line status
gist: Raman asks Kowalski whether the Cork line is still running the same plasma-spray process or if a correction has been made yet. Kowalski says the line was paused on May 9 pending a corrective action plan and recalibration of the chamber, and that no new lots have shipped since. Brief, operational chat with no mention of complaints beyond confirming the pause.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Cork production schedule - unrelated ShoulderPro line move
gist: Kowalski gives Raman a heads up that the ShoulderPro assembly line is being relocated within the Cork plant next month to make room for expanded KneeFlex production, and asks if she needs anything from him before the move disrupts the floor for a few days. No mention of the Apex coating investigation or recall; purely a facilities/scheduling note about other product lines.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: Aegis notice - preliminary heads up
gist: Steinberg, marked 'privileged & confidential', tells Okonkwo and Park she plans to send a preliminary notice of circumstance to Aegis Specialty Insurance once the recall is formally initiated, given potential future claims tied to the coating lots. She asks Park to have reserve estimate numbers ready to reference, though she notes the letter itself will be brief and general at this stage.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Distributed lot inventory tracker - V-2200 series
gist: Spreadsheet summary listing all 100 lots in the V-2200-V-2299 range with columns for units produced, units distributed, units returned/quarantined to date, and hospital account names including Northgate Health System and several others. Totals confirm 1,140 units distributed and running tally toward the 412 implanted figure, with about 60% of unimplanted stock already located and quarantined as of this date. Table includes a note that EU distribution (about 90 units) is being traced separately with the Cork logistics team.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Heads up before it goes wide
gist: Mendes gives Jenna Whitfield an informal early heads up in Teams that a recall notice for certain Apex cup lots is coming soon and that sales reps should not proactively discuss it with surgeons until the official communication goes out. Jenna asks if it affects the whole Southeast region and Mendes says only accounts that received the specific V-2200 series lots, referencing that Northgate is one of the affected hospitals.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Draft FDA recall notification - please review
gist: Okonkwo sends Steinberg the draft recall notification package intended for FDA, describing the KinetiCoat adhesion failure root cause, the affected lot range V-2200-V-2299, distribution numbers (1,140 distributed, 412 implanted), and proposed Class II classification, with a target submission date before the June 14 planned initiation. Asks for legal sign-off by end of week. Content largely restates prior findings in formal recall-notification format.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: RE: Draft FDA recall notification - please review
gist: Steinberg approves the draft with minor wording edits, marked privileged and confidential, and reminds Okonkwo to keep the recall communications strictly focused on the coating adhesion issue without referencing wear rates, revision rates, or any registry data, since those are separate matters being handled elsewhere. She confirms Class II classification language is acceptable.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Effectiveness check plan - draft outline
gist: Raman circulates a draft plan for post-recall effectiveness checks, proposing to contact all approximately 60 affected hospital accounts within 30, 60, and 90 days after notification to confirm receipt of the recall letter and disposition of remaining inventory, targeting at least 95% response rate per FDA guidance. Includes a placeholder tracking log referencing lot numbers and account names to be finalized once the recall officially launches.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Corrective action for the chamber
gist: Kowalski tells Halvorsen the corrective action plan for the plasma-spray chamber includes new automated parameter alarms and a revised preventive maintenance checklist, expected to be validated before the line restarts in July. Halvorsen asks if this connects at all to his 2019 wear-test findings and Kowalski clarifies no, this is purely a coating adhesion process fix unrelated to the wear/inclination angle issue Halvorsen worked on.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Team dinner June 10 - save the date
gist: Jenna sends a quick note to her reps Sarah Kim and Mike Ruiz about a team dinner planned for June 10 to celebrate closing a big Nashville account, asking for RSVPs and any dietary restrictions. No mention of the recall or any product issues; purely social/logistics planning within the sales team.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Final go/no-go for June 14 recall initiation
gist: Okonkwo confirms all pieces are ready for the planned June 14 recall initiation: FDA notification finalized, hospital letters printed and ready to mail, effectiveness check plan approved, and reserve estimate from Park's team incorporated. She asks Castellano for final executive sign-off, restating the scope (V-2200-V-2299, 1,140 distributed, 412 implanted, coating adhesion root cause) and confirming the recall is being classified as Class II by Veridian pending FDA concurrence.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Recall Z-1418-2022 - lot reconciliation status
gist: Raman reports on progress reconciling distribution records for cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 following the 14 June recall initiation; states 1,140 units distributed with 412 confirmed implanted per hospital returns so far, and requests Kowalski confirm the Cork batch records for the affected chamber maintenance window. Mentions TrackWise complaint TW-2022-0511 tied to the coating flaking. Tone is careful and procedural, urging accuracy for the FDA effectiveness check report due at 30 days.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: RE: Recall Z-1418-2022 - lot reconciliation status
gist: Kowalski confirms the Cork plant records show the plasma-spray chamber maintenance event occurred 3 Nov 2021, coinciding with the start of lot V-2200; he attaches (by filename) Cork_batch_log_Nov21-Feb22.xlsx and notes the drift in spray parameters was not caught until incoming inspection flagged flaking coating at two hospitals. He confirms the line resumed standard parameters after V-2299.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Recall messaging for the field
gist: Lee asks Whitfield and Mendes to make sure reps have talking points for hospitals asking about the V-2200-V-2299 recall, worried about lost confidence hurting Q3 numbers; he wants a one-pager reps can hand to purchasing. No detailed root-cause info given, mostly sales anxiety and urgency.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Recall messaging for the field
gist: Mendes shares a draft customer-facing FAQ describing the recall as limited to KinetiCoat adhesion in cup lots V-2200-V-2299 manufactured Cork Nov2021-Feb2022, distinguishing it from any general product performance issue, and asks Okonkwo to review language before distribution to hospitals like Northgate Health System.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Urgent Medical Device Recall Notice - ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200 to V-2299
gist: Formal recall notification letter to Northgate Health System (GPO VantageOne) describing the voluntary Class II recall, FDA recall number Z-1418-2022, affected lots V-2200 through V-2299, the coating adhesion defect discovered at incoming inspection, and instructions to quarantine unused units and complete an enclosed response/reconciliation form. States 1,140 units distributed nationally.

author: Northgate Health System
subject: Recall Response and Reconciliation Form - ApexHip Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299
gist: Completed hospital response form listing units received, units in stock quarantined (6 units, cup lot V-2214), units implanted (2 patients, lot V-2231), and confirming no adverse events reported to date; signed by hospital materials manager Denise Farraday and returned per the recall letter instructions.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Effectiveness check plan - draft
gist: Raman outlines the draft effectiveness check plan required under 21 CFR 806 to confirm recall notices reached all affected accounts, proposing a two-round telephone/email verification of consignees at 30 and 60 days, with a target of 100% response rate; cites the recall scope of 1,140 distributed units and the 412 implanted figure as the baseline for tracking.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Effectiveness check plan - draft
gist: Okonkwo approves the plan with minor edits, asking Raman to add a field capturing whether any quarantined units show visible coating flaking on inspection, since that data may support the CAPA root-cause analysis being drafted separately with Kowalski.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: CAPA-2022-0093 root cause draft
gist: Kowalski sends a draft root-cause summary for CAPA-2022-0093 attributing the coating adhesion failures to plasma-spray parameter drift following a chamber maintenance event, with corrective actions including revised preventive maintenance checklist and post-maintenance calibration verification before restart; explicitly states this is a manufacturing/coating issue unrelated to the metal-ion wear concerns tracked separately.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Teams - recall admin
gist: Short chat where Raman asks if the CAPA number should also be cross-referenced in the FDA recall report submission; Okonkwo confirms yes and reminds her the report is due by day 30, i.e. 14 July.

author: James Whitaker
subject: Concerns regarding recalled ApexHip cups and separate revision cases
gist: Dr. Whitaker (Denver) writes complaining both about a recalled cup lot (V-2247) that arrived with flaking coating detected at incoming inspection at his hospital, and separately about two unrelated revision surgeries he has performed on ApexHip patients for suspected metal-ion issues; the recall content is in the first two paragraphs, the revision complaints are appended lower in the letter.

author: Priya Raman
subject: FW: Concerns regarding recalled ApexHip cups and separate revision cases
gist: Raman forwards Whitaker's letter, flagging that the coating complaint should go into the recall effectiveness tracking while the revision cases should be separately logged in TrackWise for MDR evaluation; she asks Novak whether the two Whitaker revision cases already appear in the registry signal dataset.

author: Priya Raman
subject: MDR Decision Worksheet - TW-2022-0511 Coating Flaking, Denver Site
gist: MDR decision worksheet evaluating whether the coating flaking complaint at the Denver hospital (cup lot V-2247, TW-2022-0511) meets 21 CFR 803 reportability criteria; concludes the event did not cause or contribute to a serious injury since the flaking was caught at inspection before implantation, so no MDR filed, but notes the event is being tracked under CAPA-2022-0093.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA recall report submission - final review
gist: Okonkwo asks Mitchell to finalize the FDA recall report package for Z-1418-2022 before the 14 July deadline, referencing CAPA-2022-0093, the Cork batch records, and Kowalski's root-cause narrative; wants Mitchell to double check the distributed/implanted unit counts (1,140 / 412) match the reconciliation spreadsheet.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: FDA recall report submission - final review
gist: Mitchell confirms the numbers match and attaches (by filename) Apex_recall_FDA_report_Z1418_final.pdf, noting the submission will go out a day early on 13 July; mentions no open discrepancies remain in the effectiveness check data collected so far.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Recall Effectiveness Check Tracker - 30 Day Snapshot
gist: Spreadsheet summary showing consignee response rates: 210 accounts contacted, 189 responded (90%), 6 units confirmed quarantined, 2 units confirmed implanted with no adverse events reported, and 21 accounts still pending follow-up; includes a small table breaking down by region (Southeast, Midwest, West) with the West region (Denver, including Northgate-adjacent facilities) showing the highest pending count.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Recall follow-up calls - Southeast accounts
gist: Whitfield asks her reps to complete outstanding recall follow-up calls to Southeast hospital accounts still listed as pending in the effectiveness tracker, reminding them the deadline for round-two verification is end of month; references the recall notice sent in June without restating technical detail.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Teams - recall calls
gist: Kim reports she reached three of her five pending Atlanta accounts and all confirmed no affected lots in stock; asks whether she needs written confirmation or a verbal note is sufficient for the tracker.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Q3 kickoff dinner - Atlanta
gist: Lee asks Whitfield to help plan logistics for a Q3 regional sales kickoff dinner in Atlanta, restaurant options and headcount, no mention of the recall or any product performance topic; purely scheduling and catering.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Cork line requalification - post recall
gist: Kowalski confirms the Cork plasma-spray line has completed requalification following the corrective actions in CAPA-2022-0093, with three consecutive validated production runs meeting coating adhesion spec; the line resumed normal cup production under lot series V-2320 onward, distinct from the recalled V-2200-V-2299 range.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Privileged & Confidential - Recall closure summary for legal file
gist: Okonkwo sends Steinberg a summary of recall closure status for the litigation hold file: effectiveness check complete at 96% response rate, CAPA-2022-0093 closed, no MDRs filed as a result of the coating issue itself, and Whitaker's separate revision complaints referred to the ongoing metal-ion complaint tracking; banner marks it privileged and confidential.

author: Sam Ibarra
subject: Texas distributor - remaining recalled stock

author: Priya Raman
subject: Lot trace confirmation - V-2200 through V-2299
gist: Raman confirms complaint-handling review has cross-referenced all incoming inspection complaints from Northgate Health System and a Denver hospital against the affected cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 manufactured at Cork Nov 2021-Feb 2022. States 1,140 units distributed, 412 implanted per current DHR reconciliation. Asks Kowalski to confirm no other lots share the same plasma-spray chamber maintenance window. Tone is procedural, cites TrackWise IDs TW-2022-0611 and TW-2022-0618 as the originating complaints.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: RE: Lot trace confirmation - V-2200 through V-2299
gist: Kowalski replies confirming the chamber maintenance event occurred between the two dates and that only lots V-2200-V-2299 ran the affected plasma-spray parameters; he notes lots before and after used verified settings per the calibration log. He mentions the line has since been requalified with a new coating adhesion test protocol. Buried in the middle he notes two additional cups from lot V-2245 were found in a Cork warehouse bin and need to be added to the recall inventory count.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Voluntary Recall Notification - ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299
gist: Formal recall notification letter to Northgate Health System's risk management office, referencing FDA recall number Z-1418-2022, describing the KinetiCoat adhesion failures found on unwrapping, instructing the hospital to quarantine remaining stock, and providing a return/replacement process. Includes instructions to complete and return the enclosed effectiveness check response form within 10 business days. Signed by Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Recall Effectiveness Check Response Log - Northgate Health System
gist: Completed effectiveness check tracking form for Northgate Health System, listing account number, contact name (hospital risk manager Denise Farrow), date notification received, quantity of affected units on hand at time of notice (6 units, lots V-2211 and V-2260), quantity returned, and confirmation checkbox that no further affected units are in use. Notes an outstanding call needed to confirm two implanted patients scheduled for surveillance imaging.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Customer messaging for recall follow-up calls
gist: Mendes sends the approved talking points sales reps should use when hospitals call about the V-2200-V-2299 recall, emphasizing it is a coating/manufacturing issue tied to a specific Cork production window and not related to any wear performance concerns. He asks Lee and Whitfield to ensure reps do not speculate about other lots. Mentions the FDA recall number Z-1418-2022 and directs any surgeon clinical questions to Dr. Adeyemi's office.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Customer messaging for recall follow-up calls
gist: Whitfield thanks Mendes and asks whether reps should proactively call hospitals that haven't reached out yet, or wait for inbound calls only. She notes Sarah Kim already fielded one call from a purchasing agent at a Georgia hospital asking if their stock includes any of the affected lots.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Recall call notes - Piedmont area hospital
gist: Kim summarizes a call with a purchasing coordinator confirming their facility has zero units from lots V-2200-V-2299 in current inventory, based on a lot check against the packing slips. She asks if she should still send the formal recall notice letter for their records even though they have no affected stock.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: plasma spray chamber data
gist: Teams chat where Halvorsen asks Kowalski for the raw thermocouple logs from the chamber during the Nov 2021-Feb 2022 window to help finalize the root cause report for the recall CAPA. Kowalski says he'll pull it from the historian system and flags that the maintenance work order number is WO-88214.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Root Cause Investigation Report - CAPA-2022-014, KinetiCoat Adhesion Failure
gist: Formal root cause report for the recall CAPA. States the plasma-spray parameter drift began after a chamber maintenance event in late October 2021, when a replacement nozzle was installed without re-verifying spray distance and powder feed rate against the qualified process window. Describes incoming inspection findings at Northgate and a Denver facility showing coating flaking on unwrapping. Documents corrective actions: chamber requalification, added in-process adhesion pull-test sampling, and revised maintenance SOP requiring post-work verification runs. Concludes containment (1,140 units distributed, 412 implanted) is complete and recommends closing CAPA-2022-014 pending effectiveness check completion.

author: Priya Raman
subject: MDR filing status for lot V-2200-V-2299 complaints
gist: Raman updates Okonkwo that all complaints tied to the recalled lots have been evaluated per 21 CFR 803 decision tree and that two events met MDR reportability criteria due to coating fragments observed during revision surgery, while the remainder were coded as non-reportable incoming-inspection findings with no patient exposure. She lists TrackWise IDs TW-2022-0611, TW-2022-0618, and TW-2022-0629, and confirms MDRs were filed within the 30-day window.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: MDR filing status for lot V-2200-V-2299 complaints
gist: Okonkwo asks Mitchell to confirm the FDA MDR submission confirmation numbers are logged in the regulatory tracker and reminds Raman that the recall report to FDA under 21 CFR 806 already references the same root cause language from Kowalski's CAPA report, so the two filings should stay consistent.

author: Dana Okonkwo
recipients: FDA CDRH / ODE, Office of Compliance
subject: Recall Status Update - Z-1418-2022, ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299
gist: Formal status update letter to FDA's Office of Compliance regarding recall Z-1418-2022, reporting that of the 1,140 distributed units, 640 have been returned or accounted for to date, and 412 remain implanted with no reported adverse patient outcomes attributable to the coating issue. Restates the root cause as plasma-spray parameter drift following the October 2021 chamber maintenance event and references CAPA-2022-014. Requests guidance on whether continued patient surveillance reporting is required.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Recall impact on Q3 pipeline
gist: Lee asks whether the recall has affected any pending Apex deals in the pipeline, worried about a large Denver-area contract. He notes this is separate from the recall notification work and just wants a sales forecast read. No substantive detail about the coating issue itself, mostly a business-impact check-in.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Recall impact on Q3 pipeline
gist: Whitfield replies that the Denver contract negotiations continue and the hospital's purchasing team said the recall didn't change their overall Apex commitment since the affected lots represent a small fraction of total units, but she'll flag if that changes.

author: Dr. James Whitaker
subject: Question about the recalled cup lots
gist: Dr. Whitaker, a Denver surgeon, emails Whitfield asking for written confirmation of which specific lot numbers were recalled and whether the recall has any connection to complaints he's heard about elsewhere regarding higher revision rates on ApexHip generally. He references seeing coating flaking firsthand on one implant at his facility before it was used.
gray_rationale: The surgeon links the coating recall to broader revision-rate rumors, so a reviewer might read this as touching the separate wear/MDL issue rather than only the narrow recall, though the core ask is about recall scope.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Question about the recalled cup lots
gist: Whitfield replies with the specific lot range V-2200 through V-2299 and clarifies that this recall is limited to a coating adhesion issue identified during incoming inspection, distinct from any other clinical performance discussions, and offers to connect him with Dr. Adeyemi's office for further clinical questions.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Recall reconciliation summary - week 8
gist: Spreadsheet summary describing a table tracking recall reconciliation status by account: total units distributed 1,140, returned 812, confirmed implanted 412, remaining unaccounted 24 units traced to a distributor's transit inventory (Ibarra Surgical, Texas). Includes columns for account name, lot numbers, units on hand, units returned, and disposition date. Notes two effectiveness check calls still pending, including Northgate's second confirmation.

author: Sam Ibarra
subject: Transit inventory reconciliation - recalled lots
gist: Sam Ibarra of Ibarra Surgical writes that his warehouse found 24 units from lots V-2213 and V-2247 that were in transit when the recall notice went out; he confirms none were distributed further downstream to hospitals and asks for return shipping instructions and credit terms.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: trade show booth signage
gist: Casual Teams chat between Mendes and Shah about ordering new banner signage for an upcoming trade show booth, discussing booth layout and giveaway items. No mention of the recall or clinical performance; purely logistics.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Second effectiveness check round - Northgate follow-up
gist: Raman reports Northgate's second effectiveness check confirms all six affected units on hand were returned and that the hospital's risk management office has closed their internal tracking on the matter. She notes one implanted patient at Northgate is being monitored per routine post-op protocol but there is no indication of coating-related adverse event so far.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Status Review - Weekly Sync
gist: Recurring calendar invite for a weekly recall status review meeting, listing agenda bullets: reconciliation numbers, effectiveness check completion percentage, and CAPA closure timeline. No substantive content beyond meeting logistics and agenda topic labels.
gray_rationale: Pure scheduling with only topic-label agenda bullets naming the recall; a reviewer could treat the bare agenda topics as minimally responsive since they identify recall-specific tracking metrics.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR confirmation numbers logged
gist: Mitchell confirms the two MDRs tied to the recalled lot complaints (TW-2022-0611 and TW-2022-0618) have FDA confirmation numbers now logged in the regulatory tracker, and notes the recall status letter sent in July has not yet received an FDA compliance office response.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Chamber requalification complete
gist: Kowalski reports the plasma-spray chamber requalification protocol is complete, with adhesion pull-test results on the first three post-requalification lots (V-2310, V-2311, V-2312) all passing above the minimum bond strength threshold. He notes this data will support the CAPA effectiveness verification and asks Raman to include it in the closure package.

author: Owen Park
subject: Q3 close - recall-related cost tracking
gist: Park, CFO, asks Raman for an update on total costs incurred to date for the recall (returns processing, replacement units, shipping) to finalize the Q3 financial close, noting this is separate from the broader $18M reserve discussion happening elsewhere. Raman is asked to route the detailed number through Hannah Berg's team.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Southeast team offsite planning
gist: Whitfield asks Lee about venue options for the Southeast sales team's fall offsite, discussing hotel blocks and catering budget in Atlanta. Entirely scheduling and logistics, no mention of recall or product performance.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Closure Review Meeting Minutes
gist: Meeting minutes documenting a review of recall closure readiness: reconciliation stands at 1,116 of 1,140 units accounted for, remaining 24 units traced to Ibarra Surgical transit stock now returned per prior email, CAPA-2022-014 root cause and corrective actions reaffirmed as plasma-spray chamber requalification and revised maintenance SOP. Attendees discuss the pending FDA response to the July status letter and agree to send a follow-up letter if no response by mid-October. Action items assigned to Mitchell to draft the closure report and to Kowalski to finalize the CAPA effectiveness data package including the three passing post-requalification lots.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Cork corrective action plan - plasma spray parameter drift
gist: Kowalski provides a detailed corrective action plan for the KinetiCoat plasma-spray process following the June 14 recall of lots V-2200 through V-2299. He describes reinstating chamber maintenance verification steps, adding a post-maintenance test-coupon adhesion check before resuming production, and retraining line technicians. He references the root cause finding of parameter drift after the November 2021 chamber maintenance event and commits to a validation run before restarting cup production. Tone is operational and detailed, with reference to batch records and the chamber log.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Cork corrective action plan - plasma spray parameter drift
gist: Raman responds approving the corrective action plan and asks Kowalski to formalize it as a CAPA in TrackWise, requesting an effectiveness check protocol be included with acceptance criteria for coating adhesion testing on the first three production lots after restart. She notes this will support the recall effectiveness documentation required for the FDA file.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: CAPA-2022-0091 Plasma Spray Chamber Maintenance Verification
gist: A formal CAPA form documenting the corrective and preventive action for the KinetiCoat coating adhesion failures on cup lots V-2200-V-2299. Fields include problem description (coating flaking discovered at incoming inspection, Northgate Health System and a Denver hospital), root cause (plasma-spray parameter drift after Nov 2021 chamber maintenance), corrective action (revised maintenance verification checklist, post-maintenance coupon testing), and effectiveness check plan (adhesion testing on first three post-restart lots). Signed by Kowalski, reviewed by Raman.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA Recall Status Report - Z-1418-2022 due date
gist: Okonkwo reminds the team that the recall status report to FDA's Office of Compliance for recall number Z-1418-2022 is due in two weeks per 21 CFR 806.10 follow-up obligations. She asks Raman for updated numbers on units retrieved versus units still outstanding, and asks Mitchell to draft the cover letter referencing the June 14 recall initiation date and the 1,140 units distributed / 412 implanted figures already on file.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: FDA Recall Status Report - Z-1418-2022 due date
gist: Raman reports updated retrieval numbers: of 1,140 units distributed, 728 unimplanted units have been returned or accounted for, and of the 412 implanted units, hospitals have confirmed no removal is required per the surgeon notification letters since these are already-implanted patients being monitored rather than revised. She flags that three hospitals, including Northgate, have not yet returned their acknowledgment forms.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: FDA Recall Status Report - Z-1418-2022 due date
gist: Mitchell circulates a draft of the FDA recall status report cover letter referencing lot numbers V-2200 through V-2299, the June 14, 2022 recall initiation, and the updated retrieval figures Raman provided. He asks for sign-off before submission and notes the letter will go out under Okonkwo's signature.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Status Report - Z-1418-2022, ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200 through V-2299
gist: Formal letter to FDA's Office of Compliance providing the periodic status update on the voluntary Class II recall Z-1418-2022 for ApexHip acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured at the Cork facility between November 2021 and February 2022. States 1,140 units distributed, 412 implanted, 728 of the remaining units retrieved to date, and describes the root-cause corrective action (plasma-spray parameter drift, corrective maintenance verification protocol implemented). Commits to a follow-up report in 30 days.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Northgate acknowledgment form still outstanding
gist: Jenna asks Sarah and Mike to follow up in person with their Northgate and Denver hospital purchasing contacts to get the recall acknowledgment forms signed and returned, noting Priya's team needs them for the FDA report. She reminds them the recall is limited to cup lots V-2200-V-2299 and that reps should not speculate about other lots or about revision rates if asked, referring surgeons with broader questions to Dr. Adeyemi's office.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Northgate follow up
gist: Sarah reports back over Teams chat that Northgate's purchasing manager, a contact named Denise Whalen, signed the acknowledgment and returned it, confirming their remaining 14 unimplanted units were shipped back to Warsaw. She also mentions the Denver hospital contact is out until next week.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Recall retrieval tracking summary - lots V-2200 to V-2299
gist: A spreadsheet summary with a small table tracking retrieval status by hospital: Northgate Health System (44 units, 44 returned), Denver Medical Center (38 units, 30 returned, 8 outstanding), and eight other accounts with totals summing to the 1,140 distributed units. It notes 412 units remain implanted and are being tracked for adverse event monitoring rather than physical retrieval, and highlights that Denver's outstanding 8 units are the last open item before closing the retrieval phase.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Field messaging update - recall closing out
gist: Mendes sends an updated FAQ for reps as the recall retrieval nears completion, reiterating that the coating adhesion issue affecting lots V-2200-V-2299 was a manufacturing/process issue at Cork unrelated to the metal-ion discussions some surgeons have raised, and that reps should keep those topics separate when talking to customers. He asks Jenna and Marcus to distribute to their teams.
gray_rationale: The email explicitly ties recall messaging to distinguishing it from metal-ion complaint discussions, which touches complaint-handling framing even though its primary purpose is recall messaging.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Effectiveness Check Confirmation - ApexHip Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299
gist: Follow-up letter to Northgate's risk management office confirming their return of all 44 unimplanted units from the recalled lots and thanking them for completing the recall acknowledgment. It notes that Veridian's effectiveness check protocol is now complete for their account and provides a contact for any adverse events involving the four Northgate patients who received implants from the affected lots.

author: Priya Raman
subject: MDR trending question - recall-related complaints
gist: Raman asks Mitchell whether any of the incoming inspection complaints logged from the recalled lots need to be filed as MDRs, noting that the coating flaking was caught before implantation in most cases so no patient harm occurred, but two cases at the Denver hospital involved units that had already been opened in the OR before the flaking was noticed, which she thinks may trigger reportability review.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: MDR trending question - recall-related complaints
gist: Mitchell agrees the two Denver OR cases need individual review under 21 CFR 803.50 for reportability since the units were opened before the defect was caught, even though no implantation occurred. He asks Raman to pull the TrackWise complaint numbers for those two events and says he will draft MDR forms for Okonkwo's review this week.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: validation run results
gist: Kowalski reports via Teams chat that the validation run of three lots after the chamber maintenance verification protocol was implemented passed adhesion coupon testing, with all coupons meeting the pull-test threshold. He says the line is cleared to resume normal ApexHip cup production and asks if Raman wants a copy of the coupon test data for the CAPA file.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Recall closure review - 30 min
gist: Calendar invite for a short internal meeting to review whether the recall retrieval and effectiveness check documentation is complete enough to submit the closure request to FDA. No substantive content beyond the meeting purpose line and standard agenda placeholder.
gray_rationale: Pure scheduling for a recall-related meeting with essentially no substantive content beyond the topic name, borderline whether the meeting title itself counts as responsive.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Recall closure review meeting minutes
gist: Minutes recording that the team reviewed retrieval status (1,072 of 1,140 units now accounted for), the completed CAPA-2022-0091 validation run, and the two Denver MDR filings now submitted to FDA under numbers pending assignment. The group agreed the file is ready to submit a closure request once the final 12 outstanding units from two small accounts are resolved, targeted for October. Action items assigned to Mitchell to prepare the closure letter draft.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Dr. Whitaker's office called about the recall
gist: Sarah relays that Dr. Whitaker's office in Denver called asking whether the recall notice they received applies to any patients they've already treated, since Whitaker has been vocal about revisions lately. Sarah asks Jenna how to respond without overstepping into clinical territory, noting the two units in question were from lot V-2251 which is within the recalled range.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Dr. Whitaker's office called about the recall
gist: Jenna tells Sarah to direct Dr. Whitaker's office to Dana Okonkwo's team for the formal recall notice details and confirms lot V-2251 is within the affected range V-2200-V-2299. She cc's Mendes for visibility and notes Whitaker has separately raised revision concerns that are a different issue Sarah should not conflate with the recall when speaking to the office.
gray_rationale: The email references Dr. Whitaker's separate revision concerns in the context of coaching a rep, which brushes against complaint/adverse event topics even though the main thrust is recall scope.

author: Owen Park
subject: Recall retrieval costs for Q3 close
gist: Park asks for a final tally of costs associated with the recall retrieval effort (shipping, replacement units, hospital reimbursement) so finance can true up the Q3 accrual against the $18M reserve booked earlier in the year. He notes this is separate from ongoing legal reserve estimates being tracked by Steinberg's office.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Recall retrieval costs for Q3 close
gist: Raman provides a rough figure of $340,000 in retrieval and replacement costs to date, noting most of the 1,140 distributed units have now been accounted for except a handful of small accounts. She says the CAPA and effectiveness check documentation is nearly ready for FDA closure submission.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: quota check-in
gist: Casual Teams chat between Mike and Sarah comparing quarterly quota numbers and complaining about the Nashville territory being harder this quarter, with no mention of the recall or any product issues; ends with plans to grab drinks at the regional meeting next month.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Draft recall closure letter for review
gist: Mitchell attaches a draft closure letter to FDA for recall Z-1418-2022, stating that all but 6 units of the original 1,140 distributed have now been retrieved or accounted for, that CAPA-2022-0091's effectiveness check passed on three post-remediation lots, and requesting FDA concur that the recall can be classified as terminated. Buried in the last paragraph he flags one open MDR filing tied to the earlier Denver OR cases that is still pending FDA acknowledgment.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Draft recall closure letter for review
gist: Okonkwo approves the draft with minor edits and instructs Mitchell to hold submission until the pending MDR from the Denver OR cases receives an FDA acknowledgment number, so the closure letter can reference it correctly.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Closure Request - Z-1418-2022, ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299
gist: Formal closure request letter stating all but a small number of units from the 1,140 distributed under recall Z-1418-2022 have been retrieved, corrective action CAPA-2022-0091 effectiveness checks passed, and the two related MDR reports (filed for the Denver OR cases) have been acknowledged by FDA. Requests the agency terminate the recall status. Signed by Okonkwo, references lot range V-2200 through V-2299 and original recall date of June 14, 2022.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: chamber maintenance schedule going forward
gist: Kowalski asks whether the new post-maintenance coupon testing step should become a permanent part of the standard operating procedure for the plasma-spray chamber, not just for this CAPA, so future maintenance events don't risk a repeat of the parameter drift issue. Raman replies she will raise it with the CAPA board for a permanent SOP change.

author: Facilities
subject: Parking lot repaving - west lot closed next week
gist: Facilities announces the west parking lot at the Hub will be closed for repaving from October 31 through November 4, and directs staff to use the visitor lot or overflow lot C during that time. No connection to any product or quality topic.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Recall Effectiveness Check - Round 2 Summary (Z-1418-2022)
gist: Formal effectiveness check report for FDA recall Z-1418-2022 covering lots V-2200-V-2299. Reports that Round 2 verification reached 96% of the 1,140 distributed units (1,094 accounted for), with 412 confirmed implanted and 682 returned or destroyed; 46 units remain untraced, mostly at two small ambulatory surgical centers. Recommends continued follow-up letters to the 46 outstanding accounts and notes root cause (plasma-spray parameter drift after chamber maintenance) is documented in CAPA-2022-0091. Tone is procedural, citing 21 CFR 806 recall recordkeeping requirements.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Recall Effectiveness Check - Round 2 Summary (Z-1418-2022)
gist: Dana acknowledges the Round 2 report, asks Devon to draft the quarterly recall status update for FDA per the recall strategy, and reminds Bill that Cork must retain the chamber maintenance logs from Nov 2021-Feb 2022 in case of a follow-up inspection. Confirms the 46 untraced units will be closed out by end of Q4 2022. Direct and procedural.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Final Field Action Notice - ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200 through V-2299
gist: Formal closing letter to Northgate Health System confirming the recall of ApexHip cup lots V-2200-V-2299 is complete for their facility, thanking them for their cooperation returning 18 unimplanted units, and confirming no further action is needed unless additional stock is located. References FDA recall number Z-1418-2022 and provides a Veridian contact (Priya Raman, Quality) for questions.

author: Dr. James Whitaker
subject: Frustrated with ApexHip revisions - separate from the coating recall?
gist: Dr. Whitaker in Denver writes to Jenna expressing frustration that he has now seen four ApexHip revisions in his practice this year for what looks like metal wear and pseudotumor formation, not coating flaking, and asks pointedly whether Veridian is tracking this as a distinct issue from the cup lot recall. He references a patient with elevated cobalt levels needing revision surgery. Tone is irritated and clinical.
gray_rationale: He references the recall by contrast but the substance is about the separate metal-ion issue, so a reviewer might code this only under the metal-ion RFP rather than the recall RFP.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: FW: Frustrated with ApexHip revisions - separate from the coating recall?
gist: Jenna forwards Dr. Whitaker's email to Priya and Marcus, asking how she should respond and flagging that he seems ready to file a formal complaint. She notes he is not a paid consultant so this could become public criticism. Asks whether the four revisions have been logged in TrackWise yet.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Frustrated with ApexHip revisions - separate from the coating recall?
gist: Priya replies that none of Dr. Whitaker's four cases involve cup lots V-2200-V-2299 so they are unrelated to the coating recall, and that she has opened new TrackWise complaints (TW-2022-1187 through TW-2022-1190) for the metal-ion revisions. She reminds the team that Whitaker's cases should be tracked toward MDR reportability review under 21 CFR 803 given the revision surgeries.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Cork line - chamber 3 recert
gist: Bill tells Priya that chamber 3, the plasma-spray unit implicated in the V-2200-V-2299 drift, has completed its full IQ/OQ/PQ recertification and passed all coating adhesion tests at the new tighter parameter tolerances established after the recall. He mentions the recert report will go into the CAPA-2022-0091 file. Short, operational, some Irish plant phrasing about

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Cork line - chamber 3 recert
gist: Priya confirms she'll close CAPA-2022-0091 pending final sign-off from Dana Okonkwo and asks Bill to send the recert report file name so she can attach it to the recall closure package for FDA.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Recall Closure Review - Z-1418-2022
gist: Calendar invite for a 30-minute internal meeting to review final recall closure documentation before submission to FDA. No substantive content beyond meeting logistics and attendee list.
gray_rationale: Purely scheduling for a recall-related meeting with no substance, but a reviewer could argue the subject line itself ties it to the recall filing.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Closure Memorandum - Z-1418-2022, ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299
gist: Formal internal memo documenting final closure of the recall: 1,140 units distributed, 412 implanted, 728 recovered or accounted for through returns and destruction, effectiveness rate 98.6% after final reconciliation. States root cause was plasma-spray parameter drift following an October 2021 chamber maintenance event at the Cork facility, corrective action was chamber 3 recertification and tightened process controls, and CAPA-2022-0091 is now closed. Recommends notifying FDA District Office of closure and archiving the DHF-linked recall file. References 21 CFR 806.20 recordkeeping.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Recall Closure Notification - Recall Number Z-1418-2022
gist: Formal letter to FDA's Office of Compliance requesting closure of recall Z-1418-2022, summarizing the final reconciliation figures (1,140 distributed, 728 recovered, 412 implanted, effectiveness 98.6%), the corrective actions taken at Cork (chamber 3 recertification, tightened plasma-spray parameters), and confirming completion of all planned effectiveness checks. Signed by Dana as VP Regulatory Affairs.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Surgeon at Piedmont still asking about the 2022 recall
gist: Sarah writes that a surgeon at a Piedmont-area hospital, restocking ApexHip inventory, asked whether the 2022 coating recall on cup lots V-2200-V-2299 is fully resolved and whether current inventory is affected. Sarah wants a confirmed talking point that current stock is unaffected since it postdates the impacted lot range.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Surgeon at Piedmont still asking about the 2022 recall
gist: Jenna loops in Priya to confirm the exact language reps should use, and reminds Sarah that the recall was specifically limited to cup lots manufactured Nov 2021-Feb 2022 at Cork and does not affect current production, which uses the recertified chamber 3 process.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Surgeon at Piedmont still asking about the 2022 recall
gist: Priya confirms the approved talking point language and attaches a reference sheet listing the affected lot range V-2200-V-2299, states recall Z-1418-2022 is fully closed as of Nov 2022, and reminds reps not to discuss the separate ongoing metal-ion complaint tracking with customers without RA approval.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: Nashville hospital pulling old ApexHip stock
gist: Mike mentions a Nashville hospital found two old ApexHip boxes in a supply closet during inventory and asks whether they need to check the lot numbers against the 2022 recall list before using them. Casual chat tone.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Nashville hospital pulling old ApexHip stock
gist: Jenna tells Mike to send her the lot numbers and she'll cross-check against the V-2200-V-2299 recall range with Priya before the hospital uses them, standard caution.

author: Owen Park
subject: Reserve true-up - recall-related costs vs. litigation reserve
gist: Owen asks Rachel and Dana to help him separate, for the Q1 close, the direct costs of the 2022 coating recall (product replacement, logistics, effectiveness check labor, roughly $2.1M total) from the broader $18M litigation reserve booked for Apex-related metal-ion claims, since the first state-court suits were just filed. Wants clean categorization for the auditors.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Reserve true-up - recall-related costs vs. litigation reserve
gist: Dana confirms the recall closure file (Z-1418-2022) shows final direct costs of approximately $2.08M and reiterates that the coating/manufacturing recall is legally and factually distinct from the metal-ion wear issue driving the new lawsuits, though she cautions that plaintiffs' counsel may try to conflate the two.

author: Elena Ruiz
subject: Discovery request re: 2022 ApexHip recall documentation
gist: Outside counsel Elena Ruiz at Whitfield & Barr writes that plaintiffs' counsel in the newly filed state suits have requested all documents related to the 2022 cup coating recall, including root-cause investigation, CAPA-2022-0091, and effectiveness check reports, and asks Dana to confirm the recall file is complete and litigation-hold compliant.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Discovery request re: 2022 ApexHip recall documentation
gist: Dana confirms the full recall file, including the closure memo, effectiveness check rounds 1 and 2, the FDA closure letter, and CAPA-2022-0091 records, is preserved under the litigation hold in place since Feb 2022 and offers to compile it for production.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Q3 sales push - ApexHip messaging
gist: Marcus pushes the sales team for a strong Q3 with ApexHip and KneeFlex bundling promotions, mentions new territory incentives, no mention of the recall or complaints. Purely commercial cheerleading email unrelated to recall or complaint topics.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Complaint Investigation Form - TW-2023-0552
gist: TrackWise complaint form for a patient revision at a Dallas hospital involving ApexHip cup lot V-3105 (outside the recalled range) showing elevated serum cobalt and suspected ARMD, unrelated to the coating recall. Investigation section notes the lot passed all incoming coating adhesion checks and the failure mode appears consistent with the known metal-ion wear pattern rather than coating adhesion. MDR reportability assessment pending.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Annual recall file archive reminder
gist: Devon reminds Dana that per the RA document retention schedule, the Z-1418-2022 recall file (closed Nov 2022) should be moved to long-term archive storage in Agile, but flags it should remain readily retrievable given ongoing litigation hold obligations tied to the MDL formation expected later in the year.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: MDL 3102 formed - preservation reminder, recall file included
gist: Rachel notifies the group that MDL 3102 has formally been established in the Northern District of Indiana consolidating the ApexHip metal-ion cases, and reminds everyone that all documents related to both the metal-ion issue and the 2022 coating recall (Z-1418-2022, lots V-2200-V-2299) must remain under litigation hold since plaintiffs may seek both categories in discovery, even though the company maintains they are factually distinct issues.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: Cork audit - recall file requested by Investigator Delgado follow-up
gist: Bill mentions that during a routine Cork facility audit prep, someone asked whether Investigator Delgado (FDA) might request the 2022 recall file again given the upcoming market withdrawal announcement, and whether they should proactively refresh the batch records index for chamber 3 covering Nov 2021 to Feb 2022.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Market withdrawal - does this reopen the 2022 recall question?
gist: Following the Feb 2 announcement of ApexHip's voluntary market withdrawal, Priya asks Dana whether the closed 2022 coating recall needs to be referenced in the withdrawal communications, since some customers may confuse the two events; she notes the withdrawal is driven by the metal-ion/registry signal, not coating adhesion, and recommends the customer letter clearly distinguish the two to avoid confusion. The responsive distinction appears in the middle of her message after a paragraph about withdrawal logistics.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: customers confusing withdrawal with the old recall
gist: Sarah tells Jenna that two hospital purchasing contacts asked if the market withdrawal is 'the same recall from 2022,' and she wants a clear one-line answer distinguishing the coating recall (closed, lots V-2200-V-2299) from the current withdrawal (metal-ion related, all ApexHip systems).

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: customers confusing withdrawal with the old recall
gist: Jenna gives Sarah the approved distinguishing language and says Priya's team is fielding similar questions company-wide; short reply confirming the two events are unrelated on paper even though customers keep conflating them.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Complaint Intake Form - Patient JD, Atlanta Joint Institute
gist: TrackWise intake form TW-2018-0311 logs a complaint from Dr. Marcus Feld's practice: 61-year-old male patient implanted with ApexHip cup lot V-2041, stem S-7118, presenting with hip pain and elevated cobalt levels (18.2 ppb) at 14-month follow-up. Reporter is Sarah Kim relaying info from clinic nurse. Fields include device identification, event description, and preliminary MDR-reportability checkbox left blank pending review. This is the first of three similar reports from the same practice that month.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Complaint Intake Form - Patient RT, Atlanta Joint Institute
gist: Second TrackWise complaint form (TW-2018-0322) from the same Atlanta practice, another ApexHip patient with cup lot V-2044 showing cobalt 22.4 ppb and swelling; nurse reported metallosis suspected on imaging. Kim notes this is the second call this month from Dr. Feld's office about similar symptoms. Form fields largely mirror the first, device info and event narrative at top.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Two complaints from Dr. Feld's office this month
gist: Kim flags to Raman that she has now submitted two TrackWise forms (TW-2018-0311, TW-2018-0322) from Feld's Atlanta practice within a week, both involving elevated cobalt and hip pain, and asks whether this is something Raman is tracking or whether it warrants escalation. Tone is mildly concerned but deferential; top of email states the pattern plainly.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Two complaints from Dr. Feld's office this month
gist: Raman replies that Quality is aware and logging each complaint per procedure, thanks Kim for flagging, and says two complaints in a short window from one practice will be reviewed but is not yet a statistical signal; she notes she'll loop in Greg Novak if a third comes in. Reply is short and reassuring, quoted history below shows Kim's original concern.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Complaint Intake Form - Patient MK, Atlanta Joint Institute
gist: Third TrackWise complaint (TW-2018-0340) from Dr. Feld's practice this month: patient with cup lot V-2039 and head H-3087, cobalt 25.1 ppb, pain and effusion, surgeon recommending revision surgery evaluation. Form notes this completes a cluster of three ApexHip metal-ion complaints from the same clinic in August 2018.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Third Atlanta complaint - possible cluster
gist: Raman writes to Novak that a third metal-ion complaint has come in from Dr. Feld's Atlanta practice within one month (TW-2018-0311, 0322, 0340), all involving elevated cobalt and pain, and asks him to check whether this rises above baseline complaint rate for ApexHip cups from that lot range. She provides the three TrackWise IDs and cobalt values in the body.

author: Greg Novak
subject: RE: Third Atlanta complaint - possible cluster
gist: Novak responds with a preliminary look at complaint trending, noting the three Atlanta complaints are within statistical noise for now but he will run a formal quarterly trend analysis and cc's Okonkwo since MDR reportability review may be needed if cobalt levels are confirmed elevated on repeat testing. He references the current complaint rate of roughly 0.3% and says he'll flag if it moves.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: MDR reportability - Atlanta cobalt complaints
gist: Okonkwo asks Raman to walk through the MDR decision tree under 21 CFR 803.50 for the three August Atlanta complaints, specifically whether elevated cobalt with symptomatic pain meets the malfunction/serious injury threshold requiring reporting to FDA within 30 days. She wants a documented rationale either way for each TrackWise record.

author: Priya Raman
subject: MDR Reportability Assessment - TW-2018-0311, 0322, 0340
gist: Formal memo walking through the MDR decision tree for the three August 2018 Atlanta complaints. Concludes two of three (0322 and 0340) meet criteria for reportable events due to documented metallosis findings and physician-recommended revision, while 0311 is held pending additional cobalt retest data. Memo cites 21 CFR 803.50, lists device lots V-2039, V-2041, V-2044, and recommends Devon Mitchell prepare draft MDR submissions.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: MDR Reportability Assessment - TW-2018-0311, 0322, 0340
gist: Mitchell confirms he will draft the two MDR submissions identified in Raman's memo and asks for confirmation on the implant dates to calculate the 30-day reporting clock; he notes one submission is already close to the deadline and will prioritize it. Email is short, top-level content is the reporting deadline concern.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Atlanta cluster
gist: Teams chat where Kim tells Whitfield that Dr. Feld's office has now had three ApexHip patients with elevated cobalt this quarter and asks if Jenna has heard anything similar from other Southeast accounts. Whitfield says she hasn't heard of others yet but will ask reps at the next regional call. Casual tone, short exchange.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Atlanta cluster
gist: Whitfield asks Kim to keep her posted and mentions she is heading to Nashville next week to see Dr. Rao's team about the fall speaker series - purely scheduling, no substance about complaints. Hard negative continuation of the chat thread that pivots to unrelated travel logistics.

author: Dr. Marcus Feld
subject: Concerns regarding ApexHip metal ion levels in my patients
gist: Formal letter from Dr. Feld describing three patients in his practice with elevated serum cobalt (18-25 ppb range) and symptomatic pain following ApexHip implantation, requesting Veridian investigate whether specific lots (V-2039, V-2041, V-2044) or a broader design issue is responsible, and offering explant tissue samples for analysis. Tone is professional but pointed, noting his role as design consultant makes this concerning to him personally.

author: Priya Raman
subject: FW: Concerns regarding ApexHip metal ion levels in my patients
gist: Raman forwards Feld's letter to Okonkwo and Novak, noting his offer to provide explant tissue samples is valuable and asking whether Regulatory wants to coordinate a formal response referencing the open MDR submissions. Top message is brief; the substantive complaint detail is in the quoted letter below.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Concerns regarding ApexHip metal ion levels in my patients
gist: Okonkwo says Regulatory will draft a response to Feld acknowledging the complaints, confirming MDR filings are in progress, and accepting the explant tissue offer for internal engineering review; she cc's Halvorsen separately for lab coordination. She notes the response should not commit to conclusions about design causation, only process.

author: Greg Novak
subject: Q3 2018 complaint trend summary - ApexHip
gist: Novak's quarterly trending email states that ApexHip metal-ion related complaints rose from a baseline of roughly 0.3% to 0.6% of implants in Q3 2018, driven substantially by the Atlanta cluster, and that this is the first quarter showing a statistically noticeable uptick though still within historical noise bands for orthopedic MoM devices. He recommends continued monitoring and a follow-up review in Q4. Numbers and analysis are the substance of the email.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Q3 2018 complaint trend summary - ApexHip
gist: Raman thanks Novak and asks him to include the Atlanta cluster detail specifically in the next PMS report so Regulatory can reference it if FDA asks about trending; she also asks about a scheduling conflict for their weekly Quality sync next Tuesday, purely logistical addendum.

author: Greg Novak
subject: ApexHip complaint rate by lot and region - Q3 2018
gist: Spreadsheet summary table breaking down Q3 2018 ApexHip complaints by lot number and sales region: cup lots V-2039, V-2041, V-2044 (all Atlanta, Cork manufacture window mid-2017) show 3 complaints against roughly 210 units sold in that period, a complaint rate of 1.4% versus 0.3% company average across all lots; other regions show no elevated rate. Narrative notes this could reflect surgical technique, patient population, or a lot-specific issue and recommends engineering review of those specific lots.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Explant samples from Dr. Feld - engineering review requested
gist: Raman writes Halvorsen that Quality has received tissue and explant samples from Dr. Feld's three Atlanta patients and asks whether his team can examine wear patterns on the retrieved cup and head components to help determine if edge-loading or coating wear is implicated. She references the cobalt levels reported (18-25 ppb) and TrackWise IDs for context at the top.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: RE: Explant samples from Dr. Feld - engineering review requested
gist: Halvorsen replies that he's received the explants and initial visual inspection shows scratching consistent with edge loading on two of the three heads, which is concerning given the standard wear testing only validated 45 degree inclination; he says he wants to compare against the 2019 planned re-test protocol once samples are fully analyzed. This response foreshadows his later 2019 wear-test findings and sits at the bottom of the thread.
gray_rationale: Mentions edge-loading wear concern tied to a future re-test but does not itself present registry or design-history trend data, so reasonable reviewers could differ on whether it belongs with the design/registry signal thread versus purely the complaint file.

author: Priya Raman
subject: ApexHip Atlanta cluster review meeting
gist: Calendar invite for a one-hour meeting to review the Atlanta metal-ion complaint cluster, explant findings, and MDR status; agenda line lists 'TW-2018-0311/0322/0340 review, explant results, next steps'. Purely scheduling with a brief agenda line, no analysis contained.
gray_rationale: It is only a scheduling invite for a substantive meeting; a strict reviewer might treat pure logistics as non-responsive, but the agenda line naming specific complaint IDs makes it arguably responsive.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Minutes - ApexHip Atlanta Cluster Review, 2018-11-05
gist: Meeting minutes documenting discussion of the three Atlanta complaints, Halvorsen's preliminary explant finding of edge-loading wear on two of three retrieved heads, Novak's Q3 trend data showing 1.4% complaint rate in affected lots versus 0.3% baseline, and Okonkwo's confirmation that two MDRs have been filed with FDA. Action items: Halvorsen to complete formal wear analysis by Q1 2019, Novak to continue Q4 trending, Raman to monitor for additional Atlanta-area complaints. Attendees and action items listed at bottom.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: Question from Dr. Rao's office
gist: Ruiz emails Whitfield relaying that a nurse at Dr. Rao's Nashville practice asked whether Veridian has seen any issues with ApexHip and metal ions, since she saw something online; Ruiz says he didn't know what to tell her and asks how to respond. This is early evidence of field awareness spreading beyond Atlanta, top of email is the direct question.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Question from Dr. Rao's office
gist: Whitfield tells Ruiz to direct clinical questions to Medical Affairs rather than answering himself, and cc's Mendes asking if there's an approved talking point yet for metal ion questions from surgeons' offices; she notes she's aware of the Atlanta complaints internally but reps shouldn't speculate. Substance is at top of reply.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Question from Dr. Rao's office
gist: Mendes replies that Regulatory and Medical Affairs are working on standard guidance for handling metal-ion inquiries from clinics but nothing is finalized yet, and in the meantime reps should refer questions to their regional sales manager, not discuss specific complaint numbers. He mentions the fall sales conference logistics briefly at the end, which is unrelated scheduling detail.

author: Priya Raman
subject: November complaint count
gist: Quick Teams chat where Raman tells Okonkwo that November brought two more ApexHip metal-ion complaints, one from Atlanta and one new one from a Denver surgeon (Dr. Whitaker), bringing the running Q4 count to concerning levels; Okonkwo asks her to make sure both are logged for the MDR decision tree and to loop Novak in for the Q4 trend report.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Holiday party details - Southeast team
gist: Whitfield sends logistics for the Southeast regional holiday party, venue, dress code, and RSVP deadline; purely social, no product content. Hard negative from the same people and week as the complaint discussions but unrelated topic.

author: Greg Novak
subject: Q4 2018 complaint trend preview - ApexHip metal ion
gist: Novak's preview email states Q4 is trending toward 0.7% complaint rate for metal-ion related ApexHip events, now with cases in Atlanta, Nashville area, and Denver, and that the geographic spread suggests this may not be an isolated regional or surgical-technique issue; he says the formal report will follow in January and recommends Regulatory consider whether cumulative trending crosses any reporting threshold. Substance is in the body, not buried.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA Additional Information request - MDR trending
gist: Dana forwards the FDA's Additional Information request received following a routine MDR trending review, noting the agency wants a written explanation of the rising complaint rate for ApexHip metal-ion related revisions logged since 2018, including TrackWise entries TW-2018-0932 through TW-2019-0301. She asks Devon to compile a response draft citing 21 CFR 803 trending obligations and asks Priya to pull the underlying complaint counts by quarter. Tone is precise and businesslike, with a numbered list of deliverables and a due date of May 20.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: FDA Additional Information request - MDR trending
gist: Priya replies with a quarterly breakdown: Q3 2018 (3 complaints, Atlanta cluster, Dr. Feld's practice), Q4 2018 (5), Q1 2019 (9), noting the increase correlates with revision surgeries citing elevated cobalt/chromium serum levels and early loosening. She flags that several complaint records lack complete explant photos and recommends closing the gap before the FDA response goes out. She signs off per procedure per TrackWise SOP-220.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: FDA Additional Information request - MDR trending
gist: Devon circulates a draft FDA response letter summarizing the trending data and attributing part of the increase to improved reporting awareness among surgeons rather than a device defect, referencing the March 2021 NJR data as forward-looking context is not yet available so instead cites internal complaint volumes only. He asks for sign-off before the May 20 deadline. The substantive complaint trend content is buried in the second paragraph after boilerplate scheduling language about a call.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: wear test vs complaints
gist: Tom messages Priya on Teams noting his February 2019 re-run of wear testing at 55 degrees inclination showed 4-6x higher wear than the 45-degree standard test, and asks if the Atlanta complaint cluster patients' cup positioning angles have been checked against this. Priya responds that complaint intake forms don't currently capture inclination angle and she'll raise it with Greg Novak. Short exchange, engineer-to-quality tone.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: wear test vs complaints
gist: Priya continues the chat saying she'll ask hospitals for post-op x-rays where available to estimate cup angle retroactively, but warns this will be slow and incomplete. She mentions TW-2019-0417 as the lead complaint file for this effort. Tone is cautious, slightly defensive about resourcing.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Complaint intake form TW-2019-0512
gist: Standard TrackWise complaint intake form filed by sales rep Sarah Kim on behalf of Northgate Health System surgeon reporting a patient with elevated serum cobalt (32 ug/L) and chromium (18 ug/L) 22 months post-implant with ApexHip cup lot V-1987, head lot H-3021. Fields include patient age (58), symptom (groin pain, effusion), and recommendation for revision surgery pending imaging. Notes field states surgeon suspects metal-on-metal wear as cause.

author: Priya Raman
subject: New complaint TW-2019-0512 - elevated Co/Cr, lot V-1987
gist: Priya forwards the intake form to Greg asking whether V-1987 batches show any coating or metallurgy anomalies in his registry dataset, and whether this fits the pattern he's tracking for MDR trending purposes. She notes this is now the 14th metal-ion related complaint logged since the 2018 Atlanta cluster began.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Quarterly Complaint Trending Summary - ApexHip Q2 2019
gist: Formal quality memo summarizing ApexHip complaints for Q2 2019: 11 total complaints, 7 related to elevated metal ion levels and early revision, up from 5 in Q1. Memo includes a small table by region (Southeast 6, Northeast 2, Midwest 3) and notes the majority trace to surgeries performed 2017-2018. Concludes that while individual complaints do not meet MDR reportability thresholds under 21 CFR 803.50 on their own, the trend warrants continued monitoring and possible escalation to a formal CAPA. Recommends coordination with Design Engineering on the 55-degree wear finding.

author: Dr. Anita Rao
subject: Concerning revision case
gist: Dr. Rao writes to Marcus and Carlos describing a revision she performed on a 61-year-old patient implanted with ApexHip in 2017, finding significant metallosis and a pseudotumor at the joint capsule; she asks whether the company is seeing similar cases elsewhere and whether there's guidance on managing patient serum ion testing. Tone is professional but pointed, an early sign of her later skepticism.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Concerning revision case
gist: Carlos replies diplomatically, thanking Dr. Rao for flagging the case, saying he'll loop in Quality and Regulatory to log it formally, and reassures her that ApexHip's overall complication rate remains within expected ranges per current data. He does not mention the 55-degree wear finding. Marketing-speak tone, avoids commitment.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: RE: Concerning revision case
gist: Marcus, cc removed from Rao, tells Carlos privately not to let this slow down the Nashville territory push, saying Rao is an important KOL and they should handle her concerns carefully but keep pushing volume. Short, pushy tone with exclamation points.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Complaint trend review - ApexHip
gist: Calendar invite for a 45-minute meeting to review ApexHip complaint trend data and the 55-degree wear test findings together for the first time, scheduling logistics only, no substantive content in the invite body beyond agenda bullet titles.
gray_rationale: Pure scheduling logistics for a substantive meeting; some reviewers might code as responsive because agenda bullets name the covered topics.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Minutes - ApexHip Complaint Trend Review
gist: Meeting minutes documenting discussion of 16 metal-ion related complaints logged since August 2018, the 55-degree wear test finding shared by Tom showing 4-6x wear increase at higher inclination, and Greg's note that early AJRR submissions (not yet full registry data) hint at above-average revision reporting for ApexHip. Action items: Priya to add cup inclination angle field to complaint intake form; Dana to assess MDR reportability of the aggregate trend; Tom to draft a design change proposal. No decision reached on halting sales.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: ECO-2019-118 draft - cup design change proposal
gist: Tom shares a draft engineering change order proposing a redesign of the acetabular cup geometry to reduce edge-loading risk at high inclination angles, citing the wear test data and referencing the growing complaint count as motivation. He notes the change would require re-validation and estimates 9-12 months before implementation, and flags that leadership may want to weigh cost against continuing to monitor complaints. Attachment named ECO-2019-118_draft.pdf.

author: Dr. Marcus Feld
subject: Two more revisions this month
gist: Dr. Feld emails Carlos reporting two additional ApexHip revisions in his Atlanta practice in January alone, both showing elevated cobalt levels and soft tissue reaction, and asks pointedly whether Veridian is tracking a broader pattern given his prior cases from 2018. He references his consulting relationship and says he wants to be able to reassure his patients but needs real data.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: FW: Two more revisions this month
gist: Carlos forwards Feld's email up the chain asking Priya and Dana how to respond, noting Feld is a key opinion leader and paid consultant so the response needs care. Priya's later reply (same thread continuing) confirms these two cases have been logged as TW-2020-0033 and TW-2020-0041, bringing the cumulative Southeast metal-ion complaint count to 21.

author: Priya Raman
subject: ApexHip complaint log summary - through Jan 2020
gist: Spreadsheet summary describing a running complaint log with columns for TrackWise ID, region, implant date, revision date, and reported cause. Text summary states cumulative metal-ion related complaints now total 29 since August 2018, with the Southeast region (Feld and other Atlanta surgeons) accounting for 14 of those. A small table breaks counts down by quarter showing steady increase each period. Priya notes the aggregate trend approaches a threshold that Dana previously flagged for MDR reportability review.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: MDR reportability assessment - aggregate metal-ion trend
gist: Dana writes a formal assessment concluding that while individual complaints remain below single-event MDR thresholds, the aggregate trend of 29 cases may warrant a trend-based MDR filing under 21 CFR 803.50(b), and asks Devon to prepare a draft for her review with Priya's data attached. She cites the 2021 FDA inspection risk of being cited again for trending timeliness (referencing the prior 2019 AI request) as a reason to act proactively.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: nashville surgeon question
gist: Mike messages Jenna saying a Nashville surgeon asked him point blank if there have been more ApexHip revisions than usual, and he didn't know what to say. Jenna tells him to refer clinical questions to Carlos or the medical affairs team and not to speculate. No specific complaint data shared, mostly about how to handle the conversation.
gray_rationale: Touches on awareness of a revision trend but no substantive data disclosed, mostly a communications-handling exchange.

author: Greg Novak
subject: Early AJRR pull vs internal complaints
gist: Greg shares an early informal pull of AJRR data suggesting ApexHip's revision rate trend is tracking higher than the class average, though the sample size is still small and not yet a formal registry report. He asks Priya whether the internal complaint counts correlate geographically, and Tom whether the ECO-2019-118 cup redesign has moved forward. He notes the correlation is concerning enough to mention at the next quality council meeting.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: RE: Early AJRR pull vs internal complaints
gist: Tom replies that ECO-2019-118 has been deferred by leadership pending a cost-benefit review, since a full redesign would require re-validation testing and could delay the KneeFlex Revision launch timeline; he expresses frustration that the wear data hasn't driven faster action, buried at the end of an otherwise routine status update about unrelated KneeFlex tooling issues.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Complaint handling capacity
gist: Priya requests an additional headcount in the complaint handling team, citing the growing ApexHip metal-ion complaint volume (now averaging 5-6 per month) alongside routine KneeFlex and ShoulderPro complaint intake, and worries about SLA compliance for MDR evaluation timeliness. The staffing ask is the main point; ApexHip complaint volume is cited as supporting context.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: quota check
