gist: Sarah and Mike chat about their quarterly sales quotas and an upcoming regional sales contest for ApexHip units sold, with no mention of complaints or clinical issues. Purely a hard negative about sales incentives and a dinner they're planning with reps from Dallas.

author: Nurse Coordinator, Northgate Health System
subject: Explant analysis request form - patient case #NG-2044
gist: Hospital form requesting Veridian retrieve and analyze an explanted ApexHip cup (lot V-2011) and head (lot H-3055) from a revision surgery, citing pre-op serum cobalt of 41 ug/L and visible tissue staining consistent with metallosis found intraoperatively. Requests root cause analysis and asks whether the lot has other reported issues.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Explant analysis request - NG-2044
gist: Priya forwards the explant request internally, confirming lot V-2011 has two prior complaints on file for similar metallosis presentation, and asks Greg whether this lot correlates with any coating or wear anomaly identified in his registry work. She notes the explant should be sent to Meridian Testing Labs for wear pattern analysis.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR filing summary - Q4 2020 ApexHip metal-ion cases
gist: Regulatory memo documenting six individual MDR filings submitted to FDA in Q4 2020 for ApexHip cases involving elevated metal ions and revision surgery, each cross-referenced to TrackWise IDs and summarizing symptom onset timing (average 26 months post-implant). Memo notes cumulative filed and pending MDRs for ApexHip metal-ion issues now total 19 since 2018, and flags that Dana's team is preparing to discuss this trend with the Registry Signal Review group later in the year given emerging NJR data expected in March.

author: Dr. James Whitaker
subject: Denver revision cluster
gist: Dr. Whitaker, not a paid consultant, writes bluntly to Marcus complaining he's now seen four ApexHip revisions in the past year with metallosis findings and demands to know if Veridian has data on this pattern, saying he may stop using the product. Marcus's reply (same email, below) is short and noncommittal, promising to escalate to Quality but privately telling Marcus's assistant this is a distraction from the KneeFlex Revision launch he's actually focused on this week.

author: Greg Novak
subject: NJR 2021 annual report - ApexHip 5-year revision rate
gist: Greg reports that the newly published NJR annual report shows ApexHip's 5-year revision rate at 7.1% compared to a 3.2% class average for comparable hip systems, and correlates this with the internal metal-ion complaint trend the team has tracked since 2018. He recommends this be escalated to a formal signal review meeting and cc's the group that a decision on continued marketing may be needed soon. This is the clearest tie yet between the registry data and the complaint history.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: NJR 2021 annual report - ApexHip 5-year revision rate
gist: Priya replies confirming the internal complaint database now shows 34 cumulative metal-ion related complaints and agreeing the registry data lines up geographically with the Southeast and Denver clusters. She suggests convening a cross-functional meeting before Q2 to decide next steps and mentions Dana is already discussing timing with Legal.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Quarterly complaint trend rollup - ApexHip cobalt/chromium
gist: Raman circulates the Q4 2019 complaint trending summary for ApexHip: 14 new metal-ion related complaints logged in TrackWise (TW-2019-0417 through TW-2019-0431), bringing rolling 12-month total to 41, up from 22 the prior year. She flags that Atlanta (Dr. Feld's practice) and Nashville (Dr. Rao's practice) account for over half the complaints. She asks Novak whether the rate increase tracks with any registry data yet and asks Mitchell whether an MDR reportability review is needed for the newest cluster of five cases with revision surgery.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Quarterly complaint trend rollup - ApexHip cobalt/chromium
gist: Mitchell replies that per 21 CFR 803.20 he is running the reportability decision tree on the five revision cases and expects at least three will require MDR filing within the 30-day window; he asks for explant analysis and serum ion levels for each case to attach to the MedWatch forms. He notes two of the five involve cup lots outside the eventual recall range, underscoring these are wear-related not coating-related.

author: Greg Novak
subject: RE: Quarterly complaint trend rollup - ApexHip cobalt/chromium
gist: Novak responds that AJRR public data lags but he has requested an early data pull; he notes internally that the complaint uptick is consistent with what NJR flagged in other MoM systems industry-wide, though ApexHip-specific NJR numbers won't be published until March 2021. He says he'll keep tracking and loop in Dr. Adeyemi if the trend continues.

author: Priya Raman
subject: TrackWise Complaint Record TW-2020-0088
gist: Complaint intake form for a 58-year-old patient at Nashville Hip & Knee (Dr. Rao) reporting hip pain, elevated serum cobalt at 12.3 ppb and chromium at 8.1 ppb, ultrasound showing suspected pseudotumor. Cup lot V-2087, head lot H-3021, implanted 2018-05. Fields include date of complaint, product codes, event description, initial risk assessment marked 'potential ARMD, revision recommended', and investigation status 'open - explant pending'.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Explant coming for TW-2020-0088
gist: Raman tells Mitchell the explant has been scheduled for TW-2020-0088 (the Rao patient with pseudotumor) and that once tissue and serum ion data come back she'll update the reportability assessment; she notes this is the third ARMD-flagged case tied to Dr. Rao's practice in six months.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: Dr. Rao asking hard questions
gist: Ruiz writes that Dr. Rao called him directly asking why she's seeing more revisions in her ApexHip patients than she used to and whether Veridian has seen a similar pattern elsewhere; he didn't know what to say and asks Jenna for guidance or talking points before he calls Rao back.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Dr. Rao asking hard questions
gist: Jenna tells Ruiz to avoid speculating and to forward any specific patient concerns to Quality (Priya Raman) so they get logged properly, rather than him fielding it informally; she says she'll ask Carlos Mendes if there's an approved response for surgeons asking about revision trends.

author: Priya Raman
subject: ApexHip Complaint Trending Report - H1 2020
gist: Formal memo summarizing 68 complaints logged Jan-June 2020, of which 31 relate to elevated metal ions or suspected ARMD, up from 19 in H1 2019. Breaks down by lot: no single lot dominates, consistent with a wear-related rather than manufacturing-related pattern. Notes 9 confirmed revisions with explant analysis showing surface wear scars consistent with edge loading at higher cup inclination angles, echoing the internal 2019 wear-test findings. Recommends continued monthly trend monitoring and states MDR filings are current for all reportable events. States legal has been informally briefed given the volume increase.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: ApexHip Complaint Trending Report - H1 2020
gist: Okonkwo acknowledges receipt of the H1 2020 trending memo and asks Novak to cross-check the edge-loading pattern against Tom Halvorsen's 2019 wear-test re-analysis at 55 degrees inclination, since the explant findings appear consistent with that internal data. She asks whether this warrants escalation beyond routine trending given the alignment with known design test results.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Teams - wear data vs complaints
gist: Halvorsen tells Raman in Teams that yes, the explant wear scar pattern from the June trending memo matches exactly what he saw in his 2019 55-degree retest, and that this isn't surprising to him given how many patients probably get implanted outside the 45-degree assumption used in the original ISO test protocol. He says it 'keeps him up at night' that the design change proposal from 2019 was deferred.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Teams - wear data vs complaints
gist: Raman replies she'll add his comment to the file but reminds him complaint causation determinations go through the CAPA process, not informal chat; she says she'll bring this up with Okonkwo and possibly Mendes since it touches design as well as quality.

author: Dr. James Whitaker
subject: Complaint letter regarding ApexHip revision surgery
gist: Denver surgeon Dr. Whitaker writes a formal complaint letter describing a patient who required early revision at 3 years post-implant, with serum cobalt of 18.7 ppb and extensive soft tissue necrosis found intraoperatively; he asks pointed questions about whether Veridian has other similar reports and whether there's a design issue with the cup at high inclination angles, referencing conversations he's had with colleagues.

author: Priya Raman
subject: FW: Complaint letter regarding ApexHip revision surgery
gist: Raman forwards Dr. Whitaker's letter to Okonkwo and Mitchell, noting this is logged as TW-2020-0201 and that Whitaker's direct question about a design issue at high inclination angles needs a careful, legally-reviewed response given it echoes the internal wear-test findings; she asks whether Rachel Steinberg should be looped in before any reply goes out.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR filing status update
gist: Mitchell provides a status list of MDR filings for Q3 2020: 12 MedWatch reports filed for ApexHip-related revisions, all within the 30-day timeliness window per 21 CFR 803.50; he notes two cases still pending explant pathology before final causation coding can be entered but interim reports were filed to preserve the deadline.

author: Greg Novak
subject: ApexHip complaint rate vs AJRR early data - 2020
gist: Novak's summary table compares Veridian's internal ApexHip complaint rate (metal-ion/ARMD subset) at roughly 0.9% of implanted units annualized against early unpublished AJRR revision signal data suggesting the class average is closer to 0.4%. He notes AJRR data has a longer lag than NJR and that the March 2021 NJR report is expected to give a clearer multi-year picture. He flags this comparison should be treated as preliminary and not shared externally.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Q1 territory targets and CME dinners
gist: Whitfield sends routine sales admin: Q1 territory targets, upcoming CME dinner logistics with Dr. Feld and Dr. Rao, and a reminder to submit Concur expense reports promptly. No mention of complaints or clinical issues.

author: Priya Raman
subject: ApexHip complaint trending - 2020 annual summary
gist: Raman's annual trending email states total 2020 ApexHip complaints reached 139, of which 61 were metal-ion/ARMD related, a continued year-over-year increase; she notes the Atlanta and Nashville clusters remain concentrated around Dr. Feld and Dr. Rao's practices respectively and that 22 MDRs were filed for the year. She recommends the trend be included in the upcoming quality management review and flags it for possible discussion with Dr. Adeyemi given the clinical pattern.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Teams - dinner reservation mixup
gist: Sarah and Mike chat about a dinner reservation mix-up at a steakhouse for an upcoming rep meeting, joking about the restaurant double-booking the 'reserve' room; purely logistical, no clinical or complaint content.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: NJR report just published - implications for complaint trending
gist: Okonkwo forwards the newly published March 2021 NJR annual report showing ApexHip's 5-year revision rate at 7.1% versus 3.2% class average and asks the team to reconcile this external data with the internal complaint trending numbers Raman has been tracking; she notes the internal metal-ion complaint rate increase over the past two years now appears consistent with the external registry signal, and asks for a joint summary to bring to Dr. Adeyemi and eventually leadership.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: NJR report just published - implications for complaint trending
gist: Raman confirms she'll pull together a combined complaint-trend and registry summary by end of week, noting the internal MDR count for 2020-2021 YTD now stands at 34 filed reports for ApexHip metal-ion related events, and that she wants to include Halvorsen's wear-test context since it explains the mechanism behind both signals.

author: Priya Raman
subject: TrackWise Complaint Record TW-2021-0055
gist: Complaint intake for a patient at Dr. Feld's practice, cup lot V-2054 (outside recall range), reporting hip swelling and elevated cobalt at 15.9 ppb; risk assessment section notes 'consistent with known metal-ion signal pattern', investigation status 'MDR filed 2021-04-20 per Mitchell review'.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: MDR trending question from FDA follow-up
gist: Mitchell notes that in responding to an earlier FDA request about MDR trending timeliness, he's been asked to also summarize the complaint volume growth pattern for ApexHip metal-ion events over 2019-2021; he asks Raman to send him the underlying monthly complaint counts so he can prepare an accurate chart for the regulatory file.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: MDR trending question from FDA follow-up
gist: Raman sends the monthly complaint count data (attached as Apex_complaint_trend_2019-2021.xlsx) showing steady increase from about 3-4 metal-ion complaints per month in early 2019 to 8-10 per month by early 2021, and reiterates that root cause remains wear-pattern related, not tied to the later coating recall lots.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Teams - registry data timing
gist: Raman asks Novak informally whether the AJRR fall data pull will be ready before the planned September registry signal discussion; Novak says likely yes but the NJR data is already the stronger signal since it's a full published report versus AJRR's still-lagging aggregate.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Q4 2020 complaint trend summary - ApexHip metal ion category
gist: Raman circulates the quarterly complaint trend summary showing metal-ion/pain/revision complaints for ApexHip climbing to 41 in Q4 2020 versus 22 in Q4 2019, cites TrackWise IDs TW-2020-1188 through TW-2020-1231, notes majority cluster still centered on Atlanta and now spreading to Nashville and Denver surgeons. She flags that the rate per 1000 units implanted has risen from 0.9 to 1.6 and asks Novak to cross-check against AJRR figures before the March board deck. Tone is careful, procedural, 'per procedure our trending threshold is a 20% quarter-over-quarter increase, which we have exceeded.'

author: Greg Novak
subject: RE: Q4 2020 complaint trend summary - ApexHip metal ion category
gist: Novak replies confirming the TrackWise numbers roughly track early AJRR signals he is compiling for the March registry report, mentions the 5-year revision rate calculation is still preliminary but 'directionally worse than the class average we cited to FDA in 2019.' He suggests looping in Dana Okonkwo given the MDR trending implications and proposes a call next week.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Q4 2020 complaint trend summary - ApexHip metal ion category
gist: Mitchell adds Okonkwo, notes he is drafting the 2021 annual MDR summary and asks whether any of the Q4 complaints crossed the 30-day MDR reportability threshold for revision surgery due to suspected metal sensitivity; references 21 CFR 803.50 in passing. Asks for confirmation on which TrackWise records already generated MDRs.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Complaint Investigation Record TW-2021-0204
gist: Complaint form for patient implanted with ApexHip cup lot V-2091, stem S-7144, head H-3062 at Nashville Hip & Knee under Dr. Anita Rao. Reported symptoms: groin pain, elevated serum cobalt at 14.2 ug/L (reference range under 1 ug/L), MRI suggestive of pseudotumor. Investigation section states explant scheduled, samples to be sent for wear analysis, and complaint is being evaluated for MDR reportability per procedure QP-220. Disposition field left open pending pathology.

author: Dr. Anita Rao
subject: Revision case - cobalt levels and pseudotumor
gist: Dr. Rao writes directly to Raman describing a patient with a failed ApexHip (lot V-2091) with elevated cobalt/chromium ion levels and imaging consistent with adverse reaction to metal debris, expressing growing concern that this is not an isolated case among her ApexHip patients and asking whether Veridian has aggregate data on the phenomenon across sites. She references the March 2021 NJR report she recently read and asks if Veridian has seen similar registry signals.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Revision case - cobalt levels and pseudotumor
gist: Raman thanks Dr. Rao, confirms the complaint has been logged as TW-2021-0204 and is under investigation, and states company policy is to review each case individually per TrackWise procedure but does not confirm or deny an aggregate trend, deferring registry questions to the post-market surveillance team. Tone is measured and slightly guarded.

author: Greg Novak
subject: NJR 2021 annual report - ApexHip revision rate flag
gist: Novak forwards the key finding from the just-published NJR annual report: ApexHip 5-year revision rate of 7.1% versus 3.2% class average for MoM hips, explicitly ties this to the ongoing complaint trend Raman has been tracking and suggests the two data streams corroborate each other. He recommends the group convene a formal signal review meeting rather than continue ad hoc discussion, foreshadowing the September Registry Signal Review.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: NJR 2021 annual report - ApexHip revision rate flag
gist: Okonkwo agrees a formal review is warranted, asks Mitchell to pull the current MDR count for ApexHip year-to-date and Raman to prepare a complaint trend chart segmented by cup lot for the meeting, targeting a September timeframe pending calendar availability.

subject: Sunshine Act final closeout form - Feld and Rao ApexHip payments

Form includes fields for payment category, amount, date, and certification signature confirming figures reconcile to Concur and royalty accounting systems, to be submitted to CMS by the standard reporting deadline.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Active Life campaign kickoff for ApexHip launch
gist: Carlos introduces the upcoming Active Life marketing campaign ahead of the April 2017 US launch of ApexHip, describing messaging pillars: longevity, low wear, large head diameter for stability, and target patients aged 45-65. He asks Anika to loop in Kessler Reid for brochure concepts and mentions the tagline idea 'designed to last a lifetime of movement.' He notes claim substantiation will need input from Dr. Adeyemi before anything goes external.

author: Anika Shah
subject: RE: Active Life campaign kickoff for ApexHip launch
gist: Anika replies agreeing to bring in Kessler Reid and asks Dr. Adeyemi to review draft claims before print, specifically the phrase about lasting 'a lifetime of movement' and any comparison to ClassicHip wear rates. She flags that legal (Steinberg) will also need a look once copy is drafted.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: Active Life campaign kickoff for ApexHip launch
gist: Adeyemi responds cautiously that the wear-test data supporting 'lifetime of movement' language is based on standard 45-degree inclination ISO 14242 testing only, and he'd prefer softer language like 'engineered for long-term performance' until more clinical data accumulates. He asks whether they've tested at higher inclination angles representative of real patient anatomy.

author: Anika Shah
subject: ApexHip brochure copy - first draft review
gist: Anika sends the agency's first brochure draft for review, describing bullet points including 'largest head diameters in class for exceptional stability' and 'KinetiCoat technology for durable bone ingrowth.' She asks the agency to soften any absolute claims about lifespan pending legal review and to remove a direct revision-rate comparison to competitor hips that was not substantiated.

author: minor character (Kessler Reid) Ted Brannigan
subject: RE: ApexHip brochure copy - first draft review
gist: Ted from Kessler Reid confirms the agency will revise the comparison claim and softens the lifespan language per Anika's notes, but pushes back that 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' is core to the campaign concept and asks whether legal has actually reviewed it yet.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Claim Substantiation File - ApexHip Launch Materials
gist: Internal marketing communications memo documenting the substantiation basis for each major claim in launch brochures and website copy: 'largest head diameter for stability' backed by engineering spec sheet, 'durable bone ingrowth' backed by KinetiCoat porous coating studies from the KBT acquisition, and 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' flagged internally as aspirational marketing language without direct clinical revision-rate data, pending further Adeyemi sign-off. The memo lists claim owners, source documents, and review dates, and notes that the 510(k) K162447 clearance letter should not be cited as efficacy evidence.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: ApexHip launch materials now live - use these!
gist: Marcus announces the Active Life brochures and sell sheets are approved for field use ahead of the April 17 Dallas launch kickoff, and tells reps to lean into the 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' and large-head-diameter stability messaging when talking to surgeons and hospital purchasing. He says these are the only approved talking points and anything else needs Anika's sign-off.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Teams: Southeast launch prep
gist: Jenna and Sarah chat about logistics for the Atlanta launch event, catering, and booth setup; Sarah asks if there's a one-pager she can leave with Dr. Feld's office, and Jenna says the Active Life brochure covers it. No substantive discussion of claims content, purely logistics.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Website copy for apexhip.com - final review before go-live
gist: Carlos circulates the final proposed website copy for the public ApexHip product page, including a claim that ApexHip is 'clinically designed for active adults seeking a hip replacement that moves with their lifestyle for years to come.' He asks for final sign-off before the site goes live alongside the launch, noting time pressure from the marketing calendar.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: Website copy for apexhip.com - final review before go-live
gist: Adeyemi approves the website copy with one edit: removing the specific number '20 years' that had been mentioned in an earlier draft attachment as an expected implant lifespan, since no long-term data supports that figure yet. He says general 'years to come' language is acceptable but any specific year count needs actual clinical follow-up data.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Claim Substantiation Review - Q2 Marketing Materials
gist: Calendar invite for a recurring quarterly meeting to review marketing claim substantiation files for ApexHip and other product lines; agenda line mentions reviewing brochure and website claims. Purely scheduling, no substantive content in the invite body itself.
gray_rationale: The meeting is specifically about reviewing marketing claims but the invite itself has no substantive content, so a strict reviewer might exclude it while an inclusive one includes it as evidence of the claim review process.

author: Sam Ibarra
subject: Comparing revision rates to competitor systems in Texas market
gist: Sam Ibarra, the Texas distributor, asks Marcus if there's an approved slide comparing ApexHip's early revision rate performance favorably against competitor metal-on-metal systems, since a hospital purchasing committee wants comparative data before adding ApexHip to their formulary. He wants something he can hand to the committee.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: RE: Comparing revision rates to competitor systems in Texas market
gist: Marcus forwards the request to Carlos and tells Sam to hold off using any comparative revision numbers until marketing signs off, since they don't have long-term registry data yet given the product only launched in April. He says the safest approach for now is to emphasize design features rather than revision rate comparisons.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: National Sales Meeting 2018 - ApexHip Positioning Deck Notes
gist: Speaker notes for a slide deck presented at the annual national sales meeting, describing ApexHip's positioning against ClassicHip and competitor systems. Notes include talking points that ApexHip has 'lower early wear rates than legacy systems' based on the 45-degree inclination ISO 14242 bench testing, and encourages reps to highlight the KinetiCoat coating's ingrowth advantages. Notes also caution reps not to promise specific longevity numbers to surgeons since clinical follow-up is still short.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Dr. Feld wants updated stability data slide for his talk
gist: Jenna relays that Dr. Feld is preparing a conference talk and wants an updated slide showing ApexHip's large-head-diameter stability advantage over competitor hips, similar to what marketing gave the sales team last year. She asks if Carlos's team can turn around an updated version with current sales figures.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: RE: Dr. Feld wants updated stability data slide for his talk
gist: Marcus asks Carlos to pull together the slide for Feld's talk and reminds everyone that anything going out under Feld's name as a paid consultant needs to go through the standard claims review since it will be seen publicly at the conference.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Teams: brochure reprint question
gist: Anika and Carlos chat about reordering physical brochure copies from the printer since the Atlanta office ran low; brief exchange about print quantities and delivery timing, no discussion of claims content.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Revised brochure claim: 'proven long-term durability'
gist: Carlos proposes adding a new claim to the 2019 brochure refresh: 'proven long-term durability' based on two years of strong sales growth and positive surgeon feedback. Adeyemi is cc'd for review. This is early evidence of the ongoing tension between commercial pressure to strengthen durability claims and the lack of long-term clinical or registry data to support them.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: Revised brochure claim: 'proven long-term durability'
gist: Adeyemi firmly rejects the word 'proven' for the durability claim, noting that sales growth and anecdotal surgeon feedback are not clinical proof, and that they only have about 18 months of post-market data. He suggests 'engineered for durability' instead and references the need to wait for registry data before making stronger claims.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Revised brochure claim: 'proven long-term durability'
gist: Carlos agrees to soften the language to 'engineered for durability' per Adeyemi's feedback and asks Anika to update the Kessler Reid brief accordingly, noting the change should also flow through to the rep talking points deck used in the field.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Out of office - Anika Shah
gist: Automated out-of-office reply from Anika stating she is out until November 26 for a family event, with Carlos Mendes as the point of contact for urgent marketing matters in the interim.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: 2019 ApexHip messaging pillars tracker
gist: Spreadsheet summary listing the current approved marketing messaging pillars for ApexHip (stability via large head diameter, KinetiCoat bone ingrowth, active-lifestyle positioning) alongside which sales collateral and web pages use each claim, last legal/clinical review date, and next review due date. One row notes the 'engineered for durability' claim was cleared by Adeyemi in September 2018 and is due for re-review in 2020. Includes a column tracking which claims reps are authorized to repeat verbally versus only in printed materials.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: Surgeon asking about wear testing angle
gist: Mike Ruiz mentions a Nashville-area surgeon (not Dr. Rao) asked a technical question during a case observation about what inclination angle the wear testing was done at, and Mike didn't have a confident answer. He asks Jenna whether there's an approved response he should be using, since he doesn't want to say something inconsistent with marketing materials.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Surgeon asking about wear testing angle
gist: Jenna forwards the question to Carlos and asks whether there's a standard talking point for surgeons who ask technical questions about wear-testing methodology, noting reps in the field are getting more of these questions lately and need consistent guidance to avoid giving inaccurate answers.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Teams: booth signage for AAOS
gist: Carlos and Anika discuss booth signage dimensions and shipping deadlines for the upcoming AAOS conference; brief logistical chat about the trade show booth vendor and setup crew, no claims discussion.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Q2 2019 Claim Substantiation File Update - ApexHip
gist: Quarterly update to the claim substantiation memo, reaffirming existing approved claims and noting that Tom Halvorsen's engineering team is re-running wear testing at higher inclination angles which could affect future durability messaging; the memo says marketing should not make any new durability claims until that engineering analysis is complete, and flags this as a watch item for the next quarterly review. Also lists routine sign-offs for the brochure reprint and updated sell sheet with no substantive claim changes this quarter.
gray_rationale: The memo references the ongoing engineering wear-test re-analysis which is central to the registry/design-signal storyline, but here it only appears as a caution against new marketing claims, so its primary relevance is to claim substantiation rather than the underlying design signal.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Active Life 2020 refresh - claims list for legal review
gist: Anika sends Carlos and the Kessler Reid account team the updated claims list for the 2020 Active Life refresh, including the tagline 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' and a new claim 'lowest revision rate in its class among large-head MoM systems.' She asks Carlos to confirm the revision-rate claim is still supportable given recent registry data and flags that legal wants substantiation binders before print run approval.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Active Life 2020 refresh - claims list for legal review
gist: Carlos replies that the revision-rate claim should be softened to 'among the lowest' rather than 'lowest' pending final 2019 NJR figures, noting Greg Novak's team is still finalizing the annual pull. He says the lifetime-of-movement tagline is fine to keep since it's aspirational language, not a data claim, and asks Anika to loop in Dr. Adeyemi for clinical sign-off on the softened wording.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: Active Life 2020 refresh - claims list for legal review
gist: Adeyemi approves 'among the lowest revision rates' as clinically defensible language for now but cautions that the 2019 wear-test re-analysis by Halvorsen showing higher wear at steep cup angles should be considered before any broader durability claims are expanded in future materials. This caveat sits at the bottom of his short reply after the sign-off line.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Q2 2020 Sales Kickoff Deck Speaker Notes - ApexHip Positioning
gist: Speaker notes for a slide deck used at the Q2 sales call: 'Messaging Pillar 1 - Built to Last: emphasize KinetiCoat's bone ingrowth and the 5-year track record; avoid absolute superiority claims versus competitor MoM systems.' Notes instruct reps to cite the 96M revenue peak and 14,200 systems sold in 2020 as proof of market confidence, and to redirect any surgeon questions about revision rates to the medical affairs team rather than answering directly.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Southeast reps asking about the lifetime claim
gist: Marcus forwards a question from a Southeast rep who wants to know if he can tell a hospital purchasing committee that ApexHip 'lasts longer than ClassicHip.' Marcus asks Carlos for approved comparison language, noting he doesn't want reps freelancing on durability claims to win a bid.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Southeast reps asking about the lifetime claim
gist: Carlos replies with the approved comparison line: 'ApexHip's KinetiCoat is designed for durable fixation; ClassicHip remains a proven option for lower-demand patients' and says reps should not state or imply a direct revision-rate comparison since the claim substantiation file doesn't support a head-to-head number. He attaches Apex_ClassicHip_talkingpoints_v3.docx.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Southeast Team
gist: Jenna reminds the team about the upcoming AAOS regional meeting booth schedule and asks who can cover the Saturday shift; no product claims discussed, purely logistics about badges and travel reimbursement through Concur.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Website copy refresh - ApexHip landing page
gist: Anika sends draft website copy for the ApexHip landing page including the headline 'A Hip Built for the Long Run' and a bullet claiming '95% patient satisfaction at 5 years' sourced from an internal patient survey rather than registry data. She asks Carlos and Kessler Reid to confirm the satisfaction figure is still current before it goes live, noting the substantiation file needs updating.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Website copy refresh - ApexHip landing page
gist: Carlos confirms the 95% satisfaction figure comes from a 2019 patient survey of 340 respondents and says it's fine to keep as long as the source footnote stays visible on the page. He adds that marketing should hold off on any new revision-rate language on the site until Greg Novak's registry team finishes the 2020 annual pull.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: NJR report just came out - need guidance on claims
gist: Carlos flags that the March 2021 NJR annual report shows ApexHip's 5-year revision rate at 7.1% versus a 3.2% class average, and asks Adeyemi and Anika whether any current marketing materials referencing revision rates need to be pulled or revised immediately. He notes the website satisfaction claim and the Q2 2020 deck both touch on durability messaging.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: NJR report just came out - need guidance on claims
gist: Adeyemi recommends pulling any comparative revision-rate language pending the Registry Signal Review meeting, and says marketing should default to only the KinetiCoat ingrowth mechanism claims, which are separate from clinical outcome data. He cautions this is a sensitive moment and asks that this stay a small distribution.

author: Anika Shah
subject: RE: NJR report just came out - need guidance on claims
gist: Anika instructs Kessler Reid to remove the '95% patient satisfaction at 5 years' bullet from the website and any print materials referencing revision rate comparisons, effective immediately, and to hold future durability claims pending internal review. She says a revised messaging brief will follow after the September registry meeting.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Southeast Team
gist: Marcus asks Jenna about the Q1 quota attainment numbers and whether the Atlanta territory hit target; purely a sales-performance check-in with no product claim content.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Claim Substantiation File Update - ApexHip Marketing Materials
gist: Internal memo documenting the removal of the patient satisfaction claim and revision-rate comparison language from ApexHip web and print materials following the March 2021 NJR report, and listing remaining approved claims: KinetiCoat bone ingrowth mechanism, large head diameter for stability, and the 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' tagline. The memo notes that Dr. Adeyemi and legal reviewed the change and that Kessler Reid confirmed removal from all live assets as of April 2, 2021, with a table of asset IDs and takedown dates.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Updated FAQ for reps - metal ion and revision questions
gist: Carlos circulates an updated rep-facing FAQ document ('ApexHip_RepFAQ_June2021.docx') with approved talking points for questions about metal ions and revision rates, instructing reps to say the company is 'monitoring registry data closely' rather than citing specific revision percentages, and to route detailed clinical questions to medical affairs. He asks Marcus and Jenna to distribute to their teams and confirm training completion.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: FW: Updated FAQ for reps - metal ion and revision questions
gist: Jenna forwards the FAQ to Sarah and Mike with a note asking them to review before their next surgeon meetings and to not go off-script when discussing the NJR data, since legal and marketing worked hard on the exact wording.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Reps Chat
gist: Sarah and Mike chat about a hospital's cafeteria closing early during a site visit and complain about parking near the loading dock; no substantive product content.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Denver surgeon pushing back on revision data - need slide
gist: Marcus relays that Dr. James Whitaker in Denver challenged a rep on ApexHip revision rates during a case observation and asks Carlos to prepare a slide with defensible comparison data for the sales team to use in similar situations, referencing the earlier NJR figures indirectly. Marcus adds this is becoming a recurring objection across territories, not just Denver.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Denver surgeon pushing back on revision data - need slide
gist: Carlos says he cannot create a comparison slide using the NJR data since legal has flagged it as sensitive pending the September registry review, and instead offers to prepare a general 'we monitor all registries closely' response for the objection-handling deck. He asks Adeyemi to weigh in on tone.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Kessler Reid quarterly check-in
gist: Routine calendar invite for a recurring quarterly marketing agency check-in call with Kessler Reid; agenda line just says 'campaign performance review' with no specifics.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Post-Registry Review: messaging guidance going forward
gist: Carlos summarizes outcomes of the recent Registry Signal Review meeting for the marketing and sales leadership, noting the company will continue selling ApexHip with a labeling update and a Dear Doctor letter going to surgeons, and asks that all future marketing claims and rep talking points reflect the updated label language rather than prior durability messaging. Quoted below is an earlier reply from Adeyemi from August reiterating that the revision-rate comparison slide requested by Marcus should still not be created; the new top message says the label update supersedes that guidance and a revised claims document will follow within two weeks.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Revised claims doc post-label-update
gist: Anika sends the revised claims document reflecting the new ApexHip label language, removing the 'lifetime of movement' durability tagline entirely and replacing it with 'engineered for active lifestyles, with ongoing post-market monitoring.' She notes this is a significant tone shift and asks Kessler Reid to update all brochures, the website, and trade show signage by year end.

author: Kessler Reid
subject: RE: Revised claims doc post-label-update
gist: Kessler Reid confirms receipt and provides a timeline for updating the brochure print run, website, and booth signage, estimating six weeks for full rollout given existing print inventory of the old brochure needs to be destroyed. They ask whether reps should be told to stop distributing the old 'Active Life' brochures immediately.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Revised claims doc post-label-update
gist: Carlos confirms reps should stop using the old brochures immediately and asks Marcus and Jenna to collect remaining printed copies from field bags at the next regional meeting, since the durability tagline no longer matches the updated label.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Reps Chat
gist: Sarah mentions she saw a KneeFlex competitor booth at a local conference with aggressive pricing signage and asks if marketing has any KneeFlex comparison sheets; conversation is entirely about KneeFlex, not ApexHip, and includes no durability or revision claims about Apex.
gray_rationale: Mentions competitor pricing signage in passing for KneeFlex only, not substantive enough on ApexHip claims to be responsive, though a reviewer might scan for claim-adjacent content.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Claim substantiation tracker - Q4 2021 update
gist: Spreadsheet summary tracking all active ApexHip marketing claims, their substantiation source, and review status, including rows for the KinetiCoat ingrowth claim (substantiated by design verification testing), the removed durability tagline (marked 'retired 10/2021 per label update'), and the removed patient satisfaction figure (marked 'retired 4/2021'). Anika's cover note asks Carlos to confirm the tracker is accurate before year-end audit.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Reps still asking what to say re: label change
gist: Marcus reports reps are confused about how to explain the new label wording to surgeons who ask directly why the old durability claims were removed, and asks for a short explainer script reps can use in the field that doesn't reference litigation concerns or the recall.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Reps still asking what to say re: label change
gist: Carlos drafts a short field script: 'We periodically update product materials to reflect the latest available clinical and registry information; the underlying device and indications remain unchanged.' He asks Anika to review before distribution and notes reps should avoid discussing specific revision rate figures with surgeons directly.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Active Life refresh - revision-rate claim needs updated source
gist: Anika asks Carlos to confirm which data source backs the claim 'ApexHip patients experience significantly fewer revisions than metal-on-polyethylene alternatives' in the refreshed Active Life brochure, since the old citation is from 2018 and marketing wants to run the ad again for spring. She notes legal previously flagged the wording as needing a footnote. Carlos is asked to check with Greg Novak on the latest revision-rate figures before the brochure goes back to print.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Active Life refresh - revision-rate claim needs updated source
gist: Carlos forwards the request to Greg and says marketing would like to keep the 'fewer revisions' language if the data still supports it, since it's a strong differentiator against ClassicHip and competitor MoM systems. He mentions the brochure print deadline is March 2 and asks for a quick yes/no plus underlying numbers if available.

author: Greg Novak
subject: RE: Active Life refresh - revision-rate claim needs updated source
gist: Greg replies that internal AJRR-derived tracking actually shows ApexHip trending slightly worse than the 2018 figure used in the brochure, though it's not yet statistically robust with current sample size; he recommends softening the claim to something general about 'designed for durability' rather than a comparative revision-rate statistic until the 2021 NJR data comes in. This is the substantive, buried caution in what looks like a routine data-request thread.
gray_rationale: Greg's caution about weakening revision data could be read as an internal quality signal rather than pure claim substantiation, but since it's directly about whether a marketing claim can be supported it is coded responsive.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Active Life brochure print
gist: Quick Teams chat where Anika tells Carlos they went with the softened 'designed for durability and an active lifestyle' language per Greg's note, dropping the specific revision-rate comparison from this print run, and asks Carlos to sign off on final proof before Friday.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Website copy update - 'lifetime of movement' tagline
gist: Carlos sends Kessler Reid the approved website copy block for the ApexHip product page, including the tagline 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' and bullet points about large head diameter, stability for active adults 45-65, and KinetiCoat bone ingrowth technology. He asks the agency to confirm this matches the claim substantiation binder version Anika sent last month and to schedule the page refresh for early May.

author: Kessler Reid Agency
subject: RE: Website copy update - 'lifetime of movement' tagline
gist: Agency contact (Dana Alvarez, account lead) confirms receipt and asks whether the 'active adults 45-65' age framing needs any medical disclaimer language, noting a recent industry article about scrutiny of implant longevity claims. She attaches a revised copy draft for review.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: Claim substantiation review - Q2 sales deck slide 14
gist: Leon reviews a sales deck slide comparing ApexHip's early revision data favorably to a named competitor product and flags that the underlying study cited is a 2-year cohort while the competitor's cited study is 5-year, making the comparison misleading; he asks that the slide either be pulled or the study durations be matched and labeled clearly. This is squarely a claim substantiation review.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Claim substantiation review - Q2 sales deck slide 14
gist: Carlos agrees to pull the comparative slide from the Q2 sales deck used by the field team and says he'll ask Marcus Lee to have reps stop using printed copies still in the field; he thanks Leon for catching it before the regional sales meeting in Atlanta.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Q3 Sales Kickoff - Talking Points Draft
gist: Draft speaker notes for the regional sales kickoff instructing reps to lead with 'active adults deserve an active life' messaging and to reference ApexHip's large head diameter for stability when addressing surgeon concerns about dislocation risk versus competitor implants; includes a slide describing how to frame revision-rate questions from surgeons by pointing to the 'designed for durability' language rather than specific statistics, matching the softened marketing approach from earlier in the year.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Southeast rep booth setup - AAOS regional
gist: Jenna and Marcus discuss logistics for a regional orthopedic conference booth: table skirting color, badge scanner rental, and whether to bring extra brochures. No discussion of clinical claims or messaging content, purely event logistics.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Active Life digital ad copy - final approval needed
gist: Anika sends final approved digital ad copy for a social media campaign featuring a stock photo of a hiker with the tagline 'move without limits' and a bullet claiming ApexHip offers 'exceptional stability for an active life,' asking the agency to launch the campaign the following week and to route any further copy changes through her for claim review first.

author: Sam Ibarra
subject: Pricing sheet for Northgate GPO renewal
gist: Sam Ibarra of Ibarra Surgical writes asking for the updated ApexHip price list for the Northgate/VantageOne GPO renewal negotiation, listing current list price of $9,800 per system and asking about volume discount tiers. Marcus replies with the price sheet attached and no discussion of clinical claims or messaging; purely commercial pricing logistics.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Board deck slide - Apex revision rate vs class average
gist: Carlos circulates a draft Q4 board deck slide comparing ApexHip's 5-year revision rate favorably to a 'class average' figure, asking Leon to confirm the number is still defensible given the March 2021 NJR data isn't out yet but internal registry tracking has been trending unfavorably per Greg Novak's earlier note; he wants to avoid the same substantiation problem flagged on the sales deck slide in June. This slide, intended for the board and investor-facing purposes, directly implicates the claim substantiation issue raised earlier in the year.
gray_rationale: A board-facing revenue/investor deck slide could be seen as financial disclosure rather than marketing claim, but since it repeats a comparative performance claim similar to consumer-facing marketing material it is coded responsive to claim substantiation.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: Board deck slide - Apex revision rate vs class average
gist: Leon responds that he'd rather the slide cite only published external registry data (the 2018 comparison) rather than internal preliminary tracking, and suggests adding a footnote acknowledging registry data lag; he says he does not want to overstate the claim heading into next year given what Greg flagged in February.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Claim Substantiation Review - Q1 2021 Materials
gist: Calendar invite for a recurring quarterly claim substantiation review meeting covering all Active Life materials in market, with agenda line items listing brochure, website, and sales deck claims to be reviewed; no substantive discussion in the invite body itself beyond the agenda topic list.
gray_rationale: Pure scheduling with only an agenda topic line naming the review subject; a strict reviewer might treat this as logistics-only, but the explicit claim-substantiation agenda content leans responsive.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Southeast Q1 numbers
gist: Marcus and Jenna discuss Southeast region Q1 quota targets and a rep incentive trip to Cancun for top performers; purely sales performance and incentive logistics, no product claims discussed.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Kessler Reid - new patient testimonial video script
gist: Anika shares a draft script for a patient testimonial video for the Active Life campaign in which the patient describes returning to hiking and tennis after ApexHip surgery, and says the agency wants the patient to say the implant 'will last the rest of my life,' which Anika flags as a durability claim needing legal and Leon's sign-off before filming since it goes further than the approved 'designed to last' brochure language.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Kessler Reid - new patient testimonial video script
gist: Carlos agrees the 'will last the rest of my life' line is too strong and asks the agency to soften it to something like 'I trust it to keep up with me,' avoiding an absolute durability promise; he asks Leon for a quick thumbs up before responding to the agency.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Reminder: approved messaging only for surgeon conversations
gist: Jenna sends her Southeast reps a reminder to only use approved talking points from the Q3 kickoff deck when discussing ApexHip performance with surgeons, specifically telling reps not to make their own comparative revision-rate claims verbally since marketing and legal control that language; she references the softened durability messaging rather than specific statistics as the safe approach for objection handling.

author: Anika Shah
subject: NJR annual report - impact on Active Life messaging
gist: Anika forwards a summary of the newly published NJR annual report showing ApexHip's 5-year revision rate at 7.1% against a 3.2% class average, and asks urgently whether the Active Life campaign, website copy, and sales talking points need to be pulled or revised given this is now public data that surgeons and patients could find themselves; she says the testimonial video shoot scheduled for April should probably be paused pending guidance.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: NJR annual report - impact on Active Life messaging
gist: Leon says he agrees the video shoot should pause and that all comparative durability and revision claims in current materials need to be re-reviewed before the Registry Signal Review meeting scheduled for later in the year; he says marketing should not publish anything new with revision-rate implications until that internal review concludes.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: NJR annual report - impact on Active Life messaging
gist: Carlos tells the agency to formally pause the testimonial video shoot and put a temporary hold on the 'move without limits' digital ad refresh scheduled for Q2, citing an internal data review in progress; he does not mention the NJR numbers to the agency directly, only that there is a pending internal review affecting messaging.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Sales kickoff swag order
gist: Marcus asks Carlos to approve the order for branded water bottles and tote bags for the upcoming regional sales meeting; purely logistics with no discussion of messaging content or claims.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Interim guidance for reps on revision-rate questions
gist: Anika sends field-facing interim talking points instructing reps that if a surgeon or patient asks about the NJR revision-rate data, they should acknowledge the registry data exists, note the company is reviewing it, and redirect to the surgeon's own clinical judgment rather than disputing or minimizing the numbers; this is explicit objection-handling guidance issued while the internal Registry Signal Review is pending.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: RE: revision-rate talking points
gist: Sarah tells Jenna she's uncomfortable using the new interim script with Dr. Feld's office since his staff has already seen the NJR headline and asks if there's anything more concrete she can say; Jenna says to stick to the approved language for now and escalate specific surgeon pushback to Anika's team.

subject: RE: MDR reportability question re: registry signal

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Minutes - Registry Signal Review Meeting
gist: Detailed minutes of the September 14, 2021 meeting. Novak presented the NJR 7.1% vs 3.2% figure and AJRR data trending the same direction. Adeyemi gave a clinical opinion that the signal is concerning but not yet conclusive of a design defect, recommending closer monitoring rather than immediate withdrawal. Discussion of MDR trending obligations under 21 CFR 803 raised by Okonkwo. Decision recorded: continue selling ApexHip, implement a labeling update emphasizing surgical technique and inclination angle, and draft a Dear Doctor letter for October. Castellano concurred by phone. Action items assigned to Mendes (labeling), Mitchell (Dear Doctor letter draft), Raman (complaint trend monitoring).

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: Follow-up thoughts on the registry data
gist: Adeyemi writes a reflective follow-up after the Sept 14 meeting, expanding on his clinical caution. He notes the 7.1% revision rate is concerning but cites literature suggesting edge-loading at high inclination angles (echoing Halvorsen's 2019 wear-test findings) may be a surgical-technique confound rather than a pure design flaw. He recommends the labeling update proceed quickly and that PMS data be reviewed again in six months. States he is comfortable with the continue-selling decision for now but flags that this could change if AJRR Q1 2022 data worsens.

author: Greg Novak
subject: RE: Follow-up thoughts on the registry data
gist: Novak agrees with Adeyemi's assessment and adds detail: the AJRR late-2021 pull shows a similar directional trend to NJR though with smaller sample size, and he will build a quarterly registry dashboard to track ApexHip revision rates against the class average going forward. He mentions setting a recurring calendar reminder to pull updated NJR and AJRR extracts each quarter and to loop Raman in on complaint correlation.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: ApexHip Labeling Update - Draft Rationale

Proposes adding a caution statement about cup inclination angle above 45 degrees increasing wear rates, referencing internal wear-test data (without naming Halvorsen's 2019 55-degree retest explicitly but alluding to 'internal bench testing'). Ends with a request for Okonkwo's regulatory sign-off before the October Dear Doctor letter goes out.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: ApexHip Labeling Update - Draft Rationale

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi

subject: RE: Dear Doctor letter draft - first pass

author: Devon Mitchell

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: Clinical Assessment Memo - ApexHip Revision Trend
gist: Adeyemi's formal clinical memo prepared for the DHF/regulatory file, reviewing published literature on metal-on-metal hip wear, comparing ApexHip's 7.1% five-year revision rate to registry benchmarks, and discussing the biological plausibility of edge-loading wear at high inclination angles referencing Halvorsen's 2019 55-degree retest. Concludes that continued marketing with enhanced surveillance and a labeling update is clinically defensible for now, but recommends revisiting if revision rates climb further. Recommends physician education on cup positioning. This memo underpins the September decision and is filed in the regulatory record.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Dear Doctor letter - final for FDA notification

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Important Medical Device Information - ApexHip Total Hip System
gist: The final Dear Doctor letter as sent to surgeons, disclosing the NJR-reported 7.1% five-year revision rate versus 3.2% class average, describing the labeling update regarding metal ion monitoring for symptomatic patients, and referencing enhanced post-market surveillance. Recommends surgeons consider serum cobalt/chromium testing for patients with unexplained pain. Signed by Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs, with copy to FDA noted at the bottom.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Dear Doctor letter going out - heads up for reps

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Dear Doctor letter going out - heads up for reps

subject: Feld office calls

subject: MDR filing status for October complaints

subject: Registry decision - financial exposure note

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Q4 numbers vs the letter fallout

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Dear Doctor letter - final version for distribution

Memo notes the letter was reviewed by Adeyemi and Steinberg and states mailing will begin 2021-10-11 via certified mail with tracking logged in Salesforce. States that reps are not to proactively distribute the letter but respond if surgeons ask. Numbered action items for Mitchell to log distribution completion by 2021-11-01.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: Dear Doctor letter - final version for distribution

Mitchell asks Okonkwo how to respond since imaging is not being mandated, only recommended per the label update.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: Ethics hotline report - Quality complaint trending

Tran states HR and Legal will jointly investigate and asks both recipients to preserve all related documents and not discuss the matter with subordinates yet. Tone is measured but serious, referencing Workday case number HR-2021-1142.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Ethics hotline report - Quality complaint trending

She says she will cooperate fully with the investigation but wants to know who filed the report. author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Quarterly Registry Review - Q4 2021 update
gist: Minutes of a follow-up quarterly registry review meeting attended by Novak, Okonkwo, Raman, and Adeyemi. AJRR late-2021 data continues to show elevated ApexHip revision rates consistent with the NJR findings; the group discusses whether the label update and Dear Doctor letter are sufficient or whether further action such as a design change or sales pause should be reconsidered given the new litigation hold entered 2022-02-01 is anticipated. No decision is reached to change course; action item for Novak to prepare updated registry trend charts for the next board pre-read.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: Litigation hold - ApexHip registry and complaint documents
gist: Steinberg issues the formal litigation hold notice covering all ApexHip registry analyses, the September 2021 Registry Signal Review materials, complaint trending reports, and related communications, effective retroactive to 2022-02-01. She instructs recipients not to delete or alter any such documents and to expect a follow-up custodian interview. Banner reads Privileged and Confidential. Brief and directive in tone.

author: Greg Novak
subject: Registry data post-recall - any change in ApexHip revision trend?
gist: Two days after the June 14 recall announcement, Novak asks whether the coating recall of lots V-2200-V-2299 has any bearing on the ongoing registry revision-rate signal, noting the two issues are mechanistically distinct (coating adhesion vs metal-ion wear) but that plaintiffs' counsel and some surgeons may conflate them. He proposes drafting an internal FAQ distinguishing the two issues for use if asked by the board or press.
gray_rationale: Discusses the recall's relationship to the registry signal but the substantive content is about distinguishing the two issues rather than the recall's execution itself.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Registry data post-recall - any change in ApexHip revision trend?
gist: Okonkwo agrees a clarifying FAQ is wise and asks Raman to loop in Steinberg before anything circulates outside Quality/Regulatory. She notes the 7.1% NJR revision figure predates the coating recall by over a year and should not be characterized as recall-related in any external communication.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Teams chat
gist: Halvorsen asks Novak informally whether the Q3 2022 reserve of 18 million booked for Apex claims reflects the registry signal exposure or just the recall claims. Novak says it's blended, mostly recall-driven right now but Legal expects registry/MDL-related claims to dominate reserves going forward once the state court suits materialize. Short, casual exchange, six lines.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Registry Signal Review - Annual Refresh
gist: Calendar invite for an annual refresh meeting revisiting the registry signal decision framework, scheduling only, room booked as Conference Room B (the Reserve room), no agenda content included beyond the meeting title and standard Teams link.
gray_rationale: Title references the Registry Signal Review process by name but contains no substantive content beyond scheduling.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Registry Signal Review - Annual Refresh minutes
gist: Minutes record that the group reviewed updated NJR and AJRR data through mid-2022 showing the revision-rate gap persisting, discussed whether the 2021 decision to continue selling with a label update remains defensible given first state-court suits filed in March 2023 are now anticipated based on plaintiff counsel inquiries, and noted Adeyemi's continued clinical view that individual patient risk-benefit still favors availability for most candidates. Castellano is copied on the summary but did not attend. Action item to prepare a board briefing combining registry trend, reserve status, and litigation posture.

author: Rob Castellano
subject: ApexHip - board question on continued availability
gist: Castellano relays that a board member asked at the last meeting why ApexHip is still being sold given the registry data trend and now-filed state court suits, and requests a concise briefing memo addressing the clinical rationale, current reserve adequacy, and any regulatory exposure ahead of the next board meeting. Brief, direct, CEO tone.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Board briefing memo - ApexHip continued availability
gist: Formal memo addressing Castellano's request: summarizes the March 2021 NJR 7.1% versus 3.2% finding, the September 2021 decision and label update, the June 2022 coating recall as a separate matter, the $18M Q3 2022 reserve now under review for adequacy given the MDL formation expected later in 2023, and Adeyemi's clinical opinion supporting continued availability with enhanced surveillance. Recommends no change in market status at this time but flags that continued adverse registry trends could change that recommendation. Numbered sections, formal tone, cites 21 CFR 803 for MDR obligations.

author: Greg Novak
subject: Updated AJRR pull - revision gap widening
gist: Novak sends the latest AJRR pull showing the ApexHip revision rate gap versus class average has widened further, now approaching 8.4% at extended follow-up, and recommends this be included in the next registry signal review cycle and flagged for the board briefing update. Attachment described as AJRR_pull_Aug2023.xlsx.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: MDL 3102 formation - next steps for regulatory and clinical review
gist: Steinberg informs the group that the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation has consolidated ApexHip cases into MDL 3102 in the Northern District of Indiana, and requests that Okonkwo and Adeyemi reassess whether the registry-based rationale for continued market availability still holds given the volume and consistency of plaintiff allegations mirroring the internal 2021 registry signal findings. Sets up a joint call for the following week including Novak and Raman.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: MDL 3102 formation - next steps for regulatory and clinical review
gist: Okonkwo confirms availability for the call and attaches an updated summary of registry data trends since 2021 for the group's review ahead of the discussion, noting the trend has not reversed and in fact worsened per Novak's August pull. She suggests Adeyemi come prepared with a revised clinical risk-benefit assessment.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Executive review - ApexHip market status reassessment
gist: Minutes of an executive-level meeting following MDL formation attended by Castellano, Steinberg, Park, Okonkwo, Adeyemi, and Novak. The group reviews the worsened registry trend, the escalating reserve exposure, and Adeyemi's revised view that the risk-benefit calculus has shifted given cumulative registry evidence over more than two years. Consensus begins to form that a voluntary market withdrawal should be evaluated seriously, distinct from the earlier 2021 decision to continue with labeling changes. No final decision recorded; Steinberg to prepare withdrawal option analysis including regulatory and litigation implications.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Teams chat
gist: Okonkwo tells Mitchell to begin drafting the FDA notification letter and physician communication plan in anticipation of a market withdrawal decision expected within the next two to three weeks, referencing the ongoing registry data and MDL context without stating the decision is final yet. Mitchell asks whether to reference the September 2021 Dear Doctor letter as background; Okonkwo says yes.

author: Rob Castellano
subject: Decision memo - voluntary market withdrawal of ApexHip
gist: Castellano's final decision memo announcing the board-approved voluntary market withdrawal of ApexHip effective 2024-02-02, citing the sustained NJR and AJRR registry revision-rate signal since March 2021, Adeyemi's updated clinical assessment, and the litigation and regulatory environment following MDL 3102 formation. Directs Okonkwo to finalize FDA notification, Lee to prepare sales force communication, and Park to update reserve estimates. Formal, decisive tone, references the September 2021 Registry Signal Review as the point at which the signal was first formally evaluated.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: FDA notification letter - final draft for withdrawal
gist: Mitchell sends the final draft FDA notification letter for the voluntary market withdrawal, summarizing the registry-based rationale, referencing K162447 clearance history, and stating no design defect determination has been made but that the company is acting out of caution given the cumulative revision-rate data. Asks Okonkwo to confirm before transmission scheduled for the next morning.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: ApexHip market withdrawal - effective today
gist: Lee informs the sales team that ApexHip is being voluntarily withdrawn from the market effective immediately, citing the company's ongoing registry monitoring and out of an abundance of caution, and instructs reps not to place any new orders. He asks Whitfield to schedule calls with key surgeons including Feld and Rao and directs all customer questions to be routed to Regulatory Affairs rather than answered by sales directly.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: ApexHip market withdrawal - effective today
gist: Whitfield replies she'll set up the surgeon calls this week but asks whether the withdrawal is related to the 2022 coating recall or something new, since several surgeons will likely ask; she recalls Dr. Whitaker in Denver being especially vocal previously. No new substantive facts, mostly logistics and a request for a one-page talking points sheet.
gray_rationale: References the 2022 recall by comparison but the actual content is about the 2024 withdrawal messaging logistics.

author: Owen Park
subject: Reserve update - ApexHip withdrawal impact
gist: Park asks Berg to model the financial impact of the market withdrawal on 2024 revenue and to reassess adequacy of the existing 18 million Apex claims reserve in light of the withdrawal and MDL 3102, noting the withdrawal itself may accelerate plaintiff filings. subject: Teams chat

Casual tone, five lines, ends with Novak saying he'll update the registry tracking cadence to quarterly now that new implantations have stopped.

author: Hannah Berg
subject: ApexHip FY2019 Forecast v1

author: Owen Park
subject: RE: ApexHip FY2019 Forecast v1

subject: Apex Q4 2020 Revenue Update
gist: Hannah reports Apex hit peak-year pace, projecting ~14,200 systems and ~$96M revenue for 2020, about 22% of company revenue, driven by strong Southeast and Dallas performance. She notes no reserve adjustments needed this quarter. Tone is celebratory, focused purely on commercial performance.

author: Owen Park
subject: RE: Apex Q4 2020 Revenue Update

subject: Board Session Prep: Apex Financial & Registry Update

subject: RE: Apex Recall Cost Estimate - Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299

author: Rachel Steinberg

subject: Apex Claims Sensitivity Model — Draft
gist: Berg's summary presents three scenarios (base, moderate, high) for potential Apex claim volume and associated reserve needs ranging from $18M to $54M if an MDL forms and claim counts triple; table includes assumptions tied to the recall's 412 implanted units and estimated national exposure from ARMD-related revisions; flagged as sensitive and preliminary.

subject: RE: Q3 2022 Apex Litigation Reserve - Finalized $18M

author: Owen Park
subject: RE: Apex Revenue Impact Model - Q4 2022 Scenarios

author: Owen Park
subject: Audit Committee Minutes - Apex Reserve and Coverage Discussion
gist: Minutes of the audit committee meeting covering: review of the $45M reserve and the proposed increase toward a mediation funding scenario; discussion of the Aegis aggregate-limit coverage dispute status, with Rachel Steinberg noting outside coverage counsel has been retained; a decision to increase the disclosed reserve range in the upcoming 10-Q to $45-70M pending mediation outcomes; and a request that management provide quarterly updates until the MDL resolves. Attendees included Owen Park, Rachel Steinberg, two independent directors, and the audit firm engagement partner.
