gist: A short, purely social Teams chat where Priya Raman asks Lisa Tran about scheduling a team lunch-and-learn on a new TrackWise dashboard feature, with Tran suggesting a date and mentioning she'll book the reserve conference room; there is no personnel or performance content, just logistics for a training lunch.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Dr. Feld mentioned something at dinner last night
gist: Sarah recaps a dinner with Dr. Feld where he casually mentioned seeing three patients with elevated pain and one with a possible pseudotumor after ApexHip, and asked whether Veridian had seen similar reports elsewhere. She notes Feld also joked about his consulting check being late. Sarah asks Jenna whether she should log this formally or just keep an eye on it. Tone is casual but slightly worried.
gray_rationale: The dinner itself is mostly social with a payment reference, but the surgeon's clinical complaint raised during it makes the payment context arguably relevant to influence questions.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Dr. Feld mentioned something at dinner last night
gist: Jenna forwards Sarah's note to Priya Raman, asking if Quality has seen anything similar from the Atlanta cluster, and reminds Sarah that any patient complaint needs to go through TrackWise per procedure, not just conversation. She mentions Feld's speaker honoraria renewal is also coming up this quarter and asks Sarah to check the paperwork status separately.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Dr. Feld mentioned something at dinner last night
gist: Priya confirms Quality has three complaints logged from Dr. Feld's Atlanta practice in TrackWise (TW-2018-0311, TW-2018-0322, TW-2018-0340), all citing elevated pain and one revision surgery discussion, and says she'll open a trending review. She asks Sarah to formally submit any additional details Feld shared as a new complaint intake rather than informal email.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: Wear re-test results review - 55deg data
gist: Calendar invite for a meeting to review Halvorsen's new 55-degree inclination wear-test results showing 4-6x higher wear than the standard 45-degree protocol. Location is Warsaw Hub conference room, agenda line references Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx as pre-read. No substantive discussion in the invite itself beyond meeting logistics.
gray_rationale: The invite is purely scheduling but references the specific wear-test result that is core design-history material, so a reviewer might include it as context.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: 55 degree wear data - concerning
gist: Tom lays out the wear-test findings plainly: at 55 degrees inclination, edge loading produces 4-6x the wear seen at the standard 45-degree ISO 14242 angle used in the original design validation. He recommends proposing a design change (later ECO-2019-118) and flags that this could tie back to the metal-ion complaints Priya's team has been tracking from Atlanta. He asks whether this should also go to Regulatory.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: 55 degree wear data - concerning
gist: Priya loops in Dana Okonkwo, summarizing Tom's concern and noting the timing overlap with the Atlanta TrackWise cluster (TW-2018-0311 etc). She asks Dana whether this rises to a reportable trend under 21 CFR 803 and whether Regulatory needs to be briefed before any design change decision is finalized. She cautions against overreacting until more data is in.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: 55 degree wear data - concerning
gist: Dana responds formally, numbering considerations: 1) the wear data alone is not automatically MDR-reportable but should be documented in the DHF, 2) she wants a formal trending memo from Raman's team, 3) any design change proposal should be run through the ECO process with a risk assessment. She says she will monitor for now rather than escalate to FDA immediately.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: Nashville rep chat
gist: Mike texts Sarah asking if she's heard anything more about the Atlanta complaints, since one of his Nashville surgeons (not Rao) mentioned a revision case too. Casual, worried tone, asks if reps are supposed to say anything to surgeons yet. Sarah says she hasn't heard official guidance and to just log it if it comes up.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: FDA Additional Information request - MDR trending
gist: Dana forwards the FDA's Additional Information request regarding MDR trending for ApexHip and asks Devon to draft a response addressing complaint volume trends over the past 18 months, including the Atlanta cluster complaints. She references the internal wear-test discussion from February as background context that should inform, but not necessarily be disclosed in, the response.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: RE: FDA Additional Information request - MDR trending
gist: Devon attaches a draft response letter to FDA summarizing complaint counts and trend analysis, noting 11 MDR-reportable events year to date compared to 4 in the same period last year, attributing the increase partly to increased surgical volume. He asks Dana to confirm the framing doesn't need to mention the internal 55-degree wear-test data since that's design, not complaint, information.
gray_rationale: The question of whether internal wear-test data should be disclosed to FDA is a judgment call embedded in an otherwise clearly responsive regulatory-correspondence thread.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Active Life campaign refresh - any complaint context needed?
gist: Carlos asks Anika whether the marketing team should be aware of any recent complaint trends before finalizing the next Active Life brochure claims around durability and low wear. He mentions the phrase 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' is under review by Kessler Reid and wants to make sure nothing in the claims could look inconsistent with what Quality is seeing internally.

author: Anika Shah
subject: RE: Active Life campaign refresh - any complaint context needed?
gist: Anika loops in Priya and asks directly whether the current complaint trend data would affect substantiation for the 'lifetime of movement' durability claim. Priya has not yet replied in this message; Anika notes the brochure is scheduled to print in three weeks and asks for a quick answer.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: Active Life campaign refresh - any complaint context needed?
gist: Priya responds that the complaint volume is still within normal limits per her latest trending review but flags that Halvorsen's 55-degree wear finding from February is still under internal evaluation and could eventually affect durability messaging if a design change is made. She recommends holding off on any superlative wear claims until that evaluation closes.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Q3 push
gist: Marcus pushes Jenna on Q3 numbers for the Southeast, asking if she can get two more Feld cases closed before quarter end. Purely sales-quota chat with no mention of complaints or clinical issues, just numbers and encouragement with exclamation points.

author: Priya Raman
subject: Complaint Trending Summary - ApexHip Q3 2019
gist: Formal quality memo summarizing complaint trends for Q3 2019, listing TrackWise IDs for the Atlanta cluster and two new complaints from Nashville and Denver, comparing rates to prior quarters, and referencing the ongoing internal evaluation of the 55-degree wear-test data from Halvorsen's February memo as a possible contributing factor. Recommends continued monitoring and periodic re-review; does not recommend design change yet. Signed by Priya, cc'd to Dana Okonkwo and Tom Halvorsen internally per distribution list at the bottom.

author: Hannah Berg
subject: Apex 2020 forecast draft
gist: Hannah sends Owen the draft 2020 revenue forecast for ApexHip projecting continued growth to roughly 14,000 units, noting no material adjustment for complaint-related risk since volumes remain within historical norms. Purely financial forecasting email with a small table of quarterly unit projections; no discussion of clinical or legal risk beyond that single line.
gray_rationale: The forecast is primarily financial but includes an explicit statement about not adjusting for complaint risk, which touches the registry/decision-to-continue-selling theme.

author: Sarah Kim
gist: Sarah texts Mike about a surgeon dinner logistics question, asking what restaurant Jenna booked for the upcoming Feld advisory dinner in Atlanta and whether he's driving up. Purely logistical, no clinical or payment substance discussed.
gray_rationale: Mentions a Feld dinner but contains no business or payment substance, so a strict reviewer would exclude it even though Feld attendance is referenced.

author: Dr. Marcus Feld
subject: Royalty statement question and a clinical note
gist: Dr. Feld emails asking about a discrepancy in his quarterly royalty statement (he believes he's owed for 40 additional units sold in Q1), and separately mentions in the same email that he's seen two more revision cases in patients implanted with ApexHip cups from 2018, wondering if Veridian is tracking this. Carlos has not yet replied in this message.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: RE: Royalty statement question and a clinical note
gist: Carlos thanks Feld and says Finance will review the royalty discrepancy separately, then loops in Priya Raman on the clinical note about revision cases, asking her to have Quality follow up with Feld's office for formal complaint intake. He keeps the two topics clearly separated in the email body.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: Quality Team Standup Notes - Sept 2020
gist: Routine quality department standup minutes covering staffing updates, a note that a complaint-handling specialist is behind on TrackWise closure timelines, and a brief mention that Priya Raman flagged the ApexHip complaint trend for continued watch given the ongoing internal wear-data evaluation from last year. Most of the minutes cover unrelated administrative items like vacation coverage and a new hire start date.
gray_rationale: There is a mention of a complaint-handling specialist falling behind on timelines, which could be read as touching personnel performance, but it's incidental to the complaint-trending note.

author: Greg Novak
subject: Early look at 2021 NJR data ahead of March report
gist: Greg gives an early heads-up that the upcoming March 2021 NJR annual report is expected to show ApexHip's 5-year revision rate elevated compared to class average, based on preliminary data he's seen. He asks Dana and Leon whether Regulatory and Clinical want to prepare talking points before the report is public, and references the earlier 55-degree wear-test finding as a plausible mechanism.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: Early look at 2021 NJR data ahead of March report
gist: Leon responds with clinical caution, noting that revision rate differences could reflect surgical technique or patient selection rather than device design alone, but agrees the mechanism Halvorsen identified with edge loading at higher inclination is biologically plausible and should be considered. He recommends a joint Clinical-Regulatory-Quality review meeting once the report is finalized.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Southeast team lunch
gist: Jenna asks Marcus if he wants to join the Southeast team's quarterly lunch next week at a restaurant near the Atlanta office, purely social planning with no business content, mentions catering budget and headcount only.

author: Owen Park
subject: NJR report implications - initial financial read
gist: Owen circulates an initial financial read on the March 2021 NJR report showing ApexHip's elevated 5-year revision rate, asking Rachel to assess litigation exposure and Rob to weigh in on whether this warrants an early reserve discussion, well before the formal Q3 2022 reserve process. Owen also asks whether sales guidance for the year needs any disclosure caveat language given Apex represents about 22% of revenue.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: Check-in on team workload before summer review cycle
gist: Lisa checks in with Priya about her Quality team's workload ahead of the summer performance review cycle, noting the increased trending and reporting demands related to ApexHip complaint monitoring may be stretching the complaint-handling specialists thin, and asks if any additional headcount requests should be flagged for Workday budgeting purposes before the FDA inspection expected later that year.
gray_rationale: This is primarily an HR workload/staffing conversation but is tied specifically to individuals' performance capacity regarding ApexHip complaint handling, which a reviewer could treat as personnel-scope material.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Registry Signal Review - moving to 3pm Tuesday
gist: Carlos asks to move the Registry Signal Review meeting from 10am to 3pm on Tuesday due to a conflict with a KneeFlex packaging call. No substantive content about the registry data itself, purely scheduling logistics for the meeting where the NJR and AJRR signals will be discussed.
gray_rationale: Scheduling logistics for a covered meeting with no substantive discussion of the signal itself, though it identifies the meeting topic.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: RE: Registry Signal Review - moving to 3pm Tuesday
gist: Dana confirms 3pm works and adds that Dr. Adeyemi should be included since his clinical memo on ARMD risk will inform whether Veridian continues selling ApexHip or issues a label update. She references the March 2021 NJR report showing 7.1% five-year revision rate versus 3.2% class average as the driver for the meeting.

author: Dr. Marcus Feld
subject: Dinner Thursday + a question
gist: Feld confirms dinner plans for Thursday at a steakhouse in Atlanta, then in the last paragraph mentions he's seen three revisions this year in ApexHip patients with cobalt levels well above normal and asks whether Veridian has data on this trend. Jenna's reply below thanks him for flagging it and says she'll loop in Marcus Lee, treating it lightly.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: FW: Dinner Thursday + a question
gist: Jenna forwards Feld's email to Marcus Lee, flagging his cobalt-level concern and asking how she should respond given his royalty relationship and the upcoming Registry Signal Review meeting. She notes he is scheduled to speak at an upcoming conference and doesn't want him spooked.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Registry Signal Review
gist: Calendar invite for the 3pm Registry Signal Review meeting on Sept 14, 2021, in Warsaw conference room Reserve B, listing attendees and a brief agenda line referencing the NJR revision-rate data and the decision on continued sale versus label update.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Minutes: Registry Signal Review
gist: Formal minutes documenting the decision to continue selling ApexHip with a labeling update rather than a market withdrawal, citing the 7.1% vs 3.2% revision rate gap, Halvorsen's 2019 wear-test findings at 55 degrees inclination, and Adeyemi's clinical assessment that the ARMD risk is manageable with a Dear Doctor letter. Castellano approves the plan; Steinberg notes litigation exposure should be assessed. Reserve discussion is flagged for a follow-up with Owen Park.

author: Devon Mitchell
subject: Dear Doctor letter draft - please review
gist: Devon sends a draft of the Dear Doctor letter to surgeons regarding elevated ApexHip revision rates from the NJR report, describing the labeling update language and referencing the Sept 14 Registry Signal Review decision. Asks Dana to confirm the tone doesn't overstate the recall (coating) versus the metal-ion issue distinction.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Teams - Southeast Sales
gist: Sarah tells Mike a surgeon in Nashville asked what to say about the recall after hearing about it from a patient, and she wasn't sure whether to mention the coating recall was separate from the metal-ion concerns raised at the conference. Mike says he got a similar question and is waiting on official talking points from Marcus Lee.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: Teams - Southeast Sales
gist: Mike mentions the recall is only for the V-2200 through V-2299 cup lots for coating adhesion, not the whole product line, and that he doesn't want to get into the ion/revision rate topic without approved language since Dr. Rao has been asking pointed questions lately.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: Anonymous hotline report - Quality complaint trending
gist: Lisa notifies Rachel and Priya of an anonymous ethics hotline report alleging that ApexHip complaint trends were suppressed or downplayed in TrackWise reporting, and that this may relate to the metal-ion complaint cluster. She asks how to scope an HR investigation and whether it should involve the complaint-handling specialist mentioned in the report.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: RE: Anonymous hotline report - Quality complaint trending
gist: Rachel, marking the email privileged and confidential, says outside counsel should be looped in given potential litigation exposure and asks Lisa to hold off on interviewing the complaint-handling specialist until she confirms scope with Whitfield & Barr. She references the TrackWise complaint volume trend from 2018-2021 as the subject of the investigation.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: HR Investigation Intake Form - Hotline Case 21-114
gist: HR investigation intake form documenting the anonymous hotline complaint about ApexHip trending suppression, listing the complaint-handling specialist under review, scope of interviews planned including Priya Raman and two TrackWise analysts, and a note that the investigation ties to complaint trend data going back to the 2018 Atlanta cluster (TW-2018 series records).

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: Whitfield & Barr engagement - anticipated ApexHip litigation
gist: Rachel notifies the group that Whitfield & Barr has been engaged in anticipation of ApexHip litigation, citing the growing complaint volume, the recall, and the registry data as bases for the expected suits. She flags that a litigation hold will follow shortly and that Owen should begin assessing reserve exposure with Hannah Berg.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: Litigation Hold Notice - ApexHip
gist: Formal litigation hold notice instructing recipients to preserve all documents related to ApexHip design, complaints, registry data, marketing claims, surgeon payments, and financial reserves in anticipation of litigation. Lists categories of documents to preserve, including TrackWise records, wear-test data, and the Registry Signal Review materials.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: Teams - reps asking about lawsuits
gist: Marcus tells Jenna that reps in Denver and Atlanta are fielding questions from surgeons about the first state-court suits being filed against Veridian over ApexHip revisions, and asks what talking points exist. Jenna says she'll check with Carlos on updated FAQ language and mentions Dr. Whitaker in Denver has been especially vocal.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Active Life brochure - revision rate language
gist: Anika asks Carlos whether the brochure claim 'designed to last a lifetime of movement' should be revised given the ongoing registry concerns and the recall, noting Kessler Reid needs an answer before the next print run. Carlos replies that legal wants to keep current claims until the label update work is finalized, deferring the decision.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: ApexHip Recall Announcement - V-2200 to V-2299
gist: Dana announces the voluntary Class II recall of ApexHip cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 (FDA recall number Z-1418-2022), affecting 1,140 units distributed and 412 implanted, due to KinetiCoat adhesion failures traced to plasma-spray parameter drift at the Cork plant. She notes this is separate from the ongoing registry/ion issue but expects overlap in surgeon and media questions, and copies sales leadership to prepare talking points.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: RE: ApexHip Recall Announcement - V-2200 to V-2299
gist: Marcus tells Jenna and Carlos reps need talking points fast since surgeons will be calling about the recall, and asks whether the FAQ should also address the metal-ion litigation to avoid confusing surgeons, given Feld and Rao are already asking questions. Carlos says he'll draft separate FAQs for the two issues to keep them distinct.

author: Owen Park
subject: Q3 2022 Apex Reserve - $18M
gist: Owen circulates the Q3 2022 reserve memo booking $18M for Apex-related claims, referencing the recall costs, anticipated MDL exposure, and Aegis Specialty's notice of circumstance. He asks Hannah to finalize the variance commentary for the board deck and Rachel to confirm the reserve figure aligns with counsel's litigation exposure estimate.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: RE: Anonymous hotline report - Quality complaint trending (closure)
gist: Rachel tells Lisa the HR investigation into the hotline complaint about complaint trend suppression is closing without formal discipline but recommends coaching for the complaint-handling specialist and process changes to trending review cadence, to be documented in the specialist's next performance review. She notes this should be coordinated with Priya Raman's team.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: Teams - Labor Day plans
gist: Jenna and Sarah chat about Labor Day weekend plans, a cookout Sarah is hosting, and whether Jenna will make it to Atlanta before the holiday. No business content about ApexHip or any product topic; purely social scheduling chat.

author: Dr. Anita Rao
subject: Speaker bureau - concerns before Scottsdale advisory board
gist: Dr. Rao emails ahead of the upcoming advisory board meeting saying she wants to discuss the registry revision rate data and the recall before agreeing to continue as a paid speaker, noting her honoraria arrangement (~$60k/yr) shouldn't be seen as compromising her willingness to raise concerns. Marcus and Carlos are cc'd on the thread as it develops toward scheduling logistics for the advisory board dinner.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Website revision-rate comparison slide
gist: placeholder

author: Sarah Kim
subject: Dr. Feld asking about the recall AND revisions he's seeing
gist: Sarah writes that Dr. Feld called after receiving the recall notice on cup lots V-2200-V-2299 and wants to know if it's related to the two revision surgeries he's done recently on Apex patients with elevated cobalt levels. Sarah asks Jenna what she's authorized to say, noting Feld is nervous this could affect his patients beyond the recalled lots. Tone is anxious, asking for guidance fast.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: RE: Dr. Feld asking about the recall AND revisions he's seeing
gist: Jenna forwards Sarah the customer notice template and says to stick strictly to the coating adhesion issue in lots V-2200-V-2299, root cause plasma-spray parameter drift after chamber maintenance at Cork, and not conflate it with the revision cases Feld is describing, which she says are a separate quality tracking matter Priya Raman is handling. She reminds Sarah that Feld is a paid consultant so any statement to him should be careful and consistent with messaging from Carlos Mendes.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: Board pre-read prep call - Apex reserve and registry data
gist: Calendar invite for a prep call to align the board pre-read combining the newly booked $18M claims reserve, the NJR/AJRR revision-rate signal, and the label update decision from the September 2021 Registry Signal Review, ahead of the Q3 2022 board meeting. Agenda line items are listed but no substantive discussion occurs in the invite itself.

author: Owen Park
subject: RE: Board pre-read prep call - Apex reserve and registry data
gist: Owen circulates draft board pre-read language stating Apex-related claims reserve is $18M as of Q3 2022, notified to Aegis Specialty, and links the reserve rationale to the March 2021 NJR report showing 7.1% five-year revision rate versus 3.2% class average and the September 2021 decision to continue selling with a label update. He flags that legal wants the wording softened before it goes to directors and asks Rachel to redline.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: Nashville rep chat
gist: Mike asks Marcus in a Teams chat whether he can offer a surgeon dinner to Dr. Rao this month since she's been asking pointed questions about revision rates lately and he wants her back on side before her advisory board renewal. Marcus says go ahead, log it properly, and to loop Jenna in since it's cross-region. No substantive discussion of revision data occurs in the chat itself, purely scheduling.
gray_rationale: Purely logistical dinner-planning message with a passing mention of Rao's revision-rate questions; a strict reviewer might treat it as pure scheduling and not responsive to the payments RFP.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: HR investigation update - anonymous hotline complaint
gist: Lisa provides an update on the HR investigation into the November 2021 anonymous ethics hotline report alleging complaint trend suppression in the Quality group. Top message asks Priya and Dana to make themselves available for follow-up interviews the week of August 8. Quoted history further down includes an earlier note from Lisa summarizing that the investigation is examining whether TrackWise complaint trending reports were delayed or downplayed ahead of the 2021 FDA inspection, and that this ties into personnel actions being considered for a complaint-handling specialist.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: HR investigation update - anonymous hotline complaint
gist: Priya replies confirming her availability and pushing back mildly, stating that TrackWise trending reports were completed per procedure and any delays were due to staffing gaps, not suppression, referencing TW-2019-0417 as an example of a properly escalated case. She notes she is willing to walk HR through the complaint-handling timeline for the 2018 Atlanta cluster if that helps.

author: Sarah Kim
subject: quick q
gist: Sarah asks Jenna if the reserve conference room is booked for a call with Northgate purchasing next week; Jenna says she'll check the calendar. Entirely scheduling, no substance about Apex, recall, or claims.

author: Elena Ruiz
subject: Notice regarding Aegis Specialty reservation of rights
gist: Outside counsel Elena Ruiz forwards Aegis Specialty's formal notice of circumstance and reservation of rights letter concerning potential ApexHip-related claims, referencing both the coating recall (Z-1418-2022) and anticipated metal-ion litigation. The letter recommends the company continue documenting the $18M reserve basis and preserve records consistent with the litigation hold in place since February 2022, and briefly notes registry data (NJR 7.1%) as part of the loss exposure analysis.

author: Carlos Mendes
subject: Talking points update post-recall for reps facing revision questions
gist: Carlos circulates an updated version of the sales talking points document, now explicitly addressing how reps should respond when surgeons conflate the coating recall with metal-ion revision concerns. He instructs reps to acknowledge the recall scope (lots V-2200-V-2299) but redirect any broader wear or revision-rate questions to the medical affairs team and Dr. Adeyemi's office, and not to discuss the NJR data directly with customers.

author: Dr. James Whitaker
subject: Third revision this quarter - I need answers
gist: Dr. Whitaker, a Denver surgeon not on the consulting roster, writes an angry email describing a third ApexHip revision this quarter in a patient with elevated serum cobalt, asking pointedly whether the company has known about a wear problem beyond the coating recall and demanding data. He references hearing about the NJR report from a colleague and says he expects a direct answer, not marketing language.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: RE: Third revision this quarter - I need answers
gist: Marcus replies diplomatically, saying he is looping in Dr. Adeyemi and Dana Okonkwo to provide a formal response, and that Veridian takes revision reports seriously and tracks them through its complaint system. He avoids confirming or denying knowledge of a broader wear issue and promises a follow-up call, cc'ing Jenna to schedule.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
subject: RE: Third revision this quarter - I need answers
gist: Dr. Adeyemi responds clinically, acknowledging the NJR's 2021 finding of a 7.1% five-year revision rate for ApexHip versus a 3.2% class average, explaining the company's decision in September 2021 to continue marketing with an updated label and Dear Doctor letter rather than withdraw, and offering to discuss explant analysis for Whitaker's patients. This is the first internal-to-external message that directly ties the registry signal to the continued-sale decision in writing to an unpaid outside surgeon.

author: Tom Halvorsen
subject: wear data question from legal
gist: Tom messages Priya on Teams saying Whitfield & Barr's Elena Ruiz asked him informally whether the 2019 55-degree wear-test re-analysis showing 4-6x higher wear was ever shared with FDA or KOLs, and he wants to know what he's allowed to say given the litigation hold. Priya tells him to route everything through Rachel Steinberg and not answer directly.

author: Lisa Tran
subject: HR investigation closure form - Quality complaint-handling specialist
gist: HR form documenting closure of the investigation into a complaint-handling specialist in Priya Raman's group, finding that complaint trending reports for 2019-2021 were completed but sometimes delayed due to a staffing shortfall rather than intentional suppression, and recommending a performance improvement plan (PIP) rather than termination. The form references the anonymous hotline report from November 2021 and notes the finding does not implicate Raman or Okonkwo personally but recommends a process review tied to the 2021 FDA Form 483 observation on complaint trending timeliness.

author: Hannah Berg
subject: Q4 forecast - Apex volume assumptions revised down again
gist: Hannah sends Owen a revised forecast showing Apex unit volume for Q4 2022 trimmed another 8% versus the September forecast, attributing part of the decline to surgeon hesitancy following the recall and rising revision-related complaint volume noted by Priya's team, and part to normal post-recall order pauses at hospitals including Northgate. She flags this alongside the $18M reserve as a factor in year-end guidance discussions.

author: Jenna Whitfield
subject: quota check
gist: Jenna asks Marcus about adjusting Southeast quota targets for Q1 2023 given the softer Apex volume trend; Marcus says finance is already working the numbers with Hannah and to hold off announcing anything to reps yet. No mention of recall or clinical issues, purely a quota/administrative exchange.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: Minutes - Apex quarterly risk review
gist: Minutes of a quarterly cross-functional risk review covering: status of the recall effectiveness checks (lots V-2200-V-2299, response rate updates from field), continuing metal-ion complaint volume trend since the 2018 Atlanta cluster, the $18M reserve status and Aegis correspondence, and a brief discussion of surgeon relations following Dr. Whitaker's complaint and the response drafted by Dr. Adeyemi. Action items assign Dana to draft an updated FDA MDR trending summary and Owen to refresh the reserve estimate for Q1 2023.

author: Sam Ibarra
subject: Texas hospital pushing back on Apex pricing after recall and revisions
gist: Sam Ibarra of Ibarra Surgical writes that a Texas hospital system is demanding pricing concessions on remaining Apex inventory, citing both the coating recall and rumors of higher-than-average revision rates they read about from a plaintiff attorney's website referencing the NJR figures. He asks whether Veridian has an official response he can use in negotiations.

author: Marcus Lee
subject: RE: Texas hospital pushing back on Apex pricing after recall and revisions
gist: Marcus responds that pricing decisions should go through Jenna and that Sam should not speculate on revision-rate claims with the hospital; he attaches the approved customer notice for the recall and says any registry-related questions should be forwarded to medical affairs, not answered by the distributor directly.

author: Rachel Steinberg
subject: First state-court suit filed - coordination needed
gist: Rachel notifies leadership that the first state-court suit alleging ApexHip metal-ion injury has been filed and that Whitfield & Barr will lead the defense; she asks Dana and Priya's team to be ready to produce complaint trending and the 2021 Registry Signal Review materials under the existing litigation hold, and flags that Owen should prepare updated reserve figures reflecting the new filing for the upcoming board update.

author: Bill Kowalski
subject: cork line status
gist: Bill tells Priya the Cork line has resumed normal plasma-spray parameters and quality checks since the June 2022 recall corrective actions, and asks whether effectiveness check reporting to FDA is complete. Priya confirms most hospital responses are in and thanks him; short operational exchange focused on the recall closure status.

author: Anika Shah
subject: Pausing Active Life campaign renewal pending litigation review
gist: Anika tells Carlos that Rachel's office has asked marketing to pause renewal of the Active Life brochure campaign claims ('designed to last a lifetime of movement') pending litigation review, given the newly filed state-court suit and ongoing revision complaint trends, since the claim substantiation file may be scrutinized. She asks if Kessler Reid should be told to hold creative work.
gray_rationale: Focuses on pausing a marketing claims campaign due to litigation risk rather than describing the claims themselves, so a reviewer could see it as more about litigation posture than the marketing claim substance itself.

author: Mike Ruiz
subject: AAOS booth setup
gist: Mike and Sarah chat about logistics for staffing the Veridian booth at the upcoming AAOS conference, including shipping the KneeFlex demo models and confirming badge scanner equipment works. No Apex clinical or legal content at all.

author: Dana Okonkwo
subject: MDL 3102 - preliminary document scope
gist: Okonkwo notifies team that MDL 3102 has been formed in N.D. Ind. consolidating ApexHip metal-ion cases, references the litigation hold from Feb 2022, and asks Raman and Mitchell to compile all TrackWise complaint trending reports and registry signal materials from 2019-2021 for outside counsel review. Mentions Elena Ruiz at Whitfield & Barr is coordinating. Numbered list format typical of Okonkwo.

author: Priya Raman
subject: RE: MDL 3102 - preliminary document scope
gist: Raman replies that she is pulling TrackWise complaint files TW-2019-0417 and related entries plus the September 2021 Registry Signal Review minutes; notes the complaint trending reports show the 2019 uptick that was discussed with Novak. She flags that some early 2019 Atlanta cluster records reference Halvorsen's 55-degree wear memo.

author: Rob Castellano
subject: Board pre-read call - Apex market withdrawal decision
gist: Calendar invite for a leadership call to discuss whether to announce a voluntary market withdrawal of ApexHip ahead of the board meeting; agenda line references reviewing the reserve figure, registry data, and litigation exposure. Simple scheduling invite with a short agenda note in the body.

author: Owen Park
subject: RE: Board pre-read call - Apex market withdrawal decision
gist: Park circulates a pre-read summarizing the $18M Apex reserve booked Q3 2022, updated to $31M given new MDL filings, and projects a revenue hit of roughly $22M annualized if Apex is withdrawn. Adeyemi's earlier clinical note on ARMD risk is quoted below the current message. Castellano's short reply at the bottom says the board needs Adeyemi's clinical rationale in writing before the vote.

author: Dr. Leon Adeyemi
